headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said that Bowers (knee) will practice this week and is gearing up to play Sunday against the Saints, Levi Edwards of the team's official site reports.
story: Bowers missed the Raiders' first two games of the season after undergoing a meniscus trim procedure Sept. 8, but he took a major step forward in his recovery by returning to practice last Friday as a limited participant. The star tight end will aim to get in a full slate of practices during the upcoming week, and if he experiences no setbacks with his left knee in those sessions, he could be cleared to make his 2026 debut Sunday. In Bowers' absence over the previous two weeks, Michael Mayer has stepped in as the Raiders' top tight end and has produced a 9-55-0 line on 11 targets.

headline: Head coach Klint Kubiak described Bowers (knee) as "very close" to returning after Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Bowers has missed the first two games of the season, but the Raiders are off to a 2-0 start despite their star tight end's absence. He could be ready to return from a meniscus trim for Week 3 at New Orleans. Bowers' practice participation level during the week will provide an indication of his potential availability.

headline: Bowers (knee) is inactive for Sunday's game at the Chargers.
story: Bowers underwent a meniscus trim in his left knee on Sept. 8, and while he'll miss the first two games of the campaign as a result, he did practice in a limited capacity Friday, and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Sunday morning that the stud tight end is likely to make his season debut Week 3 in New Orleans. In Bowers' continued absence, though, Michael Mayer will act as the primary TE for the Raiders.

headline: Bowers (knee), who is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Chargers, is expected to sit out Week 2 but appears likely to make his season debut Week 3 in New Orleans, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Bowers underwent a meniscus trim of his left knee Sept. 8 but appears to have bounced back well from the procedure and is progressing as expecting. The tight end was able to clear a major hurdle in the recovery process by returning to practice Friday, albeit as a limited participant. Michael Mayer is expected to operate as the Raiders' top tight end in Bowers' stead for a second straight game Sunday, but Bowers should be on track to play Week 3 so long as he can upgrade to full participation in practice by next Friday.

headline: Bowers (knee) will be listed as doubtful for Sunday's game at the Chargers, and Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Friday that the tight end will be worked out pregame before a final decision is made, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Kubiak added that he's optimistic about Bowers returning for Week 3 against the Saints. For this coming Sunday, it sounds highly unlikely, but the Raiders aren't ready Friday to shut the door on the possibility. They're scheduled for a 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff, and it remains to be seen if they'll actually take a final decision on Bowers down to the wire.

headline: Bowers (knee) was seen during the open portion of Friday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: This marks Bowers' first notable on-field work since undergoing a meniscus trim in his left knee on Tuesday, Sept. 8. It's unclear if he'll do much more than take part in the team stretch and perhaps individual drills, but it's at least a sign of progress in his recovery. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will reveal if Bowers has a chance to play Sunday at the Chargers.

headline: Bowers (knee) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice, Anthony Galaviz of The Fresno Bee reports.
story: Since undergoing a meniscus trim in his left knee on Tuesday, Sept. 8, Bowers hasn't been able to practice in any capacity and sat out a Week 1 win against the Dolphins. He thus has just one more chance to mix into drills Friday before the Raiders potentially make a ruling on his status for Sunday's game at the Chargers. If Bowers ultimately can't go this weekend, Michael Mayer will be the primary beneficiary at tight end for Las Vegas.

headline: Porter (groin) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Porter injured his groin early in the first quarter, and the injury is severe enough that he will be held out for the rest of Sunday's game. Jermod McCoy will continue to operate in an elevated role in the secondary.

headline: Porter (groin) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Porter suffered a groin injury on the opening play of the game and headed for the blue medical tent. He has since been declared questionable to return. If Porter can't get back on the field in Week 8, Jermod McCoy could see more action the rest of the way.

headline: Porter is starting at outside cornerback in place of Hezekiah Masses in Sunday's game against the Bills, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Porter and Eric Stokes will be the starting cornerbacks, with Masses on the bench. Coach Klint Kubiak appears to be shaking up the defense after the team allowed 45 points to the Patriots in its Week 5 loss.

headline: Head coach Klint Kubiak expressed confidence Friday in the play of Porter, who didn't play a single defensive snap during the Raiders' Week 3 win over the Saints, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Porter did not play against the Chargers in Week 2 due to a foot injury, and since then, the Raiders have started rookie fifth-rounder Hezekiah Masses at outside corner opposite Eric Stokes. Kubiak noted that both Porter and Masses are starter-level players, and while Porter was limited to special teams work in Week 3, he could be more involved defensively Sunday against the Chiefs.

headline: Porter (foot) was a full participant in practice Thursday.
story: The cornerback was limited in Wednesday's session. Porter missed the Raiders' Week 2 win over the Chargers with the foot injury, but now that he's logged a full practice, he should be on track to play Sunday at New Orleans. Porter played on 45 defensive snaps in Week 1 and broke up two passes.

headline: Porter (foot) was a limited participant at the Raiders' practice Wednesday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Porter was unavailable for the team's Week 2 win over the Chargers while nursing a foot injury, but he was able to return to practice Wednesday. The cornerback will have two more chances to log a full practice and officially move past the foot issue ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Saints.

headline: Porter (foot) was inactive for Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
story: After injuring his foot in the Raiders' Week 1 win over the Dolphins, Porter didn't practice in any fashion this past week before being ruled out two days in advance of Sunday's contest. In Porter's stead, rookie fifth-round pick Hezekiah Masses stepped into a starting role at cornerback in Week 2.

headline: Porter didn't finish Sunday's 27-13 victory over the Dolphins due to a foot injury.
story: Porter was deemed questionable late in the game and didn't return. He logged two tackles and two defensed passes in the season-opening win. Porter will presumably be examined by the team's training staff before his availability for practice next week is determined.

headline: Powers-Johnson (groin) was a full participant in practice Thursday.
story: Powers-Johnson suffered a groin injury against New Orleans in Week 3 and didn't practice at all last week. The third-year offensive lineman didn't play against Kansas City this past Sunday, but now that he's returned to full practice participation, it seems likely Powers-Johnson will be able to suit up Sunday in New England.

headline: Powers-Johnson (groin) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Powers-Johnson was unable to practice all week due to a groin injury. Bryce Cabeldue will be the lone reserve guard behind starters Caleb Rogers and Spencer Burford in the absence of Powers-Johnson.

headline: Powers-Johnson (groin) is being evaluated to reveal the extent of his injury, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Powers-Johnson was questionable to return to Sunday's win over the Saints and was never able to reenter the contest. More clarity on the severity of the offensive lineman's injury and potential recovery timetable should be gleaned in coming days.

headline: Powers-Johnson (groin) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: Powers-Johnson is being evaluated by medical staff late in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game. Caleb Rogers figures to be the next man up at right guard if Powers-Johnson is unable to return.

headline: The Raiders have no plans on trading Crosby before the Nov. 10 deadline, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: It's a different attitude from this time last year, when Crosby was openly wondering what his future would look like in Las Vegas. It looked like the two sides were parting ways in the offseason after the Raiders traded Crosby to the Ravens in March, only for the transaction to fall through due to a failed physical. For the moment, Crosby is committed to playing with the franchise that drafted him in the fourth round of the 2019 NFL Draft, and he is under contract with the Raiders through the 2027 season.He has 18 tackles (seven solo), including 2.0 sacks, one pass defense, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through the first seven games of the 2026 regular season.

headline: Crosby had two tackles (one solo) and 1.5 sacks in Sunday's 27-13 win over the Dolphins.
story: Crosby didn't do much in the first three quarters of the contest, though it was a different story in the fourth quarter, with the veteran accounting for 1.5 of the Raiders' 5.0 sacks on the day. It was an interesting offseason for Crosby, who was nearly traded to Baltimore. He also underwent surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee. However, Crosby looks to be back at full strength, and he appears more motivated than ever, which isn't good news for opposing offenses.

headline: The Raiders placed Johnson (neck) on injured reserve Saturday.
story: Johnson was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets due to a neck injury. He'll now be required to miss at least four games, and his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Browns on Sunday, Nov. 29. His absence means the Raiders will have one less regular contributor on special teams and not as much depth at the linebacker position.

headline: Johnson (neck) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Johnson was held out of practice all week due to a stinger, which he picked up in Week 7 against the Rams. The 2021 seventh-rounder has contributed mostly on special teams, but his absence means the Raiders may have to turn to the practice squad to replenish their depth at linebacker. Johnson's next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Johnson (neck) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Anthony Galaviz of The Fresno Bee reports.
story: Johnson is dealing with a stinger issue he suffered during the Raiders' Week 7 loss to the Rams. The linebacker will need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice if he wants to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

headline: Johnson (stinger/neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Rams.
story: Johnson suffered a similar injury in Week 5 versus the Patriots, and his status for the rest of Week 7 is now in question. The linebacker is primarily a special-teams asset, so his absence doesn't carry much of an impact on defense versus Los Angeles.

headline: Johnson (stinger/neck) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Johnson exited the second quarter of the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots due to multiple injuries. The linebacker has recovered from his neck and stinger issues enough to be a full participant, meaning he will likely continue to practice throughout Week 6 in anticipation of Sunday's home game against the Bills.

headline: Johnson (stinger/neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Johnson exited the second quarter of Sunday's contest with a neck injury. The rotational edge rusher is confirmed to have suffered a stinger, meaning his return to the game is unlikely.

headline: The Chargers designated Perryman (undisclosed) for return to practice from their injured reserve list Wednesday, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Perryman has spent the entire regular season up to this point on IR with an undisclosed injury, but it now looks like he's nearing a return to game action. His activity at practice during the week will be worth keeping an eye on ahead of Sunday's game versus the Texans.

headline: Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Perryman (undisclosed) is "close" to returning from injured reserve, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Harbaugh added that Perryman isn't quite ready to return to practice, and given that the veteran linebacker's 21-day practice window has yet to open, he's probably not available for Sunday's game against the Rams. Perryman landed on IR on Sept. 1 due to an undisclosed injury that he may have picked up toward the tail end of training camp.

headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Perryman (undisclosed) won't be reinstated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Per Ricardo Sandoval of USA Today, Harbaugh said back on Sept. 1 that he expected Perryman to spend the minimum four games on IR due to his unspecified injury, but the veteran linebacker will now be sidelined for a sixth straight game to begin the campaign. The 33-year-old appeared in 10 games for the Chargers in 2025, logging 47 tackles and three pass breakups.

headline: Dupree (neck) is off the Chargers' injury report ahead of the team's matchup versus the Rams on Sunday.
story: Dupree missed the team's Week 6 loss to the Chiefs due to a neck injury but is now healthy again. The 2015 first-round pick has compiled five tackles (two solo) across five outings this season and should continue to serve as a rotational defender against the Rams.

headline: Dupree (neck) won't play in Sunday's game against Kansas City.
story: Dupree suffered a neck injury in the Week 5 meeting with the Broncos. He practiced in a limited capacity a few times during the week but ended up receiving a questionable tag. Now that Dupree has been ruled out, rookie Akheem Mesidor is in line for more snaps.

headline: Dupree (neck) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Dupree exited the third quarter of Sunday's contest with a neck injury. The linebacker was originally questionable to return, but after extended evaluation, the injury has apparently been deemed severe enough to eliminate Dupree from the rest of the Chargers' divisional showdown with the Broncos.

headline: Dupree (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Dupree exited the third quarter of Sunday's contest with a neck injury. Akheem Mesidor will be the sole rotational option at outside linebacker while Dupree is evaluated.

headline: Henley (shoulder) has returned to Sunday's matchup versus the Rams, David Droegemeier of Locked On Chargers reports.
story: Henley was briefly sidelined with a shoulder injury early in the first half, but he was able to return to the field before the break. The 26-year-old is back in his starting role at inside linebacker against the Rams.

headline: Henley (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Rams, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Henley suffered a shoulder injury early in the second half, and his availability for the rest of the game is now up in the air. In his absence, Troy Dye and Marlowe Wax will stand to see an increase in workload at inside linebacker.

headline: Henley (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Henley was listed as questionable for Sunday's game due to a knee injury. The linebacker was limited in practice all week due to the injury but has recovered enough to suit up for the Chargers' Sunday divisional contest against the Chiefs.

headline: Henley (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Henley was a limited practice participant all week due to a knee injury, which he likely picked up during the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. Troy Dye would likely start alongside Del'Shawn Phillips at inside linebacker if Henley is not cleared to play against Kansas City.

headline: Henley recorded three assisted tackles during Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders.
story: It was just the third time Henley recorded three tackles or less in a regular-season game since the start of the 2025 campaign. The fourth-year pro is up to 11 total tackles, including 0.5 sacks, through two regular-season games and is looking to log a third consecutive 100-tackle campaign.

headline: Henley posted eight tackles (two solo), including 0.5 sacks, during the Chargers' 26-14 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Henley's 67 defensive snaps and eight tackles were both second-most on the Chargers behind Derwin James (75 snaps, 10 tackles). Henley combined with Troy Dye to sack Jacoby Brissett on third down midway through the fourth quarter, forcing the Cardinals to punt on the next play. Henley reached the tackling century mark in both 2024 and 2025, and is well on pace to do so again this year.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) is not expected to practice this week, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Thompson recently suffered a setback with his pair of soft-tissue injuries. Another one of OC Mike McDaniel's swings and misses this offseason, Thompson hasn't played since Week 2 and has just one catch for 13 yards on 22 offensive snaps. The fourth-round rookie has been a non-factor.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Rams, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: Thompson didn't play a snap in Week 6 against the Chiefs despite being active for the contest due to a lingering quadriceps injury. He'll be inactive for Sunday's game, so KeAndre Lambert-Smith, Theo Wease and Derius Davis are all candidates for a bump in offensive snaps. Thompson's next chance to play is Week 9 against the Texans on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
story: It was a second consecutive DNP for Thompson, who has been battling multiple injuries for weeks. The 23-year-old was cleared to play in Week 6 versus the Chiefs after missing the three previous games, though he didn't play. It appears Thompson may not be available for the Week 8 meeting with the Rams, especially if he doesn't practice Friday.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) did not participate at practice Wednesday.
story: Thompson was active in Week 6 during the Chargers' last game before their bye, but he ended up not playing any snaps, presumably due to the quad injury that kept him out for the prior three contests. Now his availability for Week 8 is in doubt, and he'll probably have to return to practice Thursday or Friday to have any chance to play Sunday against the Rams.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) was active but didn't play any snaps Sunday in the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
story: After sitting out the Chargers' previous three games due to the quad issue, Thompson was listed as questionable heading into Sunday's contest after three limited practices. Though he got the green light to suit up, Thompson was presumably available only in an emergency since the Chargers' seven-man inactive list consisted of players who were dealing with more significant injuries. Thompson will have added time to get healthy while the Chargers are on bye Week 7, and if he can fully practice at some point during Week 8, he'll have a good chance at seeing his first game action since Week 2 in the team's Nov. 1 matchup with the Rams.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) is active for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Though Thompson is suiting up for the first time since Week 2, it's unclear how extensively he'll be able to play Sunday. The Chargers have a full list of injured players on their seven-man inactive list, so it's conceivable that much like Ladd McConkey a week ago in the team's loss to the Broncos, Thompson could be available only as an emergency option after he was limited in practices Wednesday through Friday. During the Chargers' first two games of the season, Thompson handled a light role on offense, playing just 22 total snaps while recording one reception for 13 yards on three targets.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Thompson earned the questionable tag for Week 6 after logging three consecutive limited practices, giving the rookie fourth-rounder a chance to return from a three-game absence. If he's cleared to play, then Thompson could operate in an elevated role offensively since Tre' Harris (hamstring) has been ruled out.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Thompson has appeared in just two games for the Chargers this season. He practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday and Thursday, though he has some hurdles to clear before getting the green light to play Sunday versus the Chiefs.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Thompson has returned to limited practice after logging consecutive DNPs in the lead-up to the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. The wide receiver did not participate in the contest, and the weekend of rest appears to have boosted his recovery process. Thompson will likely need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's session to dodge an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Thompson opened Week 5 prep with a limited practice Wednesday, but he followed that up with back-to-back DNPs and will miss a third consecutive game due to a quadriceps injury. Quentin Johnston (chest) has also been ruled out, and with Ladd McConkey (foot) listed as questionable, the Chargers will lean more heavily on Tre' Harris, Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Derius Davis at wide receiver.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) did not participate at the Chargers' practice Thursday.
story: Thompson returned to practice Wednesday for the first time in multiple weeks, logging a limited session. The wide receiver has now taken a step back in his participation, failing to practice Thursday. Thompson expressed some doubt about his availability for Week 5 when he spoke with the media Wednesday, and he appears to be in danger of missing another contest while recovering from a quadriceps injury.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Wednesday's practice was Thompson's first since Week 2 prep, with the rookie fourth-rounder missing the Chargers' last two games due to a quadriceps injury. However, he told reporters after Wednesday's session that he's unsure whether he'll be cleared to return for Sunday's AFC West showdown against the Broncos, per Kris Rhim of ESPN.com. A full practice over the next two days would put Thompson on track to play in Week 6, and his return would be a welcome one for the Chargers, given that top wideout Ladd McConkey is considered week-to-week due to a foot injury.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: Thompson will miss a second consecutive game while working through a quadriceps injury. He was unable to practice during Week 4 prep, so a limited session ahead of Week 5 against the Broncos would indicate that the rookie fourth-rounder is progressing in his recovery. Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Derius Davis will both work in rotational roles behind Ladd McConkey (foot), Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris in Thompson's absence.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Thompson is dealing with a quad injury that already sidelined him for this past Sunday's loss to Buffalo. He's begun Week 4 prep with consecutive DNPs, so his chance of suiting up Sunday versus Seattle is looking quite grim. Prior to getting hurt, Thompson recorded one catch on three targets for 13 yards over his first two games.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) did not practice Wednesday, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Thompson didn't practice last week and missed Sunday's loss against the Bills. With the rookie sidelined last week, Marquez Valdes-Scantling played three offensive snaps as the lightly-used fourth receiver behind Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bills.
story: A quadriceps injury prevented Thompson from practicing during Week 3 prep, and the rookie fourth-rounder will look to progress enough in his recovery to return for Week 4 against the Seahawks on Sunday, Oct. 4. Tre' Harris, Derius Davis and Marquez Valdes-Scantling are all in line for a slight bump in offensive reps in Thompson's absence.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) did not practice Thursday.
story: Thompson has missed each of the first two practices of Week 3 prep while tending to a quadriceps injury, and he'll have one more opportunity to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's road game against the Bills. The rookie fourth-rounder has operated in a depth role through the first two games of the regular season, logging one catch (on three targets) for 13 yards in that span. Derius Davis and recent free-agent signing Marquez Valdes-Scantling would see more involvement in the offense if Thompson is unable to play in Buffalo.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) did not participate at practice Wednesday.
story: Thompson drew three targets in the Chargers' loss versus the Raiders in Week 2, but it appears he may have picked up a quad injury during that contest as well. He'll probably have to return to practice Thursday or Friday to give himself a chance to play in Week 3 at Buffalo.

headline: Thompson caught one of his three targets for 13 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders.
story: Thompson's 13 offensive snaps were a distant fourth to those of the wide receivers ahead of him -- Ladd McConkey logged 31 snaps, Quentin Johnston had 55 and Tre' Harris was in on 56. Thompson's role in the pecking order is likely to remain similar for the foreseeable future.

headline: Thompson (hip) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Thompson practiced fully Friday after limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday. The fourth-round rookie wideout is expected to see some action on special teams as a returner and should slot in as the Chargers' fourth receiver behind Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris.

headline: Thompson (hip) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: Thompson's injury was previously undisclosed, but it's now known that it's a hip injury that threatens to keep him out of Week 1 action. He'll likely have to practice in full Friday to avoid taking an injury designation going into the weekend.

headline: Thompson (undisclosed) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Thompson returned to practice Monday after missing the last two weeks with an undisclosed issue. The wide receiver's designation as limited in Wednesday's first official practice means he may be able to suit up for Sunday's regular-season opener against the Cardinals.

headline: Thompson (undisclosed) was a participant in Monday's practice, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Thompson has returned to practice after missing the last two weeks with an undisclosed issue. It remains to be seen how the rest of Thompson's practice week will unfold, but there is a chance the fourth-round rookie could suit up for Sunday's opener against the Cardinals.

headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Njoku (fibula) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: The transaction opens up a 21-day window wherein Njoku can be evaluated for a return to the 53-man roster. The veteran tight end has been out of action since sustaining the fibula injury Week 2, but if he's able to turn in a full practice at some point over the next three days, he could have a chance at being activated from IR ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans. Once he's back in the fold, Njoku could push Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden for snaps at tight end.

headline: Coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that the Chargers likely will open the 21-day window for Njoku (fibula) this week, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Njoku landed on IR after sustaining a fibula injury in Week 2, but the tight end's looming return to practice should provide a nice boost to a Chargers' TE corps that also includes Oronde Gadsden and Charlie Kolar. In his only full game with the team (Week 1 versus the Cardinals), Njoku recorded a 55 percent snap share en route to catching all five of his targets for 58 yards. If he can approach that level of production once he's back in the lineup, Njoku could resurface as a fantasy option as the season rolls along.

headline: The Chargers placed Njoku (fibula) on injured reserve Wednesday.
story: Njoku will be sidelined for at least the Chargers' next four games after sustaining a fibula injury in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders. Fellow tight end Charlie Kolar (forearm) was able to avoid placement on IR but has already been ruled out for the Chargers' Week 3 contest in Buffalo, leaving Oronde Gadsden as the top option on the depth chart heading into that game.

headline: Head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters Monday that Njoku (fibula) and Charlie Kolar (forearm) will both go on injured reserve, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Both Njoku and Kolar sustained their injuries during Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders, with the former being carted off the field during the second quarter. Both tight ends will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest Njoku can return is Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1. For the time being, second-year pro Oronde Gadsden, who posted a 49-664-3 line on 69 targets across 15 regular-season games last year, is the only healthy tight end on the Chargers' active roster.

headline: Njoku (knee) won't return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Njoku was carted off the field in the second quarter due to a knee injury, which initially left him questionable to reenter this Week 2 contest. Now that he's ruled out, he'll end it with one catch (on three targets) for nine yards. Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will man tight end for the rest of Sunday's outing.

headline: Njoku (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Njoku had to be carted off the field after sustaining a knee injury early in the second quarter, and the veteran tight end is in the locker room undergoing further tests to determine the severity of the injury. Second-year pro Oronde Gadsden should see an uptick in offensive snaps for as long as Njoku is out of the game.

headline: Njoku caught five passes on as many targets for 58 yards during the Chargers' 26-14 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Njoku's 30 snaps on offense were tied with Charlie Kolar for most among Chargers tight ends, yet it was the former that was more heavily involved in the passing game, co-leading the team in catches while finishing second in both targets and yards behind wideout Ladd McConkey (ribs). Four of Njoku's five catches went for 10-plus yards, with three of those receptions resulting in first downs. Njoku's role in the Chargers' passing attack could expand for Week 2 against the Raiders this Sunday if McConkey isn't cleared to play.

headline: Lambert-Smith did not garner a target during Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
story: Lambert-Smith was expected to revert back to a minimal role on offense in Week 8 due to both Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris returning to action, and that is exactly what happened. Lambert-Smith played just two offensive snaps in the contest, and he will continue to have little to no fantasy value as long as the rest of the Chargers' primary pass catchers are healthy.

headline: Lambert-Smith is likely to drop down the wideout pecking order Sunday versus the Rams, as Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports that both Ladd McConkey (concussion) and Tre' Harris (hamstring) are set to return to action.
story: McConkey missed most of Week 6 after suffering a concussion, and Harris sat out that contest altogether. As a result, Lambert-Smith logged an 87 percent offensive snap share, which he turned into his first five catches and 39 yards of the season on nine targets. However, the Chargers' bye week has provided enough time for McConkey and Harris to recover, so Lambert-Smith will probably go back to a very minor role on offense.

headline: Lambert-Smith caught five of nine targets for 32 yards during Sunday's 22-6 loss at Kansas City. He also lost a fumble.
story: Lambert-Smith drew 12 targets total over 10 games during his rookie season in 2025, so his involvement in Week 6 is eyebrow-raising. His 59 offensive snaps actually paced the Chargers' wide receivers Sunday, with Tre' Harris (hamstring) sidelined and Ladd McConkey knocked out of the contest early by a concussion. Offensive Coordinator Mike McDaniel notoriously covets players with breakaway speed, which Lambert-Smith definitely possesses (4.37-second 40-yard dash), so despite his putting the ball on the ground Sunday, McDaniel may continue to try to find ways to get Lambert-Smith involved as the campaign progresses.

headline: Lambert-Smith (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: After being designated for return to practice this week, Lambert-Smith turned in a pair of limited sessions before upgrading to full participation Friday. He ultimately showed enough improvement in his recovery from the hamstring injury for the Chargers to clear him to play for the first time since Week 1. Lambert-Smith's return to action will bolster a receiving corps that will be without Tre' Harris (hamstring) in Week 6.

headline: The Chargers activated Lambert-Smith (hamstring) from injured reserve Saturday, and he is questionable for Sunday's matchup versus Kansas City.
story: Lambert-Smith suffered a hamstring injury in Week 1 against Arizona and has been sidelined since. He was able to post an LP/LP/FP practice log this week, but it's not yet certain that he'll suit up Sunday. Should Lambert-Smith be active, he could see some opportunities on offense given the injuries to fellow wideouts Tre' Harris (hamstring - out) and Brenen Thompson (quadriceps - questionable).

headline: Lambert-Smith (hamstring) is questionable for Sunday's game against Kansas City.
story: Lambert-Smith has a chance to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's AFC West showdown. The second-year wideout was a full participant in Friday's practice, and if he's activated from IR, then he could operate in an elevated role on offense due to the absence of Tre' Harris (hamstring).

headline: Lambert-Smith (hamstring) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: One of six Chargers receivers on the Week 6 injury report, Lambert-Smith is the only one who isn't currently on the 53-man roster. He's been on injured reserve since Week 2 due to a hamstring injury, but after having his 21-day practice window opened Tuesday, Lambert-Smith could have a shot at suiting up this Sunday in Kansas City. He's been a limited participant in both of the first two practices of the week, so he may need to turn in a full session Friday in order for the Chargers to feel comfortable activating him.

headline: The Chargers designated Lambert-Smith (hamstring) for return from injured reserve Tuesday.
story: The transaction opens up a 21-day window for Lambert-Smith to practice before the Chargers would need to add him to the 53-man roster. If he's able to turn in multiple full practices, Smith-Lambert would stand a decent chance of being activated from IR ahead of Week 6, given the banged-up state of the Chargers receiving corps. Ladd McConkey (foot), Quentin Johnston (chest) and Brenen Thompson (quadriceps) all sat out this past Sunday's loss to the Broncos, while Tre' Harris (hamstring) exited the game early.

headline: The Chargers placed Lambert-Smith (hamstring) on injured reserve Tuesday.
story: Lambert-Smith suffered a significant hamstring injury during the Chargers' Week 1 loss against the Cardinals, warranting a stint on the IR. As such, the second-year pro will be required to miss at least the next four games and is eligible to return for Week 6 against the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 18, though he may need more time to recover. Gary Jennings was signed to the Chargers' 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

headline: Lambert-Smith (hamstring) will miss some time after exiting Sunday's game against the Cardinals early, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Lambert-Smith exited the second half of Sunday's contest with a significant hamstring injury. The wide receiver will likely miss multiple weeks due to the issue. The Chargers will likely need to make some practice-squad elevations at wide receiver with Lambert-Smith out and Derius Davis (undisclosed) also dealing with an injury. No. 1 wide receiver Ladd McConkey (ribs) is also uncertain for Sunday's Week 2 game against the Raiders, leaving the team even thinner at the position.

headline: Lambert-Smith (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Lambert-Smith exited the second half of Sunday's game. If the hamstring issue is anything other than a minor hit the wide receiver will likely be required to miss time as he manages the issue. Derius Davis may see an increased role in the Chargers' passing offense in Lambert-Smith's absence.

headline: Shelley (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: Shelley will miss another contest Sunday, so his next opportunity to get back on the field will come in Week 9 against the Texans. With Donte Jackson (hamstring) ruled out, Tarheeb Still could be more involved.

headline: Shelley (hamstring) won't suit up for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Shelly didn't play in Week 5 against the Broncos. He was listed as doubtful heading into the meeting with Kansas City but will now miss his second consecutive contest. With Donte Jackson (hamstring) also sidelined, Deane Leonard is the favorite to start opposite Cam Hart at corner.

headline: Shelley (hamstring) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: It looks like Shelley will miss a second consecutive game due to a hamstring injury, which he has worked through for most of the regular season. With Donte Jackson (hamstring) already ruled out, Deane Leonard figures to start opposite Cam Hart at outside cornerback, assuming Shelley is also inactive.

headline: Shelley (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game versus the Broncos, Eric Smith of the team's official site reports.
story: Shelley has been dealing with the hamstring injury for at least a few weeks. After suiting up in the Chargers' first four games of the 2026 campaign, he will finally sit out in Week 5 against Denver.

headline: Shelley (hamstring) is active Week 3 against the Bills.
story: Shelley was at risk of missing his first game of the season after sitting out practice Thursday, but he returned on a limited basis Friday and ended up getting cleared to play. The undrafted free agent has primarily served on special teams to start his career, and he did pick up his first two career tackles in Week 2 against the Raiders. He'll be slotted for a similar role this week in Buffalo.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: Jackson will miss his third consecutive game Sunday, meaning his next opportunity to play will come in Week 9 versus the Texans. With Rodney Shelley (ankle) also sidelined, Tarheeb Still is projected to be more involved.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Rams, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: A hamstring injury prevented Jackson from playing in the Chargers' two games prior to the Week 7 bye. He was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 8 prep, but if he cannot play, then Rodney Shelley (hamstring) and Tarheeb Still would be candidates to start opposite Cam Hart at outside cornerback.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) was limited in Thursday's practice.
story: Jackson suffered a hamstring strain in the Week 4 meeting with Seattle. As a result, he didn't play in Week 5 versus Denver and Week 6 against Kansas City while also missing practice during that span. With the Chargers coming off a bye, it appears Jackson is trending in a favorable direction regarding his availability for Sunday's game against the Rams, though he likely has some more boxes to check before getting the green light.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Jackson will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a hamstring injury he sustained in Week 4 against the Seahawks. He hasn't been cleared to return to practice since sustaining the injury, but with the Chargers on a bye for Week 7, Jackson will have additional time to rest before Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1. With Rodney Shelley (hamstring) listed as doubtful, Deane Leonard will likely start at outside cornerback in Jackson's absence.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
story: Jackson didn't play in Sunday's loss to the Broncos and missed his second consecutive practice Thursday. Therefore, it doesn't appear he's moving in the right direction with respect to suiting up in Week 6 versus the Chiefs, although Friday's practice should offer further insight on his status.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Jackson was held out of practice all week due to a hamstring injury, which he picked up during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks. His next chance to play is Week 6 against the Chiefs, but in his absence, Deane Leonard and Rodney Shelley are the top candidates to start at outside cornerback opposite Cam Hart.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Jackson was in concussion protocol and listed as questionable ahead of the Week 4 meeting with Seattle. While he managed to get on the field, he exited the contest due to a hamstring issue and didn't return. It's possible Jackson didn't practice Wednesday as a precaution, so he'll have a few more chances to get out there. For now, the 30-year-old should at least be considered questionable for the Week 5 matchup with Denver.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Seattle.
story: Jackson was listed as questionable heading into this contest due to a concussion. While he was cleared to suit up, a hamstring injury could keep him off the field for the remainder of Sunday's game.

headline: Jackson (concussion) is available for Sunday's game against Seattle.
story: Jackson was in the league's concussion protocol. However, after practicing in full Friday, he will suit up for the Week 4 meeting with the Seahawks.

headline: Jackson (concussion) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: Jackson entered the league's concussion protocol during the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills. He progressively increased his practice participation this past week, culminating in a full session Friday, but Jackson will need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to be cleared to play against Seattle.

headline: Jackson (concussion) was a limited participant at the Chargers' practice Thursday.
story: Jackson suffered a concussion in the team's 24-16 loss to the Bills in Week 3, and he was considered a non-participant at Wednesday's practice. His ability to return to practice Thursday is a step in the right direction, but he still has to clear concussion protocol before he'd be eligible to play Sunday versus Seattle.

headline: Jackson (concussion) won't return to Sunday's game versus the Bills.
story: Jackson suffered a head injury and exited the game for an evaluation. Now that a concussion is confirmed, it could mean an extended absence is on the horizon. With Jackson done for the remainder of Week 3, Cam Hart and Tarheeb Still are candidates to see more action.

headline: Jackson is being evaluated for a head injury and is questionable to return.
story: Jackson has been taken to the locker room to be evaluated by medical staff after initially being looked at in the blue medical tent. Rodney Shelley is in line for more work on defense for as long as Jackson is out of the game.

headline: Leonard (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Rams, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: Leonard is in the league's concussion protocol, though it's not clear when he sustained the injury given that the Chargers were on a bye for Week 7. His absence means the Chargers will have less depth both on special teams and in the secondary. His next chance to play is Week 9 against Houston on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Leonard (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: It is unclear when Leonard sustained his concussion, as the Chargers were on bye in Week 7. The depth cornerback has enterted the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not be able to suit up for full-contact activities until he is cleared by an independent neurologist.

headline: Leonard (abdomen) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Leonard missed the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders with an abdominal issue after practicing in limited fashion during the week. The upgrade in practice participation means Leonard has likely overcome the issue and should be healthy enough to suit up for Sunday's game against the Bills.

headline: Leonard (abdomen) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Leonard was ruled out ahead of Week 1 due to his abdominal injury and was unable to recover enough to participate in Week 2. The cornerback practiced in a limited capacity throughout the week but ultimately fell short of suiting up for Sunday's contest.

headline: Leonard (abdomen) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus Las Vegas.
story: Leonard sat out Week 1 with an abdominal injury, but he was able to return to practice in a limited capacity during the week, at least giving him a chance to suit up in Week 2. With that said, if he is sidelined again Sunday, it could mean a small increase in work for undrafted rookie Rodney Shelley.

headline: Leonard has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals due to an abdominal injury.
story: Leonard was unable to practice all week while recovering from an abdominal injury, and his next chance to make his 2026 regular-season debut will be Week 2 against the Raiders on Sunday, Sept. 20. Rodney Shelley will be the primary depth option at corner behind Cam Hart, Donte Jackson and Tarheeb Still, with Nikko Reed and Kaiir Elam being candidates to be elevated from the practice squad for Week 1.

headline: Awosika (lower leg) has been ruled out for Sunday's tilt against the Rams, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: Awosika suffered an injury to his fibula in Week 2 and hasn't been able to suit up since. He remained unable to practice during Week 8 prep, so it's not clear when he'll be able to return to game action. Rookie Logan Taylor may make a third straight start Sunday in Awosika's stead.

headline: Awosika (lower leg) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Awosika continues to recover from a fibula injury he sustained in Week 2 against the Raiders. His next chance to play is Week 6 against the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 18, though he has yet to practice since picking up his injury.

headline: Awosika (leg) did not participate at the Chargers' practice Thursday.
story: Awosika has missed each of the team's first two practices of the week as he continues to recover from a fibula injury that he suffered Week 2. The 27-year-old appears unlikely to return to action Sunday versus the Broncos. With Trevor Penning (concussion) also on track to be unavailable, Logan Taylor may be the next man up at left guard for Los Angeles.

headline: Awosika (leg) is inactive for Sunday's game against Seattle.
story: Awosika injured his fibula in the Week 2 loss to the Raiders. Considering he was expected to miss time, his absence Sunday isn't surprising by any means. With Awosika off the field, Trevor Penning is in line to see more action.

headline: Awosika (leg) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Bills.
story: Awosika injured his fibula during the 26-14 loss to the Raiders in Week 2. He's expected to miss time, so Sunday's absence may not be a one-off situation. While Awosika is sidelined, Trevor Penning should take on more work.

headline: Awosika is expected to miss time after injuring his fibula during Sunday's game versus the Raiders, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Awosika hasn't been placed on IR as of Monday, but it sounds likely he'll have to miss at least one game with the injury he picked up in Week 2. Trevor Penning currently projects to step in at guard until Awosika is available again.

headline: Awosika (leg) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Awosika injured his leg in the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest. The starting left guard's exit makes the Chargers even thinner on the offensive line after already losing center Tyler Biadasz (knee) for the season. Travis Burke or Trevor Penning will likely finish the game in Awosika's stead.

headline: Kolar caught one of four targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
story: The tight end's four targets tied for third on the team, as he ran 17 routes on Justin Herbert's 37 dropbacks against Los Angeles. More of a blocker than receiver, Kolar has been forced to catch more passes out of necessity at times this season. He has 10 grabs for 98 yards on 17 targets. The catches and targets are both career highs in his fifth season.

headline: Kolar caught three of six targets for 20 yards during the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
story: Kolar finished fifth on the Chargers in receiving yards, but he was also second on the team in both catches and targets behind KeAndre Lambert-Smith (five catches on nine targets for 32 yards). Kolar has a 6-57-0 receiving line in his two outings since returning from a two-game absence due to a fractured forearm, but he's stuck in an offense that is one of the worst units in the league this season. The Chargers will look to regroup during the Week 7 bye before facing the Rams in Week 8 on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Kolar reeled in three of four targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 23-17 loss versus the Broncos. He also lost a fumble.
story: Kolar was fighting for extra yardage after making a 19-yard grab for a first down in the first quarter when safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) jarred the ball loose, creating a turnover to set up a Denver touchdown. Kolar managed two more catches for 18 yards the rest of the way, which was enough to make him the Chargers' most productive pass catcher in a game where quarterback Justin Herbert only threw for 121 yards. Kolar projects to start as a blocking-first tight end again in a Week 6 tilt against the Chiefs.

headline: Kolar (forearm) is active for Sunday's game against Denver, Eric Smith of the team's official site reports.
story: Kolar missed the last two games but will return despite practicing in a limited capacity during the week. With Kolar active in Week 5, Oronde Gadsden is expected to slide back to the No. 2 spot on the tight-end depth chart.

headline: Kolar (forearm) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Kolar was limited in practice all week due to a fractured forearm, but he's progressed enough in his recovery to draw the questionable tag after missing the Chargers' prior two games. Oronde Gadsden would continue to serve as the Chargers' top tight end if Kolar is unable to return.

headline: Kolar (forearm) remained limited in Thursday's practice.
story: Kolar broke his forearm in Week 2 against the Raiders and has missed the last two games. The block-first tight end's return will be welcomed by Los Angeles once he's cleared. The Chargers offensive line has been a nightmare, and both starting tackles Rashawn Slater (ankle) and Joe Alt (neck) are again dealing with injuries.

headline: Kolar (forearm) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Kolar has missed the Chargers' last two games while recovering from a fractured left forearm that he sustained in Week 2 against the Seahawks. He's progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice Wednesday, and his participation over the next two days will provide clarity on his chances of playing against the Broncos on Sunday. If Kolar is cleared to return, then he would likely split tight end duties with Oronde Gadsden since David Njoku (knee) is on injured reserve.

headline: Kolar (forearm) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: Kolar fractured his forearm during the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders. He'll miss a second consecutive game due to his injury, but the positive news for the fifth-year tight end is that he ended Week 4 prep with a limited practice Friday. Head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters after Friday's session that Kolar is "doing everything and anything possible" to return to the field, and he could get back as soon as Week 5 against the Broncos on Sunday, Oct. 11. For now, Oronde Gadsden will serve as the Chargers' TE1, with Hayden Rucci also in the mix for offensive snaps.

headline: Kolar (forearm) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Kolar hasn't practiced in any fashion since fracturing his left forearm in a Sept. 20 loss to the Raiders and undergoing surgery two days later. The Chargers have avoided placing Kolar on injured reserve with the expectation that he'll return to action within four games, but he'll almost certainly miss a second straight contest this Sunday in Seattle.

headline: Kolar (forearm) is not practicing Wednesday, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kolar remains unlikely to play Sunday against the Seahawks, as he continues his recovery from a broken forearm, which he suffered in Week 2. Oronde Gadsden, Hayden Rucci and Patrick Herbert handled tight-end duties against the Bills last Sunday.

headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Kolar (forearm) won't play Sunday in Buffalo but is expected to avoid placement on injured reserve, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: After undergoing surgery on his fractured left forearm Monday, Kolar had been expected to head to injured reserve and return after missing the minimum four games. However, Harbaugh noted that Kolar ended up receiving a more favorable prognosis than expected once surgery was completed, and the Chargers are now optimistic that the 27-year-old can return to action prior to their Week 7 bye. Kolar will still need to miss at least one game, and with David Njoku (fibula) still ticketed for IR, Oronde Gadsden appears likely to operate as Los Angeles' clear No. 1 tight end for Week 3.

headline: Kolar plans to undergo surgery to repair a broken forearm and is hoping to return from injured reserve when first eligible for the Chargers' Week 8 game against the Rams, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: After signing a three-year, $24.3 million deal with the Chargers in March, Kolar had opened the season as the team's top blocking tight end, a key role in Mike McDaniel's offense, while contributing three receptions for 21 yards on three targets. He exited in the second half of Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders due to the forearm fracture. With Kolar and David Njoku (fibula) both expected to be placed on IR within the next few days, Oronde Gadsden is likely to see a major uptick in snaps as the new No. 1 tight end on the depth chart, although fullback Alec Ingold could also see more work as well.

headline: Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Kolar will go on injured reserve due to a forearm injury he sustained during Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kolar was spotted with his left arm in a sling following Sunday's loss, and the injury is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on IR. That means he will be forced to miss at least the next four games and is eligible to return for Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1. David Njoku (knee) is also set to go on IR, leaving Oronde Gadsden as the only healthy tight end on the Chargers' 53-man roster for the time being.

headline: Kolar (forearm) was spotted with his left arm in a sling following Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kolar recorded three catches for 21 yards on three targets over 40 snaps on offense before a forearm injury forced him out of the contest in the second half. He was one of two Chargers tight ends to leave the game due to injury, as David Njoku (knee) also made an early departure. Head coach Jim Harbaugh declined to provide updates on Kolar and Njoku after the game, so until the team releases its first Week 3 injury report Wednesday, the statuses of both players will be muddled heading into next Sunday's matchup with the Bills.

headline: Kolar (forearm) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Kolar went to the locker room during the second half of Sunday's game after sustaining a forearm injury, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return. With David Njoku (knee) ruled out for the rest of the game, Oronde Gadsden is the only healthy tight end left on the Chargers' game day roster.

headline: Kolar played 43 snaps (30 on offense, 13 on special teams) without showing up in the box score otherwise during the Chargers' 26-14 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Kolar and David Njoku tied for the most offensive snaps among Chargers tight ends Sunday with Oronde Gadsden (10 snaps) a distant third. Kolar did not see a target from Justin Herbert during Sunday's loss, though that's not entirely surprising considering he posted a 10-142-2 line (on 15 targets) across 17 regular-season games with the Ravens last year. Gadsden and Njoku figure to operate as the Chargers' pass-catching tight ends this season, with Kolar more heavily involved as a blocker and in goal-line packages as an occasional red-zone threat.

headline: Harris caught all three of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
story: After missing Week 6 with a hamstring injury, Harris was healthy coming out of the Week 7 bye but played pretty clearly behind both Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston against the Rams. Harris ran just 20 routes to McConkey's 34 and Johnston's 30. Harris would see a big boost if Johnston gets traded ahead of next week's deadline.

headline: Harris (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: Harris, Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston have all missed time this season, but they're healthy after a Week 7 bye. Prior to the team's onslaught of injuries, Harris actually saw more targets (21) than Johnston (19) over the first four weeks of the season.

headline: Harris (hamstring) remained limited in Thursday's practice.
story: Harris suffered his hamstring injury in Week 5 against Denver and missed Week 6 ahead of last week's bye. With back-to-back limited practices to open Week 8 prep, Harris has a decent chance of suiting up Sunday against the Rams. In a broken Chargers offense, it's difficult to get excited about anyone on the team for fantasy.

headline: Harris (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Wednesday was Harris' first practice since he sustained a hamstring injury during the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. He was unable to play in Week 6 against the Chiefs, but the second-year wide receiver had additional time to rest courtesy of the Chargers' Week 7 bye. It's possible he misses only one game, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Rams.

headline: Harris (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Harris didn't practice this week, after making an early exit from the Week 5 loss to Denver. With Ladd McConkey (foot) and Quentin Johnston (chest) now returning from injuries, the team's WR room is in better shape than a week ago even without Harris.

headline: Harris (hamstring) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
story: The Chargers have held Harris out of their first two practices of the week, a development that comes as little surprise after head coach Jim Harbaugh described the wideout as "more week-to-week" than day-to-day coming out of this past Sunday's loss to the Broncos, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com. Unless Harris is able to make a surprise return to practice Friday, he'll likely miss his first game of the season this Sunday in Kansas City.

headline: Harris (hamstring) was listed as a non-participant on Wednesday's injury report.
story: Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Harris is week-to-week with the injury he sustained in Sunday's loss to the Broncos, so it comes as little surprise that he did not see any action Wednesday.

headline: Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Harris is "week-to-week" due to a hamstring injury that he sustained during Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Harris entered Sunday as the Chargers' WR1 due to the absence of Quentin Johnston (chest) while Ladd McConkey (foot) was available only as an emergency option, per Insdorf. Harris caught two of four passes for 16 yards before sustaining a hamstring injury, which was severe enough for him not to return. Given Harbaugh's update, coupled with the Chargers' bye scheduled for Week 7, it seems likely that Harris will be held out for Week 6 against the Chiefs, with an eye toward being available for Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1. Given the Chargers' injuries to the wide receiver position, the team will need to lean more heavily on Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Theo Wease, Derius Davis and tight ends Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden in the passing game.

headline: Harris (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Broncos.
story: Harris is dealing with an apparent hamstring injury, and his availability for the stretch run of Sunday's matchup is now up in the air. In his absence, Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Derius Davis will likely slot into more prominent roles on offense.

headline: Harris' workload should be larger against the Broncos on Sunday, as Quentin Johnston (chest) has been ruled out, and Ladd McConkey (foot, questionable) may not play, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Rookie fourth-rounder Brenen Thompson (quadriceps) also has been ruled out alongside Johnston. McConkey faces an uphill battle to play Sunday after sitting out of practice all week, and he may operate under a snap count if he's given the green light to suit up. That puts Harris -- who has seen five targets or more in three of four games this season -- in position to work in an elevated role against a Broncos defense that will be without both starting outside cornerbacks Riley Moss (ribs) and Patrick Surtain (ankle).

headline: Harris caught three of five targets for 60 yards during Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seahawks.
story: Harris led the team in receiving yards for the second straight week, recording at least 53 receiving yards for the third contest in a row. Ladd McConkey (foot) aggravated his pre-existing foot injury in the contest, and he is considered week-to-week for the time being. If McConkey is unavailable in Week 5 versus the Broncos, Harris may have a chance to operate as the team's primary pass catcher.

headline: Harris caught six of seven targets for 76 yards during Sunday's 24-16 loss to Buffalo.
story: Harris led the team in targets, receptions and receiving yards in the loss, all of which represented new career highs for the second-year pro. The wide receiver has now reeled in 10 of 16 targets for 149 yards over three games to open the regular season, and he appears to be on track to be a pivotal member of the team's passing attack in 2026.

headline: Harris caught one of three targets for 53 yards during Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders.
story: Harris was the Chargers' only starting wide receiver in the contest with Ladd McConkey dealing with a ribs injury. Harris played 56 of the team's 68 offensive snaps, which was more than the next closest wide receivers Quentin Johnston (55) and McConkey (31). The 24-year-old wasn't able to rack up receptions, but he did make a major splash with his one snag, connecting with Justin Herbert for a 53-yard catch and run in the third quarter. Harris now has gathered in four of nine targets for 73 yards over the team's first two games of the season.

headline: Harris caught three of six targets for 20 yards in Sunday's loss to Arizona.
story: Harris tied for the second-most targets on his team, but he couldn't do much with those looks. Fellow wideout Quentin Johnston didn't do any better, catching just two of his six targets for 17 yards, yet both wideouts might be asked to step up if Ladd McConkey (ribs) isn't able to play this coming Sunday versus Las Vegas. Harris also logged nine special-teams snaps Sunday, but he wasn't a major contributor in that regard last season.

headline: Harris (undisclosed) is not listed on the Week 1 injury report Wednesday.
story: Harris dealt with an unspecified injury last month but is fine for Sunday's season opener against the Cardinals. He's expected to fill the WR3 role behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnson this season, but the Chargers also figure to use plenty of TE-heavy sets with Charlie Kolar, Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku.

headline: Mitchell rushed four times for six yards and caught all three of his targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
story: Handpicked by first-year OC Mike McDaniel as a free-agent signing in the offseason, Mitchell has been a total non-factor for much of the first half of the season. With a career 5.7 yards per carry average, Mitchell is averaging just 3.7 yards per rush this season. Involved in a three-way backfield committee with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal, Mitchell is waiver-wire fodder in normal-sized 12-team fantasy leagues.

headline: Mitchell turned two carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned four kickoffs for 87 yards during Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Week 6 was the lowest usage Mitchell has seen this season, and his 17 snaps on offense were third most among Chargers running backs behind Omarion Hampton (34) and Kimani Vidal (25). Through six regular-season games, Mitchell has turned 35 carries into 139 yards and added 12 catches (on 15 targets) for 52 yards and a score, but it's hard to put much trust into any of the Chargers' skill-position players given the team's poor start to the season. Perhaps the Week 7 bye will help the Chargers right the ship, with their next game taking place in Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Mitchell took six carries for 11 yards and caught three of four targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 23-17 loss versus the Broncos.
story: From scrimmage, Sunday was Mitchell's least productive game since Week 1, when he played just 17 offensive snaps. His nine touches in Week 5 tied with 2024 sixth-rounder Kimani Vidal, who managed 56 yards and a touchdown by comparison. Both were outpaced in the touches department by starter Omarion Hampton (15), though both Vidal and Mitchell should continue to be somewhat involved until Hampton is able to demonstrate some explosiveness out of the backfield.

headline: Mitchell tallied 10 carries for 39 yards and five catches (on six targets) for 24 yards during Sunday's 30-23 defeat at Seattle.
story: Mitchell surprisingly led the Chargers backfield in touches with 15, ahead of Omarion Hampton's 11 and Kimani Vidal's seven, but unlike his position mates he didn't reach the end zone. Because Mitchell's touch count has increased in each successive week this season, he's trending in a positive direction, but until one of the trio is handling most of the RB reps, it'll be difficult to trust any of them for fantasy purposes on a weekly basis. He next takes the field next Sunday against the Broncos.

headline: Mitchell (ankle) was a full participant in Friday's practice and does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: After being limited Wednesday and Thursday and wearing a walking boot earlier in the week, Mitchell's good to go against Seattle. At less than 100 percent and facing a stout defense, Mitchell is tough to get behind for fantasy lineups, even after he closed the snaps and touches gap on Omarion Hampton in last Sunday's loss to the Bills. Neither is an overly exciting Week 4 fantasy bet.

headline: Mitchell (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: For the second day in a row, Mitchell had his reps capped while he manages a left ankle injury. So long as he doesn't take a step back in activity during the Chargers' final practice of the week Friday, Mitchell should still be on track to suit up Sunday against the Seahawks. Through the team's first three games, Mitchell has carried 17 times for 85 yards (5.0 YPC) while adding four receptions for 10 yards and a touchdown in a complementary role behind lead back Omarion Hampton.

headline: Mitchell (ankle) was a limited participant at the Chargers' practice Wednesday, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Mitchell was spotted with a walking boot on his left leg, and the Chargers updated their injury report to reflect the running back as limited Wednesday. He may have suffered the left ankle injury during Wednesday's session, but he didn't express much concern about the injury, and the running back will have two more chances this week to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the Seahawks. If Mitchell is unavailable for Week 4, Kimani Vidal would serve as the top reserve option behind starter Omarion Hampton.

headline: Mitchell rushed eight times for 52 yards and caught all three of his targets for minus-5 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 24-16 loss to the Bills.
story: Mitchell found himself far move involved on offense in Week 3, nearly matching his previous season total of nine carries while the three targets matched a career high. The running back reached paydirt in the first quarter, reeling in a one-yard pass from quarterback Justin Herbert. Mitchell remained the team's second option out of the backfield behind starter Omarion Hampton, but he proved that he could have standalone fantasy value if he gets more consistent touches moving forward.

headline: Mitchell rushed five times for 24 yards and caught his only target for 15 yards during Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders.
story: Mitchell operated as a distant No. 2 option in the backfield, logging 17 snaps on offense while starter Omarion Hampton was on the field for 43 of the team's 68 offensive snaps. Mitchell was able to make the most of his opportunities, averaging 4.8 YPC while reeling in his first catch of the season. The running back also added 47 yards on two kickoff returns in the contest. Mitchell has shown enough to be worth a stash in deeper fantasy leagues, but he will continue to have a limited ceiling as long as Hampton is active.

headline: Mitchell rushed four times for nine yards in a Week 1 loss to Arizona on Sunday. He added 47 yards on two kickoff returns.
story: Mitchell had a long rush of eight yards but combined for just three yards on his other three carries. While he also contributed in the return game, it was a bland Chargers debut for the 24-year-old, who joined Los Angeles as a free agent in March. The Chargers' run game as a whole was largely stifled Sunday, as Omarion Hampton -- the only other RB on the team to log a carry -- finished with a mediocre 43 yards on 12 carries, though he did score a touchdown. Mitchell will look to make more of an impression in Week 2 versus Las Vegas next Sunday.

headline: Mitchell (hamstring) was a full participant in Friday's practice and does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: After logging limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, Mitchell got a full session in Friday and thus appears ready to go for Week 1. Mitchell is an intriguing option in an offense run by coordinator Mike McDaniel, but his injury slowed him for much of the past three weeks, so it's unclear exactly how he will slot in behind starter Omarion Hampton and fellow reserve Kimani Vidal.

headline: Mitchell (hamstring) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: The Chargers put a cap on Mitchell's reps for a second straight day, but his ability to practice in any capacity on consecutive days to kick off Week 1 prep is an encouraging sign for his chances of playing in Sunday's season opener versus the Cardinals. If he's cleared to play against Arizona, Mitchell would likely be in line for a complementary role behind lead back Omarion Hampton.

headline: Mitchell (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: Mitchell returned to practice earlier this week, and a limited session to open the week gives him a good chance to take the field Sunday against the Cardinals. Mitchell is expected to serve as the big-play complementary back behind Omarion Hampton this season. He's worthy of a bench stash in most fantasy leagues.

headline: Mitchell (undisclosed) returned to practice Monday, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: After six straight missed practices, Mitchell's return is a positive step for his Week 1 outlook against the Cardinals. When healthy, Mitchell is expected to serve in a sort-of lightning role to Omarion Hampton's thunder out of the backfield. Mitchell may not be immediately usable in fantasy leagues as a starter, but he's one of the higher-upside bench stashes to see what his role is under new OC Mike McDaniel, who personally campaigned for Mitchell's signing in Los Angeles.

headline: Dicker made all three of his field-goal attempts during Sunday's 24-9 loss against the Rams. He did not kick any extra-point tries.
story: The Chargers offense put forth another poor effort in Week 8, with four of their 11 drives ending in punts and another three ending with turnovers. Dicker has mostly been efficient through his first seven games of the season, making 12 of his 14 field-goal attempts, but until the offense demonstrates it can consistently move the ball down the field, he'll be hard to trust as a fantasy option.

headline: Dicker made both of his field-goal attempts in the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
story: Dicker's 23-yard and 30-yard field goals were the only points scored by the Chargers in the team's blowout loss. While the offense could not get going, as has been the theme all season, Dicker remained reliable. The 26-year-old moves to 9-for-11 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 9-for-9 on extra-point attempts over six regular-season games in 2026.

headline: Dicker made his lone field-goal attempt and both of his extra-point tries during the Chargers' 23-17 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Dicker got the Chargers on the board with a 42-yard field goal in the second quarter before adding two PATs in the second half. Dicker has attempted one field goal or zero in three of the first five games of the regular season and has yet to make a field goal from 50-plus yards. He's 7-for-9 on field-goal attempts and 9-for-9 on extra-point tries heading into a Week 6 road matchup Oct. 18 against the Chiefs, who are coming off a bye.

headline: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 30-23 loss to Seattle.
story: Dicker made field goals from 40 and 39 yards in the first half before converting a 36-yarder late in the fourth quarter. The kicker had missed a field-goal try in each of the last two games entering Week 4, but he was able to get back on track against the Seahawks. Dicker has now gone 6-for-8 on field-goal attempts while making all seven of his extra-point tries over four contests this year.

headline: Dicker went 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made his lone extra-point try during the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
story: Dicker's made field goals came from 33, 21 and 33 yards, with his miss early in the second quarter coming from 45 yards. Dicker has missed two of his five field-goal attempts through the first three games of the regular season, well below the 90 percent success rate he enjoyed in each of the first four years of his NFL career.

headline: Dicker missed his lone field-goal attempt but made both PATs in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders.
story: The Chargers lost by the score of 26-14 for the second straight week, and both were upsets at home. The day started off on the wrong foot, as Dicker hit the right upright from 58 yards out to end Los Angeles' opening drive. Through two games, he's still looking for his first made field goal after not attempting any against Arizona in Week 1. Things won't get any easier next Sunday on the road outdoors against the Bills.

headline: Dicker converted both of his point-after tries in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
story: It was a stunning loss by the Chargers after they were installed as double-digit favorites at home against Arizona. Still the most accurate kicker in NFL history with a 93.5 percent success rate on field goals, Dicker was fantasy's No. 5 overall kicker in points per game last season, as he made 38 of 41 field-goal tries and 34 of 35 PATs. The Chargers will try to right the ship next Sunday at home against the Raiders.

headline: Dicker (undisclosed) was not listed on Wednesday's injury report.
story: Dicker was working through an undisclosed issue toward the tail end of training camp, but his absence from the Chargers' first injury report of the week indicates that he's fully healthy for Sunday's regular-season opener against the Cardinals. Dicker was a top-5 kicker in fantasy last season, connecting on 38 of 41 field-goal attempts (including 12-for-13 on attempts from 50-plus yards) while making 34 of 35 extra-point tries across 17 regular-season games.
