story: Werner has been unable to practice since sustaining a neck injury in the Saints' Week 3 loss to the Raiders. If the linebacker cannot practice in any capacity Saturday, the chances he suits up for Monday night's game against the Falcons will be low.

headline: Werner (neck) did not participate at the Saints' practice Thursday.
story: Werner sustained a neck injury in the first half of the team's Week 3 loss to Las Vegas, and he was unable to return to the contest. The linebacker will have two more chances to practice before Monday night's matchup with the Falcons.

headline: Werner (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Raiders, Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
story: Werner suffered a stinger in the first half, and his status for the rest of the game is now in question. In his absence, Isaiah Stalbird and Danny Stutsman are two candidates to see an increase in workload at inside linebacker.

headline: Werner recorded 11 tackles (eight solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Sunday's 24-17 win at Baltimore.
story: Werner was one of the main factors in keeping the Ravens' rushing attack in check in Week 2, and he managed his best tackle total since Week 5 of the 2025 season. He'll be hoping to keep the momentum up in a Week 3 tilt versus the Raiders.

headline: Werner (groin) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Werner spent most of August dealing with a groin injury he sustained in a training camp practice. The linebacker has fully recovered from the issue and is all set to practice in full as the Saints prepare for a Week 1 clash with the Lions.

headline: Sanker posted nine tackles (seven solo) in Sunday's Week 7 loss to Pittsburgh.
story: Sanker recorded his second-highest tackle tally of the campaign to lead New Orleans in that category. The second-year defender has now tallied six or more stops in five of his seven games this season. With 44 tackles through seven contests, Sanker is easily on pace to surpass the 80 stops he notched in 17 games as a rookie.

headline: Sanker (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Sanker had limited practice participation Wednesday seemingly as a precautionary measure, and his return to a full session Thursday puts the second-year defensive back on track to play Sunday against Las Vegas. Sanker has 13 tackles (10 solo) through two regular-season games.

headline: Sanker (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Sanker likely sustained his knee injury in the Saints' Week 2 win over the Ravens. The defensive back secured three solo tackles on 34 defensive snaps in the effort. The 23-year-old will need to upgrade to full practice participation by Friday to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.

headline: Sanker recorded 10 total tackles (seven solo) in Sunday's 31-30 overtime loss to the Lions.
story: Sanker started off the 2026 campaign with a bang, securing double-digit takedowns in a contest for the first time in his young career. The 23-year-old primarily played safety last season, but he now is slotted in as the team's primary slot cornerback in his second year with New Orleans.

headline: Fant gathered in all two targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 16-10 defeat against Pittsburgh.
story: After finding the end zone twice in the loss to the Raiders in Week 3, Fant has combined for just three catches in his previous three appearances. While his two receptions Sunday were a small step in the right direction, he is expected to continue to play second fiddle to Juwan Johnson moving forward. It may also be a matter of time before rookie Oscar Delp logs more snaps from week to week.

headline: Fant brought in his lone target for seven yards during the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Fant played 30 of 45 offensive snaps Sunday in his return from a one-game absence due to an abdominal injury, which was one more than fellow tight end Juwan Johnson. Fant saw only one target from Tyler Shough, although the Saints' offense struggled as a whole against the Vikings' defense. Fant has a 9-73-3 receiving line on 13 targets through four games heading into Week 7 against the Giants, whose defense has given up 33 catches to tight ends this season, tied for fifth-most in the NFL.

headline: Fant (abdomen) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Vikings.
story: Fant opened the week with back-to-back limited practices before logging a full session Friday, which was enough for him to shed an injury tag and put himself in a position to return from a one-game absence due to an abdominal injury. He has an 8-66-3 receiving line (on 12 targets) through three regular-season games while operating as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson.

headline: Fant (abdomen) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: After sitting out Monday's loss to Atlanta, Fant has had his reps capped for the Saints' first two Week 5 practices while he continues to manage the abdominal injury. He'll likely need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid taking a designation into Sunday's matchup with the Vikings. When available this season, Fant has been productive as the Saints' No. 2 tight end behind Juwan Johnson, registering eight receptions for 66 yards and three touchdowns on 12 targets over three appearances.

headline: Fant (abdomen) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: Fant missed Monday night's loss to the Falcons, but his limited start to the week would seem to give the veteran tight end a good shot to return to the field for Week 5 against the Vikings. He's turned 12 targets into eight catches for 66 yards and three touchdowns this season as one of Tyler Shough's favorite options near the end zone.

headline: Fant (abdomen) is listed as inactive for Monday's game against the Falcons.
story: Despite being a limited practice participant during Week 4 prep, Fant will miss his first contest of the campaign due to an abdominal injury. Oscar Delp and Treyton Welch thus will serve as the reserve tight ends behind starter Juwan Johnson on Monday. Fant's next chance to play is this coming Sunday versus the Vikings.

headline: Fant (abdomen) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Falcons, Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
story: Fant's practice participation was limited all week due to an abdominal injury that he likely picked up in Week 3 against the Raiders. With the questionable tag, the veteran tight end's status for Monday may not be known until the Saints announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. Oscar Delp and Treyton Welch would see more rotational snaps at tight end behind Juwan Johnson if Fant is not cleared to play against Atlanta.

headline: Fant (abdomen) practiced in a limited capacity Friday, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Fant maintained his activity level for a second session in a row, giving him just one more chance to get back to full this week. Saturday's injury report will reveal if he's in danger of missing Monday's game against the Falcons due to his abdominal issue.

headline: Fant was limited in practice Thursday due to an abdominal injury.
story: Fant has taken full advantage of his 12 targets through three games this season, turning them into eight catches for 66 yards and three touchdowns. Now, a health concern is impacting him at the start of Week 4 prep, so his status bears watching as the Saints ramp up for Monday's matchup with the Falcons.

headline: Fant caught all four of his targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 35-27 loss to Las Vegas.
story: Fant made the most of his opportunities, connecting with quarterback Tyler Shough for a three-yard touchdown in the second quarter and a 16-yard score in the third quarter. The tight end is the No. 2 option behind Juwan Johnson at his position, but Fant has still caught eight of 12 targets for 66 yards and three scores over the first three games this year.

headline: Fant caught four of his eight targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-30 overtime loss to the Lions.
story: Tyler Shough enjoyed targeting tight ends in Sunday's shootout, with the duo of Fant and Juwan Johnson totalling 87 yards and two touchdowns between them. If Shough's favoritism for the bigger-bodied targets with a higher catch radius continues, Fant could become a solid option in deeper leagues.

headline: Lance reeled in all two targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh.
story: Lance had two catches for the second consecutive game, though unlike the Week 6 win over the Giants, he didn't find the end zone. The 24-year-old has logged 332 offensive snaps this season, third in the receiving corps behind Chris Olave (387) and Devaughn Vele (438). However, despite being on the field more often than most of the other wideouts on the roster, Lance hasn't been productive thus far in his rookie campaign.

headline: Lance caught two of four passes for nine yards and a touchdown during the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants on Sunday.
story: Lance's four targets were tied with Alvin Kamara for third most on the Saints behind Chris Olave (seven) and Devaughn Vele (six), with quarterback Tyler Shough completing only 16 of 30 passes. Both of Lance's catches came in the second quarter, the second of which was a two-yard touchdown that tied the game up at 10-10 with five seconds left in the first half. Lance's 36 offensive snaps were third most among New Orleans wide receivers, but his time as the team's WR3 could come to an end as soon as Week 7 against the Steelers on Oct. 25, given that rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR) is traveling with the team to Paris, per NewOrleans.Football.

headline: Lance turned five targets into a seven-yard catch during the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday.
story: Lance finished fifth on the Saints in targets from quarterback Tyler Shough, though each of the four misses between the duo came on deep passes. After catching three of four targets for 42 yards in his NFL debut against the Lions in Week 1, Lance has just two catches (on nine targets) for 15 yards over his last three games. He'll continue to operate as the Saints' WR3 behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. Lance's playing time likely will take a significant hit once fellow rookie Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is cleared to return from injured reserve, though ESPN's Adam Schefter notes that Week 7 against the Steelers is the earliest targeted return for Tyson. The Saints will stay at home for Week 5 against the Vikings and their aggressive defense.

headline: Lance caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 24-17 victory against Baltimore.
story: Lance was on the field for 54 of New Orleans' 68 offensive snaps, but he had only one pass thrown his way by Tyler Shough. Chris Olave (10 targets) and Devaughn Vele (seven) got 17 of the Saints' 19 total wideout targets, so Lance wasn't alone in having a quiet day among the team's complementary options. Barion Brown logged just two offensive snaps Sunday and Kevin Austin notched five, so Lance seems to be clearly ahead of both in the pecking order.

headline: Lance caught three of four targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 31-30 loss to the Lions in overtime.
story: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) on injured reserve and Chris Olave in and out of the game multiple times Sunday, Lance played 62 of 90 offensive snaps against Detroit. He ran 45 routes on Tyler Slough's 63 dropbacks and looks like the clear WR3 for New Orleans while Tyson recovers from a severe hamstring strain. However, Lance is deep down the list for opportunities and touches behind Olave, Juwan Johnson, Travis Etienne and Devaughn Vele, giving him minimal fantasy appeal outside of dynasty formats.

headline: Miller rushed eight times for six yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers in Paris.
story: The Saints got absolutely nothing going on the ground against Pittsburgh, rushing 17 times for 18 yards as a team, so it's not like Miller and his team-leading eight carries was the only issue. New Orleans heads into its bye in Week 8, and Travis Etienne (hamstring) will be eligible to come off injured reserve for Week 9 against the Browns. When both Etienne and Alvin Kamara were healthy and active together earlier this season, Miller was a healthy inactive.

headline: Miller carried the ball 20 times for 70 yards and caught both his targets for zero yards in Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
story: Alvin Kamara missed time in the first half due to an undisclosed injury, and while he was able to return and make an impact as a pass catcher, Miller led the Saints in rushing yards and touches with 22. The 70 yards also represented his best total since Week 18 of his rookie season in 2023. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) not eligible to return until after a Week 8 bye, Miller should split reps in the backfield with Kamara once again in Week 7 against the Steelers in Paris.

headline: Miller turned 10 carries into 30 yards and a touchdown during the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Miller averaged only 3.0 YPC during Sunday's loss, but his two-yard touchdown run midway through the second quarter gave the Saints an early 7-3 lead, although New Orleans' offense generated only three more points the rest of the way. His 10 carries led the Saints' backfield that also includes CJ Donaldson (four carries) and Alvin Kamara (three), though Miller had only three rushes during the second half. Kamara dealt with a back issue during Week 5 prep, and if that issue continues to linger, then Miller could be the Saints' lead back for Week 6 against the Giants this Sunday.

headline: Miller rushed six time for nine yards and caught two of three targets while losing a fumble in Monday night's 45-24 loss to Atlanta.
story: Miller was rumored to be on track for a larger workload in Week 4 after starting running back Travis Etienne (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve. Miller was only on the field for 26 percent of the team's offensive snaps, which could have been as a result of a first-quarter fumble that Atlanta ultimately recovered. Veteran Alvin Kamara was on the field for 41 percent of the offensive snaps, turning seven carries into 23 yards and two scores while also reeling in five of seven targets for 35 yards in the contest. It appears as if Miller will operate as the No. 2 option behind Kamara in Etienne's absence, making him a low-upside fantasy option.

headline: Miller is in line for a larger offensive role for as long as Travis Etienne (hamstring) is on injured reserve, John DeShazler of the Saints' official site reports.
story: Etienne's placement on IR on Thursday comes after the star running back aggravated a hamstring injury during the Saints' Week 3 loss to the Raiders. With Etienne sidelined, Miller and Alvin Kamara figure to operate as the Saints' top running backs moving forward, with undrafted rookie CJ Donaldson also in the mix for backfield work. Miller has 13 carries for 44 yards (3.4 YPC) and a touchdown along with two catches (on three targets) for five yards through two regular-season games.

headline: Miller (illness) doesn't carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Miller was under the weather Thursday, keeping him off the practice field. However, he was a full participant Friday. Miller was a healthy scratch for the 24-17 win over Baltimore in Week 2, meaning he is in danger of suffering the same fate versus Las Vegas, though his services may be needed on special teams with WR Barion Brown (hamstring) ruled out. With that in mind, if Miller is inactive, that would likely mean more work for Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson behind Travis Etienne.

headline: Miller was a non-participant in Thursday's practice due to an illness, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: After being a healthy inactive Week 2 win over the Ravens while the Saints welcomed Alvin Kamara (knee) back from a one-game absence, Miller will now have to overcome an illness as he looks to re-enter the backfield mix Sunday versus the Raiders. Even if he makes a full recovery from the ailment, Miller may need No. 1 back Travis Etienne (hamstring) to sit out the Week 3 game in order to avoid another inactive status. Etienne has been limited in both of the Saints' practices this week, clouding his availability for Sunday.

headline: Miller (coach's decision) is listed as inactive Sunday in Baltimore.
story: Miller served as the No. 2 RB behind Travis Etienne in Week 1 with Alvin Kamara inactive due to a knee issue, but with Kamara back in action Sunday, Miller will be a healthy scratch. That leaves CJ Donaldson as the active third backfield option behind Etienne and Kamara in Week 2. Miller's next chance for game action is next Sunday against the Raiders.

headline: Miller turned nine carries into 30 yards and a touchdown while adding a 19-yard kickoff return during the Saints' 31-30 overtime loss to the Lions on Sunday.
story: The Saints were kept scoreless in the first half, but Miller helped get New Orleans on the board in the third quarter with an eight-yard touchdown run. In the absence of Alvin Kamara (knee), Miller played 29 of 90 offensive snaps (32.2 percent) and operated as the Saints' RB2 behind Travis Etienne (53 offensive snaps). Miller's role on offense would decrease drastically if Kamara was cleared to play against the Ravens in Week 2.

headline: Miller was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Miller was dealing with an unknown issue, but the running back's presence in practice indicates he has recovered. The 24-year-old is set to be the No. 2 option behind Travis Etienne for the Saints' Week 1 matchup with the Lions.

headline: Brown hauled in all three targets for 57 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
story: Brown had the most productive game of his NFL career thus far, catching more passes than he had in his previous five appearances combined. The 2026 No. 190 overall pick should continue to get consistent work on special teams. However, despite the recent uptick in offensive snaps, it's unknown if Brown will continue to be more involved as a pass catcher moving forward.

headline: Brown (thigh) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
story: Brown was a full participant in Friday's practice, signaling that the returner and No. 4 wide receiver has recovered from the thigh injury he suffered in the Saints' Week 4 loss to the Falcons. Brown is all set to suit up for the Saints and will likely handle most of the return duties in Sunday's contest.

headline: Brown (thigh) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Emily Leiker of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
story: Brown was limited by a thigh injury in each of the first two practices of Week 5 prep. Although he's tagged as questionable, his ability to practice in full Friday gives Brown a solid chance at being cleared to play against Minnesota. If the rookie sixth-rounder is ruled out, then Kendre Miller and Jayden Price would likely operate as the Saints' top return options on kickoffs and punts.

headline: Brown recorded one carry for a loss of five yards while also adding 130 kickoff-return yards and a two-yard punt return during Monday night's 45-24 loss to the Falcons.
story: Brown made his return to action Monday after missing the team's Week 3 loss to Las Vegas while nursing a hamstring injury. The wide receiver logged just three snaps on offense, failing to garner a target against Atlanta. Brown will continue to have no offensive upside barring an injury to another member of the Saints' WR room.

headline: Brown (hamstring) has no injury designation ahead of Monday's Week 4 matchup against Atlanta.
story: Brown missed last Sunday's loss to Las Vegas due to a hamstring injury. However, he logged an LP/LP/FP practice progression this week and has been cleared to suit up Monday. Brown's primary role for the Saints this season has been as a kick and punt returner, and he has no targets on offense so far while logging nine offensive snaps through two games.

headline: Brown (hamstring) is listed as out for Sunday's game versus Las Vegas.
story: Brown didn't practice all week due to a hamstring injury and will now miss the first game of his career. The rookie logged a combined nine offensive snaps in Weeks 1 and 2, though his absence will be felt on special teams. As a result, Jayden Price may be busier than usual in Week 3. That could also apply to Kendre Miller (illness), assuming he's not a healthy scratch for the second consecutive game.

headline: Ridgeway (foot) was not listed on the Saints' official injury report Wednesday.
story: Ridgeway sustained a foot injury during a practice in August, but it's no longer a concern with Week 1 officially underway. With veteran Cameron Jordan (hamstring) out, Ridgeway could be in line for a more significant role on the defensive line than he's accustomed to Sunday.

headline: Welch (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Steelers in Paris, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
story: Welch had appeared in five of the Saints' first six games but will be in street clothes for the contest in France while New Orleans keeps just three tight ends active (Juwan Johnson, Noah Fant and Oscar Delp). In his prior five outings, Welch had drawn just one target while seeing the bulk of his snaps on special teams.

headline: The Saints signed Welch to the active roster from the practice squad Saturday, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
story: With Audric Estime (thigh) moved to IR in a surprise move, the Saints gained an open spot on the 53-man roster. Welch will be the No. 3 tight end due to Oscar Delp (hamstring) being ruled out and will likely participate almost exclusively on special teams and in 13-personnel sets, if he plays at all in the team's Week 1 matchup with the Lions.

headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Giants on Sunday.
story: As the emergency third quarterback, Wilson is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Vikings as the Saints' emergency third quarterback.
story: Wilson remains the No. 3 QB behind Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler. Wilson can be called upon to enter the contest only if both active quarterbacks are forced out of the game.

headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback for Monday night's contest against the Falcons.
story: Wilson will operate as the team's No. 3 QB for the fourth game in a row to begin the 2026 campaign. Wilson will only be eligible to enter the contest if both starter Tyler Shough and top backup Spencer Rattler are forced out of the game.

headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday.
story: For a third consecutive week, Wilson will be the Saints' emergency QB3, meaning he cannot play Sunday unless both Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Ravens on Sunday.
story: For a second consecutive week, Wilson will be the emergency QB3 behind starter Tyler Shough and backup Spencer Rattler. Wilson is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Shough and Rattler leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive as the emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the Lions.
story: Spencer Rattler kept his gig as the QB2 behind Tyler Shough this summer, leaving Wilson as the emergency option entering the season. Wilson appeared in four games with the Dolphins last season, completing six of 11 passes for 32 yards.

headline: Johnson caught one of three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
story: Johnson was held in check yet again in Week 7. The tight end has now gone three straight games without exceeding 16 receiving yards, and he hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 3. Johnson has slowly become an unreliable fantasy option as the season has progressed, but he'll have the opportunity to hit the reset button during the Saints' bye week in Week 8.

headline: Johnson failed to reel in either of his targets during Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
story: Johnson went without a catch in a regular-season contest for the first time since Week 3 of the 2024 campaign. The tight end had reeled in at least three passes in each of the team's first five games of the year. Over the last two weeks, Johnson has caught four of seven targets for 16 yards, and his next chance to get back on track will come in Week 7 against the Steelers in Paris.

headline: Johnson brought in four of five targets for 16 yards in the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
story: The veteran tight end tied Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele for the team lead in receptions, but given Tyler Shough threw for only 96 yards overall, Johnson couldn't generate any meaningful fantasy production with his quartet of catches. Johnson has recorded at least four receptions in four straight games, and despite Sunday's season-low yardage total, he's still compiled a solid 248 receiving yards and has five catches of 20-plus yards heading into a Week 6 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

headline: Johnson secured six of eight targets for 59 yards in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday night.
story: Johnson tied for second in receptions and also finished as the runner-up in receiving yards on the night for the Saints in the lopsided loss. The veteran tight end has gotten the season off to a productive start, recording at least 53 receiving yards in each contest and posting 14 of his 21 catches of the season in the last two games alone. Johnson also has drawn at least seven targets in three of the first four games, affording him a very appealing fantasy floor going into a Week 5 home matchup against the Vikings on Sunday.

headline: Johnson caught all eight of his targets for 53 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders.
story: The veteran tight end continues to have an impressive start to the season, hauling in TD strikes of one and two yards from Tyler Shough. but Johnson had a tough end to his day as he fumbled to end the Saints' final possession while they were trying to mount a comeback late in the fourth quarter. Johnson has put together a 15-173-3 line on 19 targets through three games, and he'll look to atone for his miscue in a Week 4 home tilt against the Falcons.

headline: Johnson caught all four targets for 66 yards in Sunday's 24-17 win over the Ravens.
story: Johnson dealt with an illness during the week but played 36 of 68 offensive snaps and ran 23 routes on Tyler Shough's 39 dropbacks. It was a dip in snap rate and route share compared to Week 1 for Johnson, but he still out-targeted Noah Fant four to zero against Baltimore. Through two games, Johnson has seven catches for 120 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets. It will be interesting to see if his snaps and routes come back up to Week 1 levels next Sunday against the Raiders.

headline: Johnson (illness) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Baltimore
story: Johnson sat out Wednesday's practice entirely due to an illness, but he ramped up as the week went on, going from limited Thursday to all activity Friday, thereby clearing him for Week 2 action. The status of New Orleans' top WR Chris Olave (hamstring) is in question heading into the weekend, so Johnson could be poised for more looks from QB Tyler Shough on Sunday, even if Olave is able to suit up. Johnson turned his seven Week 1 targets into three catches for 54 yards and one touchdown in an overtime loss at Detroit.

headline: Johnson (illness) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
story: Johnson took a step in the right direction after sitting out practice entirely Wednesday. He still has a chance to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens if Johnson can upgrade to full participation Friday. Johnson caught three of seven targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints' Week 1 overtime loss at Detroit.

headline: Johnson (illness) returned to practice Thursday, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: After missing Wednesday's practice due to an illness, Johnson got back in the mix Thursday. The Saints' injury report will clarify whether he was a limited or full participant. Regardless, this is a good sign for Johnson's availability heading into Sunday's game against the Ravens.

headline: Johnson did not participate in Wednesday's practice due to an illness.
story: Johnson's absence from Wednesday's practice was likely a precautionary measure, and the veteran tight end will have two more chances to return to practice ahead of the Saints' Week 2 road tilt against the Ravens on Sunday. Johnson had a career year in 2025 and produced a 3-54-1 receiving line (on seven targets) during the Saints' 31-30 overtime loss to the Lions in Week 1. With rookie first-round wideout Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) on injured reserve, Johnson, Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele are likely going to be the go-to targets in the passing game for quarterback Tyler Shough.

headline: Johnson caught three of his seven targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-30 overtime loss to the Lions.
story: Johnson had a strong Week 1, with Tyler Shough targeting the No. 1 tight end at the third-highest rate among Saints players. Only Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele saw more targets, but Johnson's 18.0 yards per reception were second only to Olave's 18.2.

headline: Vele caught all five of his targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
story: The third-year wideout was on the other end of Tyler Shough's only TD pass of the day, hauling in a one-yard toss in the second quarter for the Saints' final points. Vele tied his career high with his third touchdown of the season, and his 33-348-3 line on 48 targets through seven games has him tracking toward a career-best campaign heading into a Week 8 bye. His role could shrink significantly after the bye, however, if rookie Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is cleared to make his NFL debut.

headline: Vele caught three of six targets for 42 yards during the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants on Sunday.
story: Vele was on the field for 66 of the Saints' 70 offensive snaps (94.3 percent), which was well ahead of fellow wideouts Chris Olave (42) and rookie Bryce Lance (36). Vele has seen at least six targets in each of the first six games of the regular season, and his 28-294-2 line on 43 targets already surpasses his totals across 13 regular-season games in 2025 (25-293-2 on 40 targets). Given his snap count, it wouldn't be surprising if Vele maintains his role in the offense even if Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR) returns, which could come as soon as Week 7 against the Steelers on Oct. 25 in Paris.

headline: Vele secured four of six targets for 26 yards in the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Vele finished in a three-way tie with Chris Olave and Juwan Johnson for the team lead in receptions and also drew even with Olave for top slotting in targets. However, that meant little on a day when Tyler Shough was held to 3.8 yards per attempt by an aggressive Vikings defense and finished with just 96 passing yards overall. Vele's quiet afternoon notwithstanding, the third-year wideout has now seen at least six targets in each game and has impressively converted 14 of his 25 receptions into first downs. Vele will take a 25-252-2 line on 37 targets into a Week 6 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

headline: Vele secured six of nine targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday night.
story: Vele tied for second in receptions and checked in as the runner-up in targets for the Saints on the night, and he rounded out a solid fantasy performance by recording a three-yard touchdown reception with 1:13 remaining. The score was ultimately meaningless to the outcome of the lopsided loss, but Vele further cemented his standing as a relatively high-volume No. 2 receiver by tying his season high in targets. Vele will take a 21-226-2 line on 31 targets into a Week 5 home matchup against the Vikings on Sunday.

headline: Vele caught three of six targets for 39 yards Sunday in a loss to Las Vegas.
story: Tyler Shough had another big day at quarterback for the Saints, with 160 of his 255 passing yards going to the combination of No. 1 wideout Chris Olave and top tight end Juwan Johnson. Vele finished third behind that duo in both targets (six) and receiving yards (39). The third-year wideout has been locked into a key role in the Saints' passing game, and through three contests he's registered 15 catches on 22 targets for 172 yards and one touchdown.

headline: Vele caught five of seven targets for 64 yards during Sunday's 24-17 win over the Ravens.
story: Vele was able to remain a major part of the Saints' offensive attack, finishing second on the team in targets behind fellow wide receiver Chris Olave (10) in Week 2. The 28-year-old appears to have solidified himself as the team's No. 2 wide receiver with Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) on injured reserve, catching 12 of 16 targets for 133 yards and a touchdown over the first two games of the 2026 campaign. Vele will have a strong chance to keep up his hot start to the season when New Orleans faces the Raiders in Week 3.

headline: Vele caught seven passes on nine targets for 69 yards and a touchdown during the Saints' 31-30 overtime loss to the Lions on Sunday.
story: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) on injured reserve, Vele lined up as the Saints' WR2 behind Chris Olave. The Saints' offense found its footing in the second half after being blanked in the first, with Vele contributing by catching a one-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Shough before the duo connected on a 31-yard pass early in the fourth quarter, leading to a 28-yard field goal from Daniel Carlson four plays later. Vele was one catch shy from matching a career high he set twice before Sunday, and he could be a prominent piece in the Saints' offense alongside Olave, running back Travis Etienne and tight end Juwan Johnson. Vele and the Saints will stay on the road for Week 2 against the Ravens on Sept. 20.

headline: Eluemunor (calf) is active Week 7 against the Texans, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Eluemunor managed just a pair of limited practices this week, but the veteran tackle will ultimately be available for a Giants team that has both Marcus Mbow (knee) and Josh Sills (coach's decision) on the inactive list Sunday.

headline: Eluemunor (calf) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: Eluemunor missed Week 6 due to a calf injury he sustained during prep earlier in the week. The right tackle has a chance to suit up for Sunday's contest, but if he must miss consecutive weeks, Marcus Mbow will likely see another start.

headline: Eluemanor (calf) was a limited participant at the Giants' practice Thursday.
story: Eluemanor was inactive for the team's Week 6 loss to the Saints while nursing a calf injury, and he opened the week as a non-participant at practice Wednesday. The offensive lineman's ability to return to practice Thursday is a step in the right direction, and he'll have one more chance to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with Houston.

headline: Eluemunor (calf) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Saints, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
story: While left tackle Andrew Thomas is set to suit up, Eluemunor was unable to overcome his calf injury in time for Sunday's contest. Marcus Mbow or J.C. Davis will start at right tackle against the Saints in Eluemunor's absence.

headline: Eluemunor (calf) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: Eluemunor was injured in last Sunday's tie with the Commanders and was unable to return. With both Eluemunor and starting left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) questionable, the Giants have a pair of key injuries along the offensive line.

headline: Eluemunor (calf) is considered day-to-day ahead of the Giants' Week 6 matchup with the Saints, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News
story: Eluemunor suffered a calf injury during Sunday's 27-27 tie against the Commanders, and he required assistance to get off the field. The 31-year-old appears to have avoided a significant injury, and his first chance to practice this week will come Wednesday.

headline: Eluemunor (calf) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Commanders, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
story: Eluemunor needed assistance off the field, and with the game nearing the end, it's possible he's done for the remainder of Week 5. If that's the case, Marcus Mbow would likely take over the rest of the way.

headline: Newsome (concussion) wasn't listed on the Giants' injury report Wednesday.
story: Newsome is healthy again after missing the Week 7 win over the Texans due to a concussion. The 26-year-old signed a three-year extension with the team Tuesday and will resume his role as one of its starting cornerbacks during Sunday's matchup against the Eagles.

headline: Newsome (concussion) agreed Tuesday with the Giants on a three-year $46 million extension that includes $32 million guaranteed, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Newsome joined the Giants in the offseason on a one-year, $8 million deal, but he earned himself some longer-term security with his standout play to begin the campaign. Before a concussion kept him out for the Giants' Week 7 win over Houston, the 26-year-old cornerback recorded 25 tackles (17 solo), six pass breakups and one interception through the team's first six games.

headline: Newsome (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: Newsome entered the league's concussion protocol during the Giants' Week 6 loss to the Saints, and he was held out of practice all week. The Giants are thin in the secondary, so one of Colton Hood or Nic Jones figures to start opposite Deonte Banks at outside cornerback. New York is on a bye for Week 8, so Newsome's next chance to play is Week 9 against Philadelphia on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Newsome (concussion) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Newsome was knocked out of Sunday's game versus the Saints early by a concussion, and now his availability for Week 7 is in jeopardy. He'll have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before getting the green light to return to full-contact football activities, and whether he's able to return to practice Thursday or Friday may shed some light on any potential progress.

headline: Newsome (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Saints, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
story: Newsome exited Sunday's game with a head injury. The cornerback was diagnosed with a concussion and has now entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol. Newsome will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact football activities.

headline: Newsome registered seven tackles (four solo) and an interception during the Giants' win Sunday versus the Cardinals.
story: Newsome had his most productive outing of the campaign, logging a season-high seven tackles in addition to recording his first interception. The 26-year-old will look to build on this strong performance and keep producing during next week's matchup against the Commanders.

headline: Newsome (ribs) does not have any injury designation ahead of Monday night's game against the Rams, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Newsome upgraded to full participation in Saturday's practice after being limited Thursday and Friday. The cornerback has overcome his rib injury just in time to suit up for Monday night's game. With Deonte Banks (calf) still questionable to play, Newsome's presence will be huge for a Giants defense that will have to deal with Davante Adams and maybe Puka Nacua (hip).

headline: Newsome (ribs) was a limited participant at practice Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: The exact nature of his injury is still unknown, but Newsome's status for Week 2 is now up in the air. If he can't return to practice in full Friday or Saturday, he might end up carrying an injury designation on the final injury report before Monday night's game against the Rams.

headline: Newsome (knee) was not listed on the injury report following Wednesday's practice.
story: Newsome was working through a knee issue during training camp, but his full participation in Wednesday's practice indicates that he'll play against the Cowboys on Sunday. Newsome joined the Giants in March on a one-year, $10 million contract, and he projects to start opposite Deonte Banks at outside corner, while Paulson Adebo and rookie second-rounder Colton Hood provide depth at the position. Newsome appeared in 12 regular-season games for the Jaguars in 2025, finishing with 29 tackles (23 solo) and six pass defenses (including one interception).

headline: Holland (concussion) was not listed on the Giants' injury report Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
story: Holland was forced to miss the team's overtime win against the Texans in Week 7 while recovering from a concussion, but he now appears to have cleared concussion protocol. The 26-year-old will be back in his starting role in New York's secondary versus Philadelphia on Sunday.

headline: Holland (concussion) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Holland entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol after the Giants' Week 6 loss to the Saints. The safety has not been cleared by an independent neurologist to play in Sunday's game, leaving Ar'Darius Washington to suit up as the starting free safety for the Giants in Week 7.

headline: Holland (concussion) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: Holland entered the league's concussion protocol following the Giants' Week 6 loss to the Saints. He was limited in practice Thursday and Friday, but he won't be permitted to play Sunday unless he's cleared to do so by an independent neurologist. Tyler Nubin (neck) is also listed as questionable, so Jason Pinnock and Ar'Darius Washington could be the Giants' starting safeties for Week 7.

headline: Holland (concussion) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: Holland will still need to go through the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before Sunday's game at Houston if he is going to play in that contest, but he's at least moving in the right direction. His activity at practice Friday could give some indication as to how close he is to being cleared for game action by an independent neurologist.

headline: Holland (concussion) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Holland presumably suffered the concussion during Sunday's game versus the Saints, and now his status for Week 7 is up in the air. He'll need to clear league concussion protocol before being allowed to return to game action, and his activity at practice Thursday and Friday could offer some insight into any progress he makes as the week continues.

headline: Holland logged eight tackles (five solo), one pass defensed for an interception and one fumble recovery in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
story: Holland tied Tyler Nubin for the most Giants tackles in Monday's loss. The free safety picked off reigning MVP Matthew Stafford in the second quarter of the game as the Giants tried to mount a comeback. Holland also helped force and recovered a Kyren Williams fumble at the Rams' 11-yard line late in the first half, setting up the first of two field goals that constituted New York's scoring Monday night.

headline: Johnson (neck) was a full participant at the Giants' practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
story: Johnson appears to be back to full health after missing the team's last two contests while nursing a neck injury. The 25-year-old will be back in his No. 2 role at tight end behind starter Isaiah Likely against the Eagles on Sunday.

headline: Johnson (neck) participated during practice Monday, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
story: Johnson missed the Giants' last two games before their bye in Week 8 due to a neck injury, but it looks like the last week of rest may have benefitted him. His status on the Giants' first official injury report of the week Wednesday should shed more light on whether he'll be available in Week 9 at Philadelphia.

headline: Johnson (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Johnson's lack of participation in Friday's practice session appears to have been indicative of his playing status for Sunday's contest. The tight end will not be able to overcome his neck injury in time for Week 7 and will have to look toward the Giants' Week 9 contest against the Eagles after the bye.

headline: Johnson (neck) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: Johnson's reps in each of the first two practices of Week 7 prep were limited due to a neck injury, and he was sidelined entirely for Friday's session. He's trending toward missing a second consecutive game, so Thomas Fidone and Chris Manhertz would both be in line for more work behind Isaiah Likely in the event that Johnson is ruled out for Sunday's contest.

headline: Johnson (neck) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: Johnson was back at practice Wednesday after being sidelined because of a neck injury in Week 6 versus the Saints, but another day later, it's still hindering him ahead of a Week 7 tilt at Houston. He'll probably have to log a full practice Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Johnson (neck) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Johnson was practicing in a limited capacity in the leadup to the Giants' matchup versus the Saints in Week 6, but he ultimately downgraded to missing practice later in the week before sitting out that contest. He'll likely have to participate fully in practice Thursday or Friday to dodge taking an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Johnson (neck) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: A neck injury limited Johnson's practice participation Wednesday and Thursday, but he was a DNP for Friday's session before being subsequently ruled out for Sunday's contest. In his absence, Chris Manhertz and Thomas Fidone are candidates to step into the TE2 role behind Isaiah Likely. Johnson's next chance to play is Week 7 against the Texans on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: Johnson (neck) was listed as a limited practice participant on Wednesday's injury report, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Johnson caught two of three passes for 35 yards during the Giants' 27-27 tie against the Commanders in Week 5, but he may have tweaked his neck at some point during the game. He would avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest against the Saints if he can log a full practice in one of the next two days.

headline: Johnson caught his lone target for an 11-yard touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Cardinals.
story: Johnson caught the third of Jameis Winston's three touchdowns, scoring from 11 yards out late in the third quarter to give the G-Men a 27-24 lead. Working more as a blocker alongside Isaiah Likely, Johnson has just two catches for 20 yards and a touchdown on six targets this season.

headline: Johnson played 16 of the Giants' 58 offensive snaps but did not haul in any of his four targets during Monday's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
story: All four of Johnson's targets came in the first half, three of which were in the opening quarter. The third-year tight end failed to record a catch, but he did log a tackle on Trent McDuffie after the latter intercepted Jameis Winston midway through the second quarter. Johnson is firmly behind Isaiah Likely on the depth chart, though all of the Giants pass catchers figure to see their production dip with Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart, the latter of whom could miss the rest of the season due to a knee injury.

headline: Johnson caught his only target for nine yards in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Cowboys.
story: Johnson operated as a clear second-fiddle to Isaiah Likely at tight end in Week 1, with the latter reeling in all eight of his targets for 78 yards and two scores in the game. Johnson was on the field for only 32 of the team's 69 offensive snaps, and as long as Likely is available, he won't have much fantasy appeal this season.

headline: Johnson (shoulder) was a full practice participant Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Johnson is coming off a 2025 regular season in which he posted a 45-528-5 line on 74 targets in 15 games, but the arrival of TE Isaiah Likely via free agency has provided the former with some competition at the position ahead of his third pro campaign. With the shoulder injury he picked up in an Aug. 24 practice behind Johnson, he'll focus on being a regular part of the Giants offense in Sunday's Week 1 matchup with the Cowboys.

headline: Skattebo (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: The Giants are coming off of their bye and preparing for the Eagles, and Skattebo was not available to practice as the week got underway. Skattebo tweaked his hamstring on his last carry of the game against the Texans in Week 7. His status in practice the remainder of the week will be crucial given the Giants' shorthandedness in the backfield. Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers are the healthy options at RB beyond Skattebo.

headline: Skattebo (hamstring) didn't take part in Wednesday's practice and instead was seen working with a trainer on the side, Jordan Raanan of ESPN reports.
story: Skattebo tweaked his hamstring on his final carry during a Week 7 win at Houston, but even with the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he's kicking off Week 9 prep with a DNP. Head coach John Harbaugh told Raanan on Monday that Skattebo may be a game-time decision for Sunday's contest at Philadelphia, but he likely will need to mix into drills Thursday and/or Friday to put himself at least in that position. At the moment, Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers are the Giants' healthy backfield options.

headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said that Skattebo (hamstring) is day-to-day and could end up being a game-time decision for Sunday's tilt with the Eagles, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
story: After tweaking his hamstring late in the Giants' Week 7 overtime win over Houston, Skattebo was seen working off to the side Monday during an unofficial practice coming out of a bye week. Skattebo will still have three more opportunities to log on-field reps in Week 9, and the Giants should have a better idea about his status for Sunday's game based on what he's able to do in those sessions. Devin Singletary would be the next man up in the New York backfield if Skattebo is unable to play or is limited against the Eagles.

headline: Skattebo (hamstring) was spotted working out off to the side during the Giants' unofficial practice session Monday, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
story: Skattebo tweaked his hamstring at the end of a 42-yard run in overtime during the Giants' Week 7 win over the Texans, capping off a season-best performance during which he accounted for 121 yards and a touchdown on 18 touches. Though a well-timed Week 8 bye gave Skattebo additional time to recover, he may not be back to 100 percent as the Giants begin prepping for Sunday's game against the Eagles. The Giants will release their first official Week 9 injury report Wednesday, when it will be known whether Skattebo is healthy enough to practice fully or if he's operating with limitations.

headline: What to make of the Giants' backfield situation
story: What to make of the Giants' backfield situation

headline: Skattebo is expected to "OK" after tweaking his hamstring on a 42-yard run in overtime during Sunday's 27-21 win over the Texans, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Skattebo's explosive run put the Giants within field-goal range before he was subbed out for Devin Singletary, who ran up the middle for a 30-yard score to seal the win on the very next play. Though he told Dan Graziano of ESPN.com after the game that he "felt something" in his hamstring that prompted him to slide down at the end of his run rather than being tackled to the ground, Skattebo doesn't sound like he'll require an MRI and should be ready to play in the Giants' next game Nov. 8 versus the Eagles following a Week 8 bye. After being limited to just six snaps in a Week 6 loss to the Saints following a string of poor outings to begin the campaign, Skattebo stepped back into a lead role out of the backfield in Sunday's victory and delivered his best performance of the season, finishing with 121 total yards and a touchdown on 18 touches.

headline: Skattebo told Dan Graziano of ESPN after Sunday's 27-21 overtime win at Houston that he "felt something in his hamstring" during his final carry of the game.
story: One week removed from not receiving a touch while playing six offensive snaps in a loss to the Saints, Skattebo was back in the saddle in the Giants backfield this Sunday, turning 17 rushes into 124 yards and one touchdown and gathering in his only target for minus-3 yards. Meanwhile, fellow RBs Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) combined for 15 touches in Week 7. Both Skattebo and Tracy emerged from this contest with health concerns, but with a Week 8 bye on tap for New York, both players will have time to rest up for the team's next game Sunday, Nov. 8, in Philadelphia.

headline: Skattebo is expected to resume his role as the Giants' lead running back in Sunday's game at Houston, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Skattebo ranked fourth in offensive snaps (six of 77) among Giants running backs behind Devin Singletary (31), Tyrone Tracy (29) and Najee Harris (11) last Sunday against the Saints, failing to log a touch in the process. The team has since released Harris, and Skattebo's brief benching appears to be over. It's unclear who among Skattebo, Singletary and Tracy will get the start this Sunday, but the former did average 18.2 touches per game through the first five weeks of the campaign.

headline: Head coach John Harbaugh said Friday that Skattebo had a "good week" of practice and that the second-year running back should be back in the mix for backfield touches against the Texans on Sunday, Jordan Ranaan of ESPN.com reports.
story: Skattebo didn't log a single carry during the Giants' 34-27 loss to the Saints in Week 6, spending most of the game on the bench. That lack of production stemmed from his critical fumble during overtime against the Commanders in Week 5, but following the release of Najee Harris on Tuesday, Ranaan indicates that Skattebo is expected to reclaim a key role in the Giants' backfield this weekend alongside Tyrone Tracy, with Devin Singletary also in line for work.

headline: Skattebo played only six snaps and got zero carries or targets in the Giants' 34-27 loss to the Saints on Sunday.
story: One week after losing a key fumble in a 27-27 tie to the Commanders, Skattebo was removed from his starting job as the Giants backfield devolved into a four-man committee. Tyrone Tracy was the team's most productive back, scoring one rushing and one receiving touchdown but managing just 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches, while Devin Singletary had 33 yards on five touches and Najee Harris eked out just two rushing yards on four carries. With no one really stepping up in his place, Skattebo could return to a more significant role in Week 7 against the Texans, but it will be hard to trust any New York running back in fantasy lineups until one emerges from the pack.

headline: Skattebo had a "pretty even split in reps" this week with fellow running back Najee Harris and could be in store for fewer snaps and touches than usual in Sunday's game against the Saints, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
story: Coming off a significant ankle injury that cut short his rookie season, Skattebo has handled a lead role out of the New York backfield through the first five games, playing no fewer than 57 percent of snaps on any occasion while averaging 18.2 touches per contest. The second-year back hasn't shown the same burst he displayed in 2025, however, averaging just 3.6 yards per carry and 7.9 yards per reception while finding the end zone only once. Perhaps more troublingly, Skattebo has struggled with ball security, fumbling four times and losing one. As a result of Skattebo's poor form to begin the season, the Giants may be compelled to lighten his workload Sunday and open up more opportunities for Harris compared to previous weeks.

headline: Skattebo rushed 13 times for 59 yards and caught two of three targets for 12 yards in Sunday's 27-27 tie against the Commanders. He also lost a fumble.
story: After a quiet performance in regulation, Skattebo saved his best and worst moments for overtime. He racked up 40 of his 71 scrimmage yards in OT, but Skattebo fumbled on Washington's 24-yard line as the Giants were in range for a potential game-winning field-goal attempt. That mistake was matched by a clock-management error on the other end, which prevented the Commanders from attempting a game-winning field goal of their own prior to the end of OT. Skattebo will be motivated to atone for his fumble in Week 6 against the Saints' leaky run defense.

headline: Skattebo (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Washington, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Skattebo was limited at practice Wednesday and Thursday due to a shoulder injury, which he touched on Friday when he told Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com that he dealt with a "little muscle tightness." With his status now not in question for Week 5, Skattebo will continue to operate as the Giants' lead runner, as he's turned his 76 touches into 302 yards from scrimmage and one TD in four contests this season.

headline: Skattebo (shoulder) was listed as a limited participant at practice Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Skattebo has opened Week 5 prep with consecutive limited sessions. The top backfield option for the Giants will have one more opportunity Friday to upgrade to full participation as he looks to avoid carrying an injury designation into a game for the first time this season.

headline: Skattebo was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a shoulder injury, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Skattebo has yet to hit 100 rushing yards in a game this season and currently is sitting on 302 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD on 76 touches through four contests. As the Giants kick off prep for a Week 5 road matchup with the Commanders, he's dealing with a health concern and likely will need to practice fully Thursday or Friday in order to avoid a designation ahead of the weekend.

headline: Skattebo carried the ball 18 times for 58 yards and caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Cardinals.
story: The second-year back failed to top 60 rushing yards for a third straight game, but at least in Week 3 he was able to add a 3-40-0 line through the air. Skattebo hasn't gotten into the end zone since the Giants' opener, and through four contests he has 302 scrimmage yards while averaging a disappointing 3.5 yards per carry. He'll try to get going on the ground in a Week 5 road clash with the Commanders.

headline: Skattebo carried the ball 20 times for 60 yards and caught three of four targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans.
story: With Jameis Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart (knee), the Giants leaned a little more heavily on their backfield and Skattebo saw a season high in touches while hitting for 100-plus scrimmage yards for the first time in 2026. The second-year back's longest play came on a 30-yard toss in the first quarter, as he made himself available downfield to bail out a scrambling Winston. Through three games, Skattebo is showing no ill effects from the ankle injury that ended his rookie campaign early, and he's collected 177 rushing yards and a TD on 50 carries while adding a 7-59-0 line on eight targets. He figures to see a big workload again in Week 4 at home against the Cardinals.

headline: Skattebo rushed 12 times for 36 yards and brought in all four targets for 19 yards in the Giants' 28-6 loss to the Rams on Monday night. He also committed a fumble recovered by New York.
story: Jaxson Dart's first-half exit due to a knee injury naturally put a damper on the Giants offense as a whole, and Skattebo unsurprisingly faced more stringent fronts than he otherwise would have had Dart been in the game. Skattebo did have a solid passing game role as New York trailed throughout, but with Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reporting Dart has been diagnosed with an MCL sprain, it's possible the second-year back may play at least Sunday's Week 3 home matchup against the Titans without his talented teammate.

headline: Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown but wasn't targeted in the passing game during Sunday's 28-20 win over the Cowboys.
story: Skattebo opened the scoring with a three-yard touchdown run to cap the Giants' first possession of the season. The 2025 fourth-round pick looked spry in his return from a season-ending ankle fracture suffered in Week 8 of his rookie campaign. He led the team in both rushing attempts and rushing yards Sunday while Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy combined for just 30 rushing yards on eight carries, though Singletary got all four targets among Giants running backs and scored a fourth-quarter receiving touchdown. Skattebo should continue to spearhead the Giants' rushing attack in Week 2 against the Rams on Monday Night Football.

headline: Thomas (groin) does not have an injury designation against the Texans on Sunday.
story: Thomas ended Week 7 prep with back-to-back limited practices, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He's been working through a groin injury the last few weeks but hasn't missed a game this season.

headline: Thomas (groin) was a limited participant at the Giants' practice Thursday.
story: Thomas has been dealing with a groin injury for a series of weeks, but he has been able to play through it. The offensive lineman was a non-participant at practice Wednesday, but his ability to return to the field Thursday suggests that he will be good to go for Week 7 versus the Texans.

headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh confirmed after Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints that Thomas didn't sustain a concussion during the contest, Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post reports.
story: Thomas exited Sunday's contest in the fourth quarter for a concussion check but was able to pass all testing. However, Thomas didn't re-enter the contest in what Harbaugh called a "coach's decision," with the Giants instead using rookie J.C. Davis at left tackle down the stretch. Thomas had been slowed by a groin injury leading up to the game, so that may have been a factor in Harbaugh's decision to keep him on the sideline for the rest of the contest. The 27-year-old should be ready to start in next Sunday's game at Houston.

headline: Thomas (head) is being evaluated for a potential concussion and is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Saints, Art Stapleton of The Bergen Record reports.
story: Thomas exited the fourth quarter of Sunday's game with an apparent head injury. The left tackle is being evaluated by one of the NFL's independent neurologists. If Thomas is deemed to have suffered a concussion, he will be ruled out for the remainder of the game.

headline: Thomas (groin) is active for Sunday's game against the Saints, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
story: Thomas is set to play through a groin injury as he has for most of the 2026 regular season. The left tackle will protect starting quarterback Jameis Winston as the Giants attempt to make a home stand against the Saints.

headline: Thomas (groin), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints, is expected to play, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Thomas turned in just one limited practice this week while managing the groin issue, but he looks set to play through the injury Sunday. Official word on the left tackle's status will arrive when the Giants post their inactive list 90 minutes prior to the 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Thomas (groin) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: Thomas has dealt with ankle and groin injuries all season to this point but has yet to miss a single offensive snap through five contests. He didn't carry an injury designation into any of the previous three games, so the questionable tag this time is new. Fellow starting tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) is also listed questionable for Week 6.

headline: Thomas (groin) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Commanders.
story: Thomas was a DNP during Wednesday's practice but upgraded to a limited participant Thursday and a full participant Friday. The starting left tackle avoided any injury designation ahead of Sunday's contest and is all set to suit up to protect Jameis Winston as the Giants face the Commanders.

headline: Thomas (groin) was a limited participant in practice Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Thomas has been dealing with a groin issue for the past few weeks, but he's yet to miss an offensive snap this season. Despite beginning Week 5 as a DNP and logging a limited session Thursday, it seems likely the standout left tackle will be able to suit up Sunday against the Commanders.

headline: Thomas (groin) does not carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Thomas faded an injury tag despite logging a DNP-DNP-LP practice log, which was part of the maintenance plan set up by the Giants' medical staff, per Dan Duggan of The Athletic. Thomas will start at left tackle Sunday, with J.C. Davis and Marcus Mbow providing depth on the offensive line.

headline: Thomas (groin) did not participate at the Giants' practice Thursday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
story: Thomas has missed back-to-back practices to open the week as he continues to nurse a groin injury. The offensive lineman was able to play through the injury during the team's win over Tennessee in Week 3, and he'll look to do the same Sunday versus Arizona.

headline: Thomas (groin) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Thomas was limited in Wednesday's practice before logging a DNP on Thursday. The left tackle upgraded to a limited participant once again Friday, managing to avoid any injury designation for Sunday's contest. Thomas will be protecting Jameis Winston's blind side due to the injury to starting quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee).

headline: Thomas (groin) did not practice Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Thomas sustained a groin injury during the Giants' 28-6 loss to the Rams on Monday, and he's opened Week 3 prep with an LP-DNP practice log. His practice participation Friday and the subsequent injury designation announced by the Giants will provide clarity on Thomas' status for Sunday's home game against the Titans. J.C. Davis and Marcus Mbow figure to be the top candidates to start at left tackle if Thomas is not cleared to play against Tennessee.

headline: Thomas (groin) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice,  Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Thomas exited Monday's game in the fourth quarter with a groin injury. The adductor issue he suffered is not considered a serious injury, and the left tackle could play in Sunday's game against the Titans, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Thomas will probably spend the week as a limited practice participant before likely suiting up for Sunday's game to play through the injury.

headline: Thomas (groin) is questionable to return to Monday's game against the Rams, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Thomas sustained a groin injury in the fourth quarter of Monday's contest. The Giants were already down by three scores at the time of Thomas' exit, so it is unlikely the left tackle will return to the contest regardless of the verdict on his ability to play.

headline: Thomas (ankle) does not have any injury designation ahead of Monday's game against the Rams.
story: Thomas logged limited participation in practice throughout Week 2. The left tackle appears to have managed his ankle injury well enough to avoid any injury designation heading into Monday's game. Both Thomas and Francis Mauigoa are set to suit up and complete the Giants' starting offensive line for the contest.

headline: Thomas was a limited participant in Friday's practice due to an ankle injury, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Thomas has opened the week with back-to-back limited practices due to an ankle injury that he may have picked up during the Giants' Week 1 win over the Cowboys. A full practice Saturday would likely be enough for the seventh-year pro to avoid an injury designation for Monday's game against the Rams.

headline: Harrison was signed to the Giants' active roster Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
story: Harrison will officially join the active roster ahead of the team's Week 6 matchup with New Orleans. Harrison has been elevated from the practice squad to appear in three games with New York this season, recording two total tackles and a fumble recovery over 56 snaps with the special-teams unit.

headline: The Giants signed Jones to the active roster from their practice squad Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
story: Jones will slot in as the team's fifth-string receiver following the release of Odell Beckham earlier in the day. Jones is also expected to serve as the backup punt returner behind Braxton Berrios.

headline: Hood (concussion) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
story: Hood wasn't able to practice at full speed Wednesday due to the concussion that knocked him out of the Giants' game versus the Saints in Week 6 early, but it didn't hold him back Thursday. He'll still have to clear league concussion protocol to be eligible to suit up in Week 7 at Houston, so there's no guarantee yet that he'll be available come Sunday.

headline: Hood (concussion) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: Hood has not cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in time to suit up for Sunday's game against the Saints. The Giants' reserve cornerback remains unable to participate in full-contact practices and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full practice participation in Week 7.

headline: Hood (concussion) is considered day-to-day ahead of the Giants' matchup with the Saints in Week 6, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
story: Hood suffered a concussion during Sunday's 27-27 tie against the Commanders, and he'll have to clear concussion protocol in order to be available for Week 6. If he is unavailable versus New Orleans, Nic Jones may work as one of New York's starting cornerbacks.

headline: Hood (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Commanders, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Hood has entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not be able to participate in full-contact practices or games until he has been cleared by an independent neurologist. Nic Jones will finish Sunday's contest at outside cornerback opposite Greg Newsome.

headline: Hood is being evaluated for a concussion and is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Commanders, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
story: Hood exited the second half of Sunday's divisional contest with a head injury. If the cornerback is deemed to have suffered a concussion, his day will be over and he will be placed in the NFL's five-step concussion protocol.

headline: Hood (quadriceps) was not listed on the Giants' injury report Wednesday.
story: Hood sustained a quadriceps injury during a training camp practice in mid-August. It appears the rookie second-rounder has recovered from the injury based on Wednesday's report, putting him on track to make his NFL regular-season debut Sunday against the Cowboys. He figures to operate in a rotational role in the secondary, with most of his reps coming on special teams.

headline: Carter (calf) is active for Sunday's game against the Saints, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
story: Carter was absent for the first two practices of Week 6 prep before upgrading to a limited participant in Friday's session. The strongside linebacker looked great in practice and has recovered in time to suit up for Sunday's game against the Saints.

headline: Carter (calf), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints, is expected to play, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Carter sat out the Giants' first two Week 6 practices but "looked explosive" while he was on the field as a limited participant for Friday's session, per Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com. The Giants apparently agree with Raanan's assessment, though Carter won't be officially cleared to play until the team releases its inactive list 90 minutes prior to Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff. Through New York's first five games, Carter has accrued 2.0 sacks among his 14 tackles while also forcing a fumble.

headline: Carter (calf) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: Carter upgraded to limited participation in Friday's practice after missing the earlier sessions of Week 6 prep. He'll try to suit up Sunday and build upon the 2.0 sacks he's logged through five games.

headline: Carter (calf) did not practice Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Carter didn't practice for the second consecutive day. The 23-year-old will need to at least practice in a limited capacity Friday if he hopes to avoid an injury designation for the Week 6 meeting with the Saints.

headline: Carter (calf) was listed as a DNP on Wednesday's injury report, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Carter likely injured his calf during the Giants' Week 5 tie with the Commanders, when he logged five tackles (two solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one forced fumble. Head coach John Harbaugh told reporters before Wednesday's session that Carter was "doing well," per Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com, but the second-year pro's practice participation over the next two days will provide clarity on his status heading into Sunday's contest against the Saints.

headline: Singletary is expected to handle a bigger role out of the Giants' backfield after Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
story: The Giants have their bye in Week 8, but Tracy will be required to miss at least four games with his injury, so it appears Singletary and Cam Skattebo (hamstring) will form the backfield duo with Tracy sidelined and Najee Harris recently released. Singletary scored the game-winning touchdown in overtime last Sunday against the Texans, finishing with 55 total yards and the touchdown on eight touches. If Skattebo is healthy, he figures to operate as the lead back, but Singletary showed enough to warrant 6-to-10 touches with upside for more. He's worth picking up in most fantasy leagues.

headline: What to make of the Giants' backfield situation
story: What to make of the Giants' backfield situation

headline: Singletary carried the ball five times for 41 yards and a touchdown and caught all three of his targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 27-24 overtime win over the Texans.
story: Attrition may have helped solve the Giants' backfield mess, at least in the short term. Tyrone Tracy left the game in the second quarter with a hamstring injury and didn't return, and Cam Skattebo may also have picked up a hamstring strain on his final tote of the day, a 42-yard dash in OT that set up a 30-yard TD run for Singletary that won the game. A well-timed Week 8 bye could allow both RBs to avoid missing any further time, but if either or both are still on the shelf on the other side of the break, Singletary could wind up handling a much bigger role in Week 9 against the Eagles.

headline: Singletary turned four carries into 14 yards and hauled in his lone target for 19 yards during Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints on Sunday.
story: Singletary was back in action Sunday after being a healthy scratch in each of the Giants' three games prior to Week 6. Three of his four carries went for two yards or fewer, although he did log a nine-yard rush and 19-yard catch on back-to-back plays early in the fourth quarter. Singletary's 31 offensive snaps were most among Giants running backs, but the team's backfield situation is a mess, given Cam Skattebo saw the field for only six offensive snaps and did not record a carry. The Giants will hit the road for Week 7 against the Texans on Oct. 25.

headline: Singletary (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Singletary will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive week while the Giants roll with Tyrone Tracy and Najee Harris as the backup options in the backfield behind Cam Skattebo. Singletary's next opportunity to suit up is Week 5 against the Commanders on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Singletary (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Titans, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Singletary had little impact in Week 2, rushing just three times for nine yards amongst a busy backfield. Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy will serve as complementary options behind Cam Skattebo against Tennessee.

headline: Singletary rushed three times for nine yards during Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
story: Singletary took a step back in production after showing off his dual-threat abilities in Week 1 against the Cowboys, failing to garner a target versus Los Angeles.
