Williams and Shepard could see a bit more volume this week, but the offense still figures to run through Wilson, the RBs and the TEs. As for Mitchell, his next chance to play will be Week 5 against Cleveland (Oct. 11).

headline: Mitchell (finger) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Mitchell sat out this past Sunday's loss to the Lions and could be trending toward a second consecutive absence Sunday against the Bears after being unable to practice Wednesday or Thursday. The 2024 second-round pick of the Colts is considered week-to-week by the Jets. He'll have one more chance to practice Friday.

headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Mitchell (finger) won't practice Wednesday and is considered week-to-week, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
story: Mitchell sat out the Jets' 31-24 loss to the Lions in Week 3 due to the finger injury, and his absence to begin Week 4 prep in addition to Glenn classifying him as week-to-week rather than day-to-day suggests that the receiver is trending toward another absence this Sunday versus the Bears. If Mitchell ends up sitting out a second straight game, Isaiah Williams would be in store for another elevated snap count as the Jets' No. 2 wideout behind Garrett Wilson.

headline: Mitchell (finger) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions.
story: Mitchell was listed as questionable for Week 3 after sustaining a finger injury last week, and it turns out he is not ready to take the field Sunday. Mitchell -- who garnered 12 targets last week -- joins fellow pass catchers Omar Cooper (ankle) and Mason Taylor (thumb) on the sidelines, so Kenyon Sadiq and Isaiah Williams figure to see some extra opportunities behind top option Garrett Wilson.

headline: Mitchell (finger) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Detroit.
story: Mitchell was added to the injury report Thursday as a limited participant, and he again was limited at Friday's session while wearing a large wrap over his right hand, per Brian Costello of the New York Post. Mitchell isn't sure-handed even in the best of times, but he's been piling up targets and air yards anyway and now will get a favorable dome matchup with the Lions (if he's able to suit up). If Mitchell doesn't end up playing, the Jets may need a lot of snaps from a practice-squad veteran like Sterling Shepard or Tyler Johnson. Their WR depth wasn't great in the first place and already has been stretched thin with rookie Omar Cooper (ankle) on injured reserve for at least three more weeks.

headline: Mitchell (finger) will be limited in Friday's practice.
story: With Mitchell now limited in back-to-back practices due to the finger issue, it's possible he receives an injury designation for the Week 3 matchup with Detroit. The Jets' final injury report Friday afternoon will reveal Mitchell's status.

headline: Mitchell was a limited participant in Thursday's practice due to a finger injury, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
story: Mitchell wasn't included on the Jets' initial Week 3 injury report released Wednesday, so the finger issue may have been something that popped up during Thursday's session. The Jets haven't revealed whether the injury is anything that will affect Mitchell's availability for Sunday's game in Detroit, but his activity at Friday's practice will bear monitoring nonetheless. Through the first two games of the season, the Jets' No. 2 wideout has reeled in nine of 15 targets for 123 yards.

headline: Mitchell caught six of 12 targets for 63 yards in the Jets' 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers on Sunday.
story: Mitchell's dozen targets easily led the team, as he was the intended receiver on 29.3 percent of Geno Smith's 41 pass attempts. The defense kept Mitchell in front of them, keeping his longest gain to 15 yards after he produced a 40-yard reception in Week 1 against the Titans. Mitchell is playing virtually every snap for the Jets, as he's cemented himself as the team's WR2 alongside Garrett Wilson. Mitchell will be an upside WR3/4 for fantasy in next Sunday's mouthwatering draw against the Lions' depleted secondary.

headline: Mitchell caught all three of his passes for 60 yards during the Jets' 23-10 win over the Titans on Sunday.
story: Mitchell connected with Geno Smith on a 40-yard pass early in the third quarter to set the Jets up in the red zone, leading to a Breece Hall four-yard touchdown run two plays later. Mitchell's catch was the longest play of the game for the Jets, and that deep-threat ability is a big reason why New York acquired him from Indianapolis last November. Mitchell's 46 snaps on offense were second-most among Jets wide receivers behind Garrett Wilson (50), though the former's extended playing time was partially due to an ankle injury that ended Omar Cooper's day early. The Jets will welcome in the Packers for Week 2 on Sept. 20.

headline: Eric Moody: Braelon Allen remains a must-hold player in fantasy
story: Eric Moody: Braelon Allen remains a must-hold player in fantasy

headline: Allen rushed 21 times for 147 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for six yards in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.
story: Allen made a fifth consecutive start in the absence of Breece Hall (quadriceps) and exceeded 100 scrimmage yards for the fourth consecutive game. The 2024 fourth-round pick set a new career high with 147 rushing yards, surpassing Allen's 116 yards on the ground in the Week 5 win over the Browns. Allen scored his third rushing touchdown of the season on a 21-yard run in the third quarter to give the Jets a 30-21 lead, but the Raiders closed the game on a 17-3 run to drop the Jets to 2-6. If Hall's ready to return in Week 9 against the Chiefs, the Jets could opt for a backfield split between Allen and Hall.

headline: Allen is slated to serve as the Jets' starting running back Sunday against the Raiders, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: For a second week in a row, fellow running back Breece Hall (quadriceps) is listed questionable to play, but he was inactive in Week 7, and he's considered unlikely to play again in Week 8, per Rapoport. Assuming Hall is officially ruled out when the Jets release their inactive list 90 minutes prior to the 1 p.m. ET kickoff, Allen should be headed for another heavy workload out of the New York backfield. In the Jets' last four games sans Hall, Allen combined for 83 touches for 421 yards from scrimmage and one rushing touchdown.

headline: Allen (ankle) was a full participant at Thursday's practice.
story: Allen began Week 8 prep as a limited participant at Wednesday's practice, but he shed all limitations Thursday, while Breece Hall (quadriceps) remained limited for a second consecutive practice Thursday. Hall got the majority of backfield touches over Allen when both were healthy to begin the season, but the former hasn't seen game action since Week 3. Allen should be good to go for Sunday's game against the Raiders, but uncertainty lingers regarding Hall's status.

headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Allen will be a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to ankle injury, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
story: Over the past four games, Allen has filled in for Breece Hall (quadriceps) as the Jets' lead back, but both players will kick off Week 8 prep with limitations in practice. In Allen's case, he may just be a bit banged up after averaging 20.8 touches per contest in Hall's absence, so as long as doesn't take any steps back in terms of practice activity as the week rolls along, Allen should be on track to play Sunday versus the Raiders. The extent of Allen's role will depend on the availability of Hall, who could also suit up this weekend if he responds well to practicing over the next three days.

headline: Allen rushed 17 times for 104 yards and caught six of seven targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins.
story: Allen worked as the lead back for a fourth consecutive game, as Breece Hall (quadriceps) was ultimately inactive after being listed as questionable heading into the game. The 235-pound Allen continued to struggle in short yardage, getting stuffed on a goal-line attempt in the fourth quarter as the Jets were denied a game-tying touchdown and instead settled for a field goal to cut the deficit to four points with 8:57 remaining. Allen has exceeded 100 rushing yards twice during Hall's absence but has just one touchdown over that span and two touchdowns this season. Hall worked ahead of Allen prior to getting hurt, but they may split the backfield workload more evenly if Hall's cleared to return against the Raiders in Week 8.

headline: Allen will remain the Jets' No. 1 back for Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Dolphins, as Breece Hall has been declared inactive for the contest.
story: With Hall unavailable for a fourth straight game Sunday, Allen will have a chance to build on the averages of 18.3 rush attempts, 84.3 rushing yards, 1.7 receptions and 11.3 receiving yards he's generated in the lead role over his teammate's first three absences. Despite their winless record, the Dolphins have been respectable defending the run, allowing 4.0 yards per carry to running backs, albeit while also conceding a 25-197-5 receiving line to the position.

headline: Allen's workload and role Sunday against Miami is unclear given that Breece Hall (quadriceps) is officially questionable to play, per Amanda Vogt of the Jets' official site.
story: With Hall sidelined the past three weeks, Allen has stepped up to lead New York's backfield. He's performed well in that role, averaging 84.3 rush yards per game and 4.6 yards per carry, albeit with only one touchdown. Hall will likely step back into the starting role if he's able to suit up Sunday, though Allen is expected to get a fair amount of work as well. Even if Hall does return to action, both ball carriers could find success against a Dolphins defense that has given up the second-most fantasy points per game (23.7) to running backs.

headline: Allen rushed 17 times for 78 yards and brought in both targets for 26 yards in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Allen served as the Jets' clear lead back during Breece Hall's second straight absence due to a quadriceps injury, and the former put together a productive effort that featured a new season high in receiving yards. Allen has acquitted himself very well as the No. 1 option over the last two games, posting 194 rushing yards and a touchdown alongside three receptions and the 26 receiving yards he accrued Sunday. If Hall remains sidelined in Week 7, Allen will get a crack at a beatable Dolphins defense at home.

headline: Allen will once again operate as the Jets' primary running back for Sunday's game against the Patriots due to the absence of Breece Hall (quadriceps).
story: Allen had a huge part in the Jets' Week 5 win over the Browns, totaling 116 yards and a touchdown over 24 rushes. The running back is set to reprise his role as one of the team's foremost offensive weapons against the Patriots on Sunday as Breece Hall (quadriceps) continues to recover.

headline: Allen rushed 24 times for 116 yards and a touchdown while catching one of four targets for no gain in Sunday's 17-12 win over the Browns.
story: Allen ran in the go-ahead 22-yard touchdown with 3:01 remaining, and the Jets' defense held twice after that to secure the team's second win of the season. The 2024 fourth-round pick handled lead-back duties for the second consecutive game in the absence of Breece Hall (quadriceps), notching 25 touches to Isaiah Davis' three. After reaching 100 rushing yards in a game for the first time in his career, Allen would be in line for another substantial workload in Week 6 against the Patriots if Hall remains sidelined.

headline: Allen will once again operate as the Jets' top running back for Sunday's game against the Browns due to the absence of Breece Hall (quadriceps).
story: Hall will miss a second consecutive game due to a quadriceps injury, and the star running back has yet to be cleared to return to practice. As such, Allen will be the Jets' RB1 versus Cleveland, with Isaiah Davis and Kene Nwangwu providing backfield depth. Allen was the starter for the Jets' Week 4 loss to the Bears, when he turned 14 carries into 59 yards and added two catches (on as many targets) for eight yards.

headline: Allen rushed 14 times for 59 yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards in Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
story: Allen accounted for all 14 of the Jets' rushing attempts in the absence of Breece Hall (quadriceps), who is considered week-to-week. The Bears dominated time of possession as Geno Smith completed just eight passes in the loss. If Hall isn't ready to return in Week 5 against the Browns, Allen would retain the lead role in the backfield for the Jets.

headline: Allen and Isaiah Davis will man the Jets backfield for as long as Breece Hall (thigh) is potentially sidelined, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
story: Hall exited in the fourth quarter of Sunday's loss at Detroit due to a thigh injury, and afterward he relayed that he "felt something" while running, per Brian Costello of the New York Post. Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter of ESPN then reported Monday that Hall is considered week-to-week. While Hall hasn't outright been ruled out for Week 4 or beyond, Allen currently ranks second on the team in carries with 19, which have gone for 61 yards, while Davis hasn't logged an offensive snap through three contests to begin the season. As a result, Allen is the better bet to take advantage of an absent Hall, if that comes to pass.

headline: Allen rushed five times for seven yards and a touchdown while catching his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers.
story: Allen scored a touchdown in the second quarter of Sunday's game on a five-yard rush. The running back played 23 offensive snaps in the contest, seeing supplemental volume behind No. 1 running back Breece Hall's 47 snaps and 16 carries.

headline: Allen rushed 10 times for 40 yards in the Jets' 23-10 win over the Titans on Sunday.
story: Allen failed to secure his lone target in the pass game. With Breece Hall past his groin issue, he operated as the clear RB1 in a workhorse role, rushing 22 times for 102 yards and one touchdown while adding two catches for 16 yards. Hall out-snapped Allen 39 to 27, cementing the former as an RB2 with RB1 upside for fantasy, especially if the Jets can get into positive game scripts like they had in Tennessee on Sunday. Allen is an upper-tier fantasy bench stash at the position.

headline: Allen is listed second on the Jets' unofficial depth chart behind Breece Hall.
story: Allen worked with the starters for most of the preseason while Hall was sidelined by a groin injury. Hall practiced without limitations Wednesday, as did Isaiah Davis (knee), who is listed third on the team's unofficial depth chart. Allen is listed at 235 pounds and has reportedly bulked up to around 250. The 2024 fourth-round pick's large frame could help Allen command valuable goal-line and short-yardage work even while Hall is healthy.

headline: Parham (knee) is active for Sunday's game against Las Vegas.
story: Parham will be back in action for the first time since Week 3, when he sustained a knee injury in a loss to the Lions. Though he was listed as questionable heading into Sunday, Parham was cleared to play after logging a pair of limited practices and a full session during the week. He should step back in as the Jets' starting left guard, sending Jordan Meredith back to the bench.

headline: Parham (knee) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Parham will be sidelined for a fourth consecutive game due to a lingering knee injury. The good news for the 2022 third-rounder is that he was able to practice during Week 7 prep, so he's progressing in his recovery and could return for Week 8 against the Raiders on Nov. 1. Jordan Meredith will continue to start at left guard in Parham's absence.

headline: Parham (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Wednesday was Parham's first practice since sustaining a knee injury in Week 3 against the Lions, which prevented him from playing in each of the Jets' three following games. He'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If Parham is cleared to return, then he would likely reclaim his starting job at left guard from Jordan Meredith.

headline: Parham (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Patriots, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
story: Parham will miss a third consecutive game due to a knee injury. His next chance to play is Week 7 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Oct. 25, although the fifth-year pro has yet to practice since sustaining his injury. Jordan Meredith will continue to start at left guard in Parham's absence.

headline: Coach Aaron Glenn said Wednesday that Parham (knee) is still week-to-week as the Jets start preparing for Week 6, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
story: Parham has been sidelined for the Jets' last two games with the knee injury he suffered in Week 3 at Detroit, and he appears to be in danger of missing a third straight contest. His activity at practice during the week will be worth monitoring ahead of Sunday's game at New England, but his coach's words don't suggest a ton of optimism he'll be able to play against the division rival.

headline: Parham (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
story: A knee injury prevented Parham from practicing all week. He'll miss a second game in a row as a result of his injury, and his next chance to play is Week 6 against the Patriots on Sunday, Oct. 18. Jordan Meredith figures to once again start at left guard in Parham's absence.

headline: Coach Aaron Glenn said Wednesday that Parham is still week-to-week as he nurses a knee injury, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
story: Parham sat out Sunday's game at Chicago with the knee injury he picked up in Week 3 at Detroit, and it's still bothering him as the Jets begin preparing for Week 5. Barring an unexpected development, he's trending toward missing Sunday's contest versus the Browns.

headline: Parham (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bears, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
story: Parham was unable to finish the Jets' Week 3 loss to the Lions after sustaining a knee injury. He could not participate in any of the Jets' three practice sessions during Week 4 prep, and in his absence, Jordan Meredith will likely start at left guard against Chicago.

headline: Parham is considered week to week due to a knee injury, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
story: Parham is expected to sit out Sunday's matchup versus the Bears after suffering a knee injury during the Week 3 loss to the Lions. In his absence, Jordan Meredith will likely start at left guard.

headline: Parham (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Lions.
story: Parham was carted off the field after sustaining a knee injury and will not return. Jordan Meredith will take over at left guard for the rest of Sunday's game.

headline: The Jets placed Sweat (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: Sweat was diagnosed with a knee injury during the Jets' Week 7 loss to the Dolphins. The initial diagnosis was week-to-week, and the Jets medical staff has determined that a stint on IR is warranted for the third-year defensive lineman, although he's expected to return this season. Sweat will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can play is Week 12 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 29, although he could be held out until after the Jets' Week 13 bye. Darrell Jackson and Harrison Phillips will both step into more prominent roles on the defensive line in Sweat's absence.

headline: Sweat (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Sweat is considered week-to-week due to a knee injury that he sustained against the Dolphins in Week 7. He was unable to practice during Week 8 prep, and in his absence, the Jets will turn to Jowon Briggs and Darrell Jackson to step into more prominent roles on the interior defensive line. Sweat's next chance to play is Week 9 against the Chiefs on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Sweat (knee) is week-to-week and is unlikely to suit up for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reported Wednesday.
story: Sweat did not participate in Wednesday's practice as he continues to deal with the knee injury he sustained in the Jets' Week 7 loss to the Dolphins. The defensive tackle will likely miss Week 8 against the Raiders and could miss even longer due to the new injury.

headline: Sweat (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Sweat exited during the third quarter with a knee injury. The starting defensive tackle will likely be replaced by a rotation of Darrell Jackson and Jowon Briggs.

headline: Nwangwu was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Nwangwu remained inactive for the Jets' Week 7 loss to the Dolphins despite logging a full practice Friday. The running back has returned to form for Week 8 prep and should be all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the Raiders.

headline: Nwangwu (knee) is inactive against the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Nwangwu drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game after logging a full practice Friday. However, the sixth-year pro has not been cleared by medical staff to play, so Isaiah Williams will operate as the primary returner on both punts and kickoffs. Nwangu's next opportunity to suit up is Week 8 against the Raiders on Nov. 1.

headline: Nwangwu (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Nwangwu started Week 7 prep with consecutive DNPs before upgrading to a full participant in Friday's session. The sudden upgrade to full participation likely means the kick returner and depth running back will be capable of suiting up for the Jets' divisional bout against the Dolphins on Sunday.

headline: Nwangwu (knee) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Nwangwu has now been unable to practice for two straight days because of a knee issue, and his availability for Week 7 is in serious doubt. He'll probably need to get back onto the practice field Friday to have a realistic chance of suiting up Sunday versus the Dolphins.

headline: Nwangwu (knee) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Nwangwu likely picked up his back issue during the six special-teams snaps he played in the Jets' Week 6 loss to the Patriots. It remains unclear how significant the running back's injury is and whether he will be able to suit up for Week 7 against the Dolphins.

headline: Nwangwu (back) was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Head coach Aaron Glenn suggested before Wednesday's session that Nwangwu would be limited in practice, but the running back instead took every rep in the Jets' first Week 4 session. With the back issue seemingly behind him, Nwangwu looks ready to make his 2026 debut Sunday against the Bears. Lead back Breece Hall (quadriceps) is considered week-to-week and will likely sit out Sunday, leaving Nwangwu in line to serve as the Jets' No. 3 back behind Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis.

headline: Nwangwu (back) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
story: Nwangwu has yet to play this season and is miles away from fantasy relevance, even with Breece Hall nursing a quad injury. Nwangwu's contributions come on special teams when healthy.

headline: Nwangwu (back) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Lions.
story: Nwangwu was listed as doubtful for Sunday's contest after Friday's practice. The Jets' kick returner had an outside chance to suit up Sunday despite not logging a single day of practice throughout Week 3 prep. After a Saturday examination, it's been determined that Nwangwu will not be ready for the game, leaving Isaiah Williams as the primary kick and punt returner for the Jets' showdown with the Lions.

headline: Nwangwu (back) is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Lions, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
story: It looks like Nwangwu will miss each of the Jets' first three games of the regular season due to a back injury he picked up in a practice prior to the Jets' Week 1 win over the Titans. He was a DNP in all three practices during Week 3 prep, so a return to practice in at least a limited capacity would be a positive step in Nwangwu's recovery. Isaiah Williams will continue to serve as the Jets' primary returner on kickoffs and punts for as long as Nwangwu is sidelined.

headline: Nwangwu (back) did not participate in practice Thursday.
story: The running back and kick returner did not practice Wednesday either after missing the Jets' Week 2 overtime loss to the Packers. He is not on injured reserve, but he also does not appear to be on track to return for this Sunday's matchup with the Lions. Nwangwu has yet to suit up for a regular-season game in 2026.

headline: Nwangwu (back) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Nwangwu did not practice at all leading up to Week 2 and missed the Jets' overtime loss to the Packers on Sunday. The running back and kick returner has missed every practice and game since sustaining a back injury on Sept. 11. Nwangwu was not placed on IR after the injury, so it is reasonable to expect the 28-year-old to return to the field by Week 4, even if he cannot increase his practice participation soon enough to play in the team's Week 3 contest against the Lions.

headline: Nwangwu (back) won't play in Sunday's game against the Packers, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
story: Nwangwu will miss a second consecutive game Sunday, and he's considered week-to-week. With Nwangwu sidelined again in Week 2, Isaiah Williams will presumably handle most of the return duties versus Green Bay.

headline: Nwangwu (back) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: The 2021 fourth-rounder is considered week-to-week due to a back injury, so his absence from Wednesday's practice isn't a surprise. Nwangwu will have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity, which would give him a chance to return for Sunday's home game against the Packers.

headline: Nwangwu (back) is considered week-to-week, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
story: Nwangwu didn't play in Sunday's 23-10 win over the Titans. It appears he won't suit up versus Green Bay, though it's anyone's guess when he will get back on the field. The 2021 No. 119 overall pick most recently appeared in 12 regular-season games for the Jets during the 2025 campaign, totaling 13 carries for 49 yards.

headline: Nwangwu (back) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Nwangwu was designated as doubtful after Friday's practice, so the eventual ruling that he will not suit up for Sunday's contest is not surprising. The depth running back and primary kick returner for the team continues to deal with a back injury he likely suffered during a practice session earlier in the week. With Nwangwu out, wide receiver Isaiah Williams will likely add kick return duties alongside his punt return duties in Sunday's game.

headline: Nwangwu (back) is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Titans, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
story: Nwangwu wasn't listed on the Jets' injury report until Friday as a DNP, indicating that he may have tweaked his back in a practice session. He wasn't expected to see much playing time on offense given that he's behind Breece Hall, Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis on the depth chart. However, if Nwangwu is indeed ruled out for Week 1, then Isaiah Williams figures to operate at the Jets' top returner, with Davis also in the mix.

headline: Davis finished Sunday's Week 7 loss to Miami with three tackles (two solo) and one defensed pass.
story: Davis' tackle tally was his lowest of the campaign, but he did record his first effort of multiple defensed passes. The durable linebacker has played every defensive snap for the Jets so far this season. With 46 stops through seven games, Davis is on pace for a 10th consecutive 100-tackle campaign.

headline: Davis ended with 10 total tackles (five solo) and 1.0 sacks in Sunday's 23-12 loss to Chicago.
story: Davis has been on a roll of late, amassing 10 total tackles and 1.0 sacks in each of his last two games. The 37-year-old veteran has shown no signs of slowing down, and he has a favorable opportunity on the horizon in Week 5 against the Browns, a team that surrendered nearly 3.0 sacks per game in the first month of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Davis recorded 10 tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Sunday's 31-24 loss at Detroit.
story: Davis again led Jets linebackers in snaps in Week 3, but it was his first time registering a double-digit tackle total since Week 12 of the 2025 season. With that said, he remains solidly on the IDP radar in most formats going into a Week 4 matchup against a run-first Chicago offense.

headline: Davis posted four tackles (three solo) during the Jets' 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers on Sunday.
story: Davis was one of six Jets players to play all 59 defensive snaps during Sunday's OT loss. The veteran linebacker is up to 12 total tackles through two games and on pace to crack 100 tackles for a 10th straight year and the 13th time in his NFL career. He should stay busy Week 3 against the Lions on Sunday.

headline: Davis made eight tackles (four solo) and had one pass defensed over 50 defensive snaps in Sunday's 23-10 win over the Titans.
story: Davis was on the field for every Jets defensive snap in the contest. The linebacker also led the team in tackles in his first game as a Jet. Davis signed a two-year, $22 million contract with the team in March.

headline: Sherwood totaled eight tackles (four solo) and two defensed passes Sunday in a loss to Miami.
story: Of Sherwood's eight stops, two went for a loss. He also notched multiple defensed passes for the first time this season. Sherwood has been quite disruptive so far in 2026, tallying 54 tackles, four defensed passes, two forced fumbles and a recovered fumble through seven games.

headline: Sherwood recorded 11 tackles (six solo), a forced fumble and a fumble recovery during Sunday's 26-19 loss at New England.
story: Sherwood made a huge hustle play on a third down early in the fourth quarter, punching the ball out of the arms of DeMario Douglas after chasing him down 39 yards beyond the line of scrimmage. He also recovered a fumble in the third quarter, and both turnovers set up Jets field goals. He profiles as a solid IDP option in many formats heading into a Week 7 tilt versus the Dolphins.

headline: Sherwood finished with 13 total tackles (five solo) and one forced fumble in Sunday's 23-12 loss to Chicago.
story: Sherwood finished behind Dane Belton (14) and Minkah Fitzpatrick (16) for the game high in total tackles. He also came up big in the third quarter by forcing a fumble on D'Andre Swift, which ultimately resulted in a 30-yard field goal from Jason Sanders.

headline: Sherwood posted six tackles (three solo) and a pass defense during the Jets' 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers on Sunday.
story: Sherwood was working through a minor knee issue during Week 2 prep, but he managed to play every single defensive snap during Sunday's OT loss and finished tied with Dane Belton for the most tackles on the Jets. Sherwood is up to 10 total tackles through two games, and he's currently behind pace to reach the 100-tackle mark for a third consecutive year. He'll have his hands full in the Jets' Week 3 road tilt against the Lions on Sunday.

headline: Sherwood (knee) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
story: Sherwood popped up on the Jets' injury report Wednesday with a knee issue, but it appears he's back on track to suit up in Week 2. He projects to start at linebacker next to veteran Demario Davis on Sunday versus the Packers.

headline: Sherwood was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a knee injury.
story: Sherwood may have tweaked his knee during the Jets' 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1, when he played 45 defensive snaps and finished with four tackles (two solo). The sixth-year pro will have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation for Sunday's home game against the Packers.

headline: Sherwood made four tackles (two solo) in Sunday's 23-10 win over the Titans.
story: The starting middle linebacker played 45 defensive snaps, good for 90 percent of the Jets' total defensive plays. Sherwood also played two special teams snaps, filling in whenever needed.

headline: Campbell (hamstring/quadriceps) did not participate at the Eagles' practice Wednesday.
story: Campbell was unable to play in the team's Week 8 loss to the Commanders while nursing hamstring and quadriceps injuries, and he appears to still be dealing with the injuries ahead of Week 9. The linebacker will have two more opportunities to return to practice prior to Sunday's matchup with the Giants.

headline: Campbell (hamstring/quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Washington.
story: Campbell was held out of practice all week due to hamstring and quad injuries, so Jeremiah Trotter figures to start alongside Zack Baun at inside linebacker for Sunday's contest. Campbell's next chance to play is Week 9 against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Campbell (hamstring/quadriceps) didn't participate in Wednesday's walkthrough.
story: Campbell likely picked up the injuries during the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday, when he logged two assisted tackles while playing 41 snaps (37 on defense, four on special teams). He has two more chances to return to practice this week, although he could be tagged with an injury designation for Sunday's NFC East tilt against the Commanders depending on his participation levels.

headline: Campbell (knee) does not have an injury designation against the Jaguars on Sunday.
story: Campbell tweaked his knee during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams, but the second-year linebacker was able to log a full practice Friday, which was enough for him to fade an injury tag for Sunday's road game. Campbell has 37 tackles (24 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one forced fumble through the first four games of the regular season.

headline: Campbell (knee) was limited during Thursday's practice.
story: Campbell didn't practice Wednesday, but he was out there in a limited capacity Thursday, which is an encouraging sign regarding his potential to play against Jacksonville in Week 5. The 22-year-old has had a fantastic 2026 campaign thus far, amassing 37 total tackles (24 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one forced fumble (four games).

headline: Campbell (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
story: Campbell has played well this season, recording at least nine tackles in each of the Eagles' first four games of the 2026 campaign. It's possible he didn't practice Wednesday as a precautionary measure, so he could be out there at some point ahead of the Week 5 meeting with Jacksonville.

headline: Campbell recorded nine solo tackles during Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
story: Campbell was able to notch a season-high nine solo stops, while he has now registered at least nine total tackles in each of the team's first four games this year. The linebacker has compiled 37 total tackles (24 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also forcing a fumble over four contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Campbell (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Campbell is dealing with a knee injury and was limited during Wednesday's practice. However, he logged a full session Thursday, so all signs are pointing toward his availability for Sunday's game versus the Rams. The 22-year-old has played well through the first three weeks of the 2026 campaign, amassing 28 total tackles (15 solo), 1.0 sacks and one forced fumble.

headline: Campbell (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Campbell likely suffered his knee injury during the Eagles' Week 3 loss to the Bears. The linebacker practicing in a limited capacity despite the new injury is a good sign. Campbell should be able to avoid any injury designation for Sunday's Week 4 matchup with the Rams by upgrading to a full participant in practice by Friday.

headline: Campbell totaled nine tackles (four solo) in Monday's loss to the Bears.
story: Campbell was one of three Philadelphia defenders to co-lead the squad with nine stops. The second-year linebacker has gotten off to a strong start to the campaign in the tackling department, as he is tied for seventh in the NFL with 28 stops through three contests. Campbell had 80 tackles over 17 regular-season games last year, and he's well above pace to surpass that mark in 2026.

headline: Campbell recorded 10 total tackles (six solo) and a forced fumble during Sunday's 24-20 win over the Titans.
story: Campbell was able to notch double-digit takedowns for the first time this season, and he stripped running back Tyjae Spears in the second quarter, but the ball went out of bounds before it could be recovered. The linebacker has now compiled 19 total tackles (11 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and a forced fumble over two games this year.

headline: Campbell recorded nine tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Sunday's 24-22 win over the Commanders.
story: The linebacker also played on 64 of 70 defensive snaps. Campbell made 80 tackles (44 solo) as a rookie, but he did not record a sack, and he ultimately lost his starting job to Nakobe Dean. With Dean now in Las Vegas, Campbell, a 2025 first-round pick, appears primed for a bigger role in 2026.

headline: Elliott (ankle) was a limited participant at the Eagles' practice Wednesday.
story: Elliott opened the week with a limited session as a result of an apparent ankle issue. The kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT try during the team's 27-10 loss to Washington in Week 8, and he may have picked up the ankle injury during the contest. Elliott will have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the Giants.

headline: Elliott went 1-for-2 on field-goal tries and hit his only extra-point attempt in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
story: Elliott clanged a 41-yard attempt off the left upright in the fourth quarter. It was the veteran's first miss of the season, but the Eagles are simply not giving him enough scoring chances to keep him relevant in fantasy football.

headline: Elliott made all three of his PAT attempts and didn't attempt a field goal in Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys.
story: Elliott hasn't missed a kick all season, but he remains stuck on five field-goal attempts for the campaign, as the Eagles aren't moving the ball consistently but have found ways to punch in touchdowns when they get in scoring range. With Philadelphia banged up on offense and in the midst of a five-game losing streak, Elliott is facing some headwinds heading into a favorable Week 8 matchup on paper against the Commanders, who are giving up 28.7 points per game.

headline: Elliott made both of his extra-point attempts during the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
story: With Jalen Hurts (calf) out for the year, Sunday was the Eagles' first game with Tanner McKee under center. The offense labored to get up and down the field, and it was the fifth time in six games that Elliott attempted zero or one field goals. Week 7 against the Cowboys on Monday, Oct. 26 could be a better night offensively for the Eagles, given that Dallas' defense ranks 30th in the league in yards allowed per game.

headline: Elliott made his lone field-goal attempt and both of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars in London.
story: Elliott's only field-goal try came late in the fourth quarter, when he knocked through his 48-yard attempt to give the Eagles a 17-16 lead with only eight seconds left to play. He has yet to miss a kick through five regular-season games, though he's made only one field goal or zero in four of those contests. Elliott's scoring floor ceiling figures to be limited given that the Eagles' offense has the second-fewest yards per game (262.2) and ranks in the bottom-5 in points allowed per game (18.4). The Eagles will be home for four of their next five games, starting with Week 6 against the Panthers on Oct. 18.

headline: Elliott converted both field-goal attempts and both PATs in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
story: Elliott made field goals from 29 and 56 yards against Los Angeles and remains perfect on the season. He has just four field goals through four games and is 9-for-9 on extra-point attempts. The Eagles aren't currently scoring enough on offense to warrant elite kicker status for Elliott.

headline: Elliott converted his sole PAT and attempted no field goals in the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears on Monday night.
story: Elliott had an uneventful day, kicking through his one extra point on a second-quarter touchdown. The kicker remains 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and moves to 7-for-7 on extra-point tries through three regular-season games.

headline: Elliott converted his only field-goal attempt and made all three of his PATs in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Titans.
story: Elliott made the most of his lone field-goal try of the day, making a 58-yarder in the third quarter. The kicker hasn't been leaned on often so far this year, but he has made both of his field-goal tries, and Sunday's 58-yard make is rather inspiring after Elliott combined to make five of 15 attempts from 50-plus yards over the last two seasons.

headline: Elliott made his sole field-goal attempt and converted all three of his PATs in Sunday's 24-22 win over the Commanders.
story: Elliott made a 35-yard field goal and provided the consistency that Washington's Drew Stevens could not on PATs, something that ultimately decided the game in the Eagles' favor. The kicker heads into Week 2 without being tested from range, and it remains to be seen how the 31-year-old will fare on 50-yarders or more in 2026.

headline: Wicks (ankle) was a non-participant at Wednesday's practice.
story: Wicks hasn't practiced due to an ankle injury since preparation for a Week 6 matchup with the Panthers, missing the last two games in the process. He likely will need to mix into drills in some capacity Thursday and/or Friday to put himself in a position to return to action Sunday versus the Giants.

headline: Wicks (ankle) wasn't spotted at Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: Wicks has missed the last two games with an ankle injury and is trending towards being a DNP to start Week 9. If he's unable to ramp up his activity in the coming days, another missed game would be very much on the table. The Eagles are readying Joe Milton at quarterback, and he could be without both Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring), who was also absent from Wednesday's viewing period.

headline: Wicks (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday night's game against the Commanders.
story: With both Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) missing a second straight game, Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore should again handle most of the wide-receiver duties for the Eagles. Wicks' next chance to suit up for game action will arrive Nov. 8 against the Giants.

headline: Wicks (ankle) wasn't spotted at the start of Friday's practice, Andrew DiCecco of InsideTheBirds.com reports.
story: With Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) both remaining DNP on Friday, it appears as if the Eagles are going to head into Sunday night against the Commanders leaning on Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore at wide receiver for the second straight week.

headline: Wicks (ankle) isn't participating in Thursday's practice, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: Wicks hasn't practiced in any fashion since Week 6 while he continues to manage an ankle injury. Unless he's able to get back on the field in some capacity Friday, Wicks will likely be ruled out for a second straight game this Sunday at Washington.

headline: Wicks (ankle) didn't take part in Wednesday's walkthrough.
story: Wicks thus has logged a DNP on four consecutive injury reports going back to last week as he deals with an ankle issue. He likely will need to practice in some capacity Thursday and/or Friday to have a chance to suit up Sunday at Washington.

headline: Wicks (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game versus the Cowboys.
story: Wicks wasn't able to practice in any capacity during Week 7 prep due to an ankle injury and thus will miss his first contest of the campaign. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also sidelined Monday, the Eagles will rely on a receiving corps composed of Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey, though TE Dallas Goedert (knee) may end up being the favorite target of QB Tanner McKee.

headline: Wicks (ankle) was not on the field for the start of Saturday's practice, Andrew DiCecco of Inside the Birds reports.
story: It looks like both Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will miss all three Week 7 practices, so the duo's chances of playing Monday against the Cowboys appears to be slim, but the Eagles will announce their injury designations following Saturday's session. Rookie Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) would all be involved more heavily in the offense if one or both of Wicks and Smith is sidelined.

headline: Wicks (ankle) didn't take part in Friday's practice.
story: With back-to-back DNPs to kick off Week 7 prep due to an ankle issue, Wicks has only one more opportunity to mix into drills Saturday before the Eagles potentially make a ruling on his status for Monday's contest against the Cowboys. Fellow WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also hasn't practiced this week, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey as the healthy options at the position on the active roster.

headline: Wicks (ankle) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice.
story: Wicks made a very brief exit late in this past Sunday's loss to the Panthers but was able to return. With an ankle injury being cited as the reason for Thursday's absence, the nature of the injury has been revealed. Both Wicks and No. 1 WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) were DNPs to kick off Week 7 prep, so the situation bears watching to see if either of them will be able to play Monday against the Cowboys.

headline: Wicks was not spotted during the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Jimmy Kempski of The Philly Voice reports.
story: The Eagles are holding a few key pass catchers out of practice Thursday, including Wicks, DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert. It could just be a rest day for those players, with clarification on any potential injuries to come on Thursday's injury report. If Wicks is dealing with an injury, he'll have an extra day to recover since the Eagles play Monday against Dallas.

headline: Wicks caught two of four passes for 24 yards during the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Wicks' 24 receiving yards were his second lowest of the season, but he still finished third among Eagles pass catchers in that category Sunday behind DeVonta Smith (75) and Dallas Goedert (61). Week 6 was the Eagles' first game with Tanner McKee under center, and with Jalen Hurts (calf) out for the rest of the season, the scoring floors of Wicks and the other Philadelphia pass catchers figure to be lower moving forward. That said, the Eagles have a juicy Week 7 matchup on Monday, Oct. 26 against the Cowboys, whose defense ranks in the bottom-10 in the league in fantasy points allowed per game to wide receivers.

headline: Wicks (undisclosed) returned to Sunday's contest versus the Panthers, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: Both Wicks and fellow WR Makai Lemon (undisclosed) visited the medial tent in the second half, but both of them were able to rejoin Week 6 action.

headline: Wicks (undisclosed) went to the medical tent during Sunday's game versus the Panthers, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: Wicks was tripped up by a Panthers defender at the end of a catch and run in the fourth quarter, and he went down to the turf before going to the sideline. He had two catches (on four targets) for 24 yards before his departure.

headline: Wicks (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest versus the Panthers.
story: Wicks was limited Wednesday and didn't log any on-field work Thursday, but an uncapped session Friday has him in the clear for Week 6 action. He'll be welcoming back DeVonta Smith (hamstring) to the lineup, though, which may not allow Wicks to reach the 6.5 targets per game that he received during Smith's two-game absence.

headline: Wicks (hamstring) is practicing Friday, Andrew DiCecco reports.
story: The extent of Wicks' participation is unclear, but it's at least a good sign relative to Thursday when he didn't practice at all. He was limited Wednesday, after playing through the injury in a Week 5 loss to Jacksonville. Fellow Eagle wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also returned to practice Thursday, but it isn't clear if he has a real shot to play Sunday against the Panthers.

headline: Wicks (hamstring) didn't practice Thursday, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.
story: Wicks was limited on the final two Week 5 injury reports due to a hamstring issue, but he didn't carry a designation into the weekend and suited up for this past Sunday's loss to the Jaguars in London, earning an 84 percent snap share and hauling in five of eight targets for 63 yards. He opened this week as limited Wednesday, so his downgrade one day later may be cause for concern. Friday's practice report could unveil if Wicks is in danger of missing Sunday's contest against the Panthers.

headline: Wicks (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday.
story: Wicks now has been listed as limited on three consecutive injury reports dating back to last week due to a hamstring issue, but he wasn't tagged with a designation for a Week 5 matchup with the Jaguars in London. He ended up earning an 84 percent snap share in that contest, which he parlayed into five catches (on eight targets) for 63 yards with top WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) out for a second game in a row. Wicks doesn't appear to be in danger of sitting out this Sunday versus the Panthers, but his status nonetheless will be monitored as the week goes on.

headline: Wicks caught five of eight targets for 63 yards during Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
story: Wicks led the team in targets, and he was able to match his season-high five catches in the defeat. The wide receiver also exceeded 60 receiving yards for the third time this season and first time since Week 2. Wicks has now caught 17 of 28 targets for 260 yards and a touchdown over his first five regular-season contests as a member of the Eagles.

headline: Wicks (hamstring) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London.
story: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) set to miss a second straight contest, Wicks, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper should comprise Philly's three-wide sets against Jacksonville. Wicks paced the group in snaps and routes last Sunday against the Rams and saw five targets.

headline: Head coach Nick Sirianni anticipates that Wicks (hamstring) "will be out there" at Friday's practice.
story: Sirianni confirmed that Wicks injured his hamstring during Thursday's session, and he wound up as a limited participant on the injury report. While it appears Wicks will get some work in Friday, his status for Week 5 will not be known until the Eagles release their final injury report of the week following Friday's practice.

headline: Wicks was limited at Thursday's practice due to a hamstring injury, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: Wicks' addition to the injury report midweek indicates that he may have picked up the health concern at practice, but he joins DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Hollywood Brown (ankle) as banged-up players at the position. Currently, rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey are the Eagles' healthy wide receivers.

headline: Wicks caught three of five targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
story: Wicks was slated to operate as the team's No. 1 wide receiver in Week 4 with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) sidelined. He finished third on the team in targets behind fellow wideouts Darius Cooper (7) and Makai Lemon (6), while his 18 receiving yards were a season low. Wicks will have an easier matchup in Week 5 against the Jaguars, regardless of whether Smith is available or not.

headline: Wicks will operate as the top wide receiver against the Rams on Sunday due to the absence of DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Chris McPherson of the Eagles' official site reports.
story: Wicks has the second-most targets, catches and receiving yards on the Eagles behind Smith through the first three games of the regular season. Smith gutted through a hamstring injury against the Bears in Week 3, but the star wide receiver will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines, meaning Wicks, rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper are all in line for more offensive snaps and targets from Jalen Hurts.

headline: Wicks recorded two receptions for 32 yards on five targets in Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears.
story: Though he didn't find paydirt, Wicks played a critical role on the Eagles' lone scoring drive late in the second quarter, leading off the possession with a 13-yard catch and run. He was otherwise held in check while the game was still competitive, with his other reception coming in the fourth quarter when the Bears had built a 20-point lead. Through his first three games with Philadelphia, Wicks has produced a 9-179-1 receiving line on 15 targets.

headline: Wicks caught five of six targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Titans.
story: While he wasn't able to get into the end zone, Wicks still had a strong showing as the Eagles' clear WR2 behind DeVonta Smith and ahead of rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon. The former Packer is looking good in his new offense, producing a 7-147-1 line on 10 targets through two contests, and Wicks will look to keep developing chemistry with Jalen Hurts in a Week 3 road trip to Chicago.

headline: Wicks caught two of four targets for 73 yards and a touchdown Sunday in a 24-22 Week 1 victory against Washington.
story: Wicks didn't log a particularly high volume of targets, but he nonetheless put up a nice fantasy score thanks to a 64-yard connection with Jalen Hurts late in the first quarter and a nine-yard TD catch in the second. Hurts spread the ball around pretty evenly, hooking up with six different pass catchers, none of whom logged more than four receptions. It could play into Wicks' favor if the Eagles' new offense encourages Hurts to spread the ball around, though all of DeVonta Smith, Makai Lemon and tight end Dallas Goedert figure to need to be fed in addition to Wicks.

headline: Wicks is listed as a starter on the Eagles' unofficial depth chart.
story: Philadelphia lists three starting wide receivers, with those spots going to Wicks, DeVonta Smith and rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon. Wicks had 581 receiving yards as a rookie with the Packers during the 2023 regular season and has failed to reach that mark since, posting only 415 receiving yards in the 2024 regular season and 332 yards in 2025. The 25-year-old wide receiver has an opportunity to play a larger role with his new team, which will kick off regular-season action Sunday against the Commanders.

headline: Smith (hamstring) didn't practice Wednesday.
story: Smith's lack of activity to kick off Week 9 prep doesn't come as a surprise, as he wasn't present during the media-access portion of Wednesday's session. He hasn't practiced since his last appearance in a Week 6 loss to the Panthers, when he went for seven catches (on 14 targets) for 75 yards and one touchdown. If he's able to put himself in a position to play Sunday against the Giants, Smith will be on the receiving end of passes from QB Joe Milton, who is replacing Tanner McKee as the starter.

headline: Smith (hamstring) wasn't spotted at Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: Smith has missed four of the last five contests due to a lingering hamstring injury, and until he's able to mix into drills again, he may not be a candidate to be active on game days. The Eagles have a Week 10 bye after Sunday's matchup with the Giants, so the team could be focusing on getting him healthy for Week 11 and beyond. In any case, fellow WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) also wasn't seen Wednesday, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore as the healthy options at the position on the active roster.

headline: Smith (hamstring) is listed as out for Sunday night's game against the Commanders.
story: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) has also been ruled out, so both wideouts will miss a second straight contest. Look for Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore to soak up most of the snaps at wideout for Philadelphia. Smith will thus target a potential return to action Nov. 8 against the Giants.

headline: Smith (hamstring) remains sidelined for Friday's practice, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: Smith has missed practice all week, making him unlikely to play Sunday night against the Commanders. Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was also absent Friday, paving the way for Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore to again handle wideout duties in Week 8.

headline: Smith (hamstring) missed Thursday's practice.
story: Smith so far has sat out Wednesday's walkthrough and Thursday's practice due to a lingering hamstring injury, giving him just one more opportunity to mix into drills this week. The Eagles may make a ruling on Smith's status for Sunday's game in Washington once they post their final Week 8 injury report Friday.

headline: Smith (hamstring) wasn't spotted during the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: Smith was a non-participant at Wednesday's walkthrough, and he doesn't appear ready to rejoin his teammates one day later. He has sat out three of the past four games and will likely need to practice in at least some capacity Friday to have a chance to play Sunday night against the Commanders.

headline: Smith (hamstring) was a non-participant at Wednesday's walkthrough.
story: Smith has missed three of the last four games due to a hamstring injury, and his lack of activity to begin Week 8 prep isn't a great sign for his odds to return to action Sunday in Washington. He likely will need to mix into drills Thursday and/or Friday to have a chance to play this weekend.

headline: Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Cowboys.
story: Smith was unable to practice all week while nursing a hamstring injury, and the Eagles will be without both of their top wide receivers, as Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) has also been ruled out. Rookie Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown figure to be the Eagles' top wideouts for Monday night's game, and tight end Dallas Goedert will be a go-to target for quarterback Tanner McKee due to the absences of both Smith and Wicks. Smith's next opportunity to play is Week 8 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Smith (hamstring) was not seen at the Eagles' practice Saturday, EJ Smith of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: Smith missed each of the first two practices of Week 7 prep while tending to a hamstring injury that he aggravated against the Panthers in Week 6. His absence for a third consecutive practice doesn't bode well for his chances of playing Monday against the Cowboys, but his status for that contest will be more clear once the Eagles announce their injury designations following Saturday's session. Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was also not on the field, so Dallas Goedert (knee), Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper could be the top targets for quarterback Tanner McKee in Monday's NFC East showdown.

headline: Smith (hamstring) didn't practice Friday.
story: Smith previously sat out Weeks 4 and 5 due to a hamstring issue, but he was able to suit up this past Sunday against the Panthers, logging a 66 percent snap share and reeling in seven of 14 targets for 75 yards and one touchdown. It's unclear if Smith may be in danger of missing Monday's game versus the Cowboys, but Saturday's practice report will unveil his chances to suit up in Week 7.

headline: Smith (hamstring) wasn't spotted at Friday's portion of practice open to the media, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: Smith continues to miss practice with a hamstring injury that cost him two games prior to last Sunday's return against the Panthers. However, he may have aggravated the issue, considering his back-to-back DNPs to begin Week 7 prep. Makai Lemon, Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) and Darius Cooper would be in line for the wideout duties if Smith needs to sit Monday night against Dallas, though Wicks has an injury of his own.

headline: Smith (hamstring) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Smith wasn't present in the media-access portion of Thursday's session, and his previous hamstring issue appears to be the culprit for his absence to begin Week 7 prep. He thus will have two more chances to prove his health before the Eagles potentially tag him with a designation for Monday's game versus the Cowboys.

headline: Smith wasn't spotted at Thursday's practice, Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reports.
story: Smith sat out Weeks 4 and 5 due to a hamstring injury, but he logged a full practice last Friday before suiting up this past Sunday against the Panthers. His snap share (66 percent) in that contest was below his weekly norm, but he still hauled in seven of 14 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown while working with QB Tanner McKee. Thursday's practice report will reveal if Smith is dealing with a health concern, or is merely getting the day off.

headline: Smith brought in seven of 14 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Smith had an eventful day in his return from a two-game absence, leading the Eagles in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the afternoon. He also worked around getting briefly shaken up following a long incompletion where he appeared to have taken a blow to the chest area, and he added his second touchdown reception of the campaign via a 19-yard grab early in the fourth quarter. Smith displayed solid chemistry with fill-in signal-caller Tanner McKee, which certainly is a welcome development considering Jalen Hurts (IR, calf) is sidelined indefinitely.

headline: Smith (hamstring) practiced in full Friday and doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Panthers.
story: Prior to logging a limited practice Thursday, Smith had been working on a side field for roughly one week, so a return to action seemed possible before the Eagles cleared him outright Friday. He thus will be making his first appearance this weekend since a Week 3 loss at Chicago, looking to build upon his 19-235-1 line on 27 targets through the first three contests. Smith won't be working with Jalen Hurts (calf) due to a blood clot, though, with backup QB Tanner McKee subbing in for Hurts for as long as the latter is sidelined.

headline: Smith (hamstring) said Friday that he is "good" and that his availability for Week 6 is "up to the doctors," Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
story: Smith returned to practice Thursday and per reporters also got some work in Friday, so it seems he will have a chance to return to action in Week 6. His status for Sunday's matchup with the Panthers will officially be revealed when the Eagles release their final injury report of the week later Friday.

headline: Smith (hamstring) is practicing Friday, Jimmy Kempski of The Philly Voice reports.
story: Smith returned to practice Thursday as a limited participant, after missing the past two games. If he does play against the Panthers on Sunday, he'll be catching passes from backup QB Tanner McKee.

headline: Smith (hamstring) practiced on a limited basis Thursday.
story: Before he mixed back into drills Thursday, Smith hadn't practiced since logging all 50 offensive snaps during a Week 3 loss at Chicago. On a positive note, he's been working on the side since last Thursday, and his upgrade from DNP this Wednesday to limited one day later gives him a reasonable to chance to return to action Sunday versus the Panthers. Friday's injury report will reveal Smith's odds to play this weekend, and if he's able to do so, he'll be on the receiving end of passes from QB Tanner McKee after Jalen Hurts was ruled out for Week 6 action due to a blood clot.

headline: Smith was not seen with his helmet during the media viewing period Thursday,Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
story: Smith is nursing hamstring and toe injuries and it appears he'll be missing his second straight practice Thursday. He has missed back-to-back games and doesn't seem to be trending towards a return in Week 6 against the Panthers. The Eagles will already be missing Jalen Hurts (blood clot) for Sunday's game.

headline: Smith (hamstring/toe) was a non-participant at Wednesday's practice.
story: While Smith remained sidelined from on-field work and now appears to be dealing with a toe injury in addition to his hamstring issue, he was spotted working on a JUGS machine during the open portion of Wednesday's session, per Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer. Smith has missed the last two games and may be trending toward a third absence if he isn't able to get back on the practice field by Friday.

headline: Smith (hamstring) was working on the JUGS machine during Wednesday's practice, Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: Smith thus is unlikely to practice Wednesday after missing the last two games due to a nagging hamstring issue. Head coach Nick Sirianni told Zach Berman of The Athletic on Monday that he's hopeful Smith will return this Sunday versus the Panthers, but he likely will need to mix into some drills this week to have a chance to do so.

headline: Head coach Nick Sirianni expressed hope Monday that Smith (hamstring) will return for this Sunday's game against the Panthers, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.
story: Smith has missed the Eagles' last two games due to a hamstring injury, and the Eagles also were without Saquon Barkley (hamstring) for their 19-17 Week 5 loss to the Jaguars in London. Smith has been limited to side work over the last couple of weeks, but a return to practice during Week 6 prep, even in a limited capacity, will be a positive step in his rehab program. Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon will continue to be the Eagles' top wide receivers in Smith's absence, though Darius Cooper appears to have been the biggest beneficiary of Smith's injury, with Cooper logging a 5-104-3 line on 10 targets over his last two games.

headline: Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's contest versus the Jaguars in London.
story: Smith was seen running on a side field Thursday before getting in some rehab work Friday, but he was listed as a non-participant on all three of the Eagles' Week 5 injury reports due to a lingering hamstring issue and thus won't play Sunday. With Hollywood Brown (ankle) also sidelined this weekend, Philadelphia's options at wide receiver will be Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey.

headline: Smith (hamstring) is doing rehab work on a side field at Friday's practice, EJ Smith of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: It leaves Smith's status in considerable doubt for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London, but the Eagles will release official injury designations later Friday. With Smith looking likely to miss Week 5, rookie Makai Lemon and Week 4 standout Darius Cooper once again will be in line to handle prominent pass-catching roles. Neither is particularly exciting in a broken Philadelphia offense.

headline: Smith (hamstring) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice.
story: Per Tim McManus of ESPN.com, Smith was seen running on a side field Thursday, but the activity wasn't enough for him to be considered limited. It could be a sign that Smith is closing in on a return to practice, but until he does he may be trending toward a second straight absence Sunday at Jacksonville due to a hamstring issue. Friday's injury report may provide clarity on that front.

headline: Smith (hamstring) was spotted running on a side field during Thursday's practice, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
story: It's a sign of progress as Smith deals with a hamstring injury that already has sidelined him for one game and didn't allow him to practice Wednesday. In any case, Thursday's injury report will unveil if he was able to upgrade to limited or instead remain a DNP for a second consecutive session.

headline: Smith (hamstring) isn't taking part in Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: Smith hasn't practiced since a Week 3 loss at Chicago in which he played all 50 offensive snaps on an existing hamstring issue, which is leaving him as, "at very best, questionable" for this coming Sunday's game in Jacksonville, per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network. Smith likely will need to mix into drills Thursday and/or Friday in order to give himself a chance to be available in Week 5. Currently, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey are the healthy wide receivers on the Eagles' active roster.

headline: Smith (hamstring), who has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Rams, is viewed "at very best, questionable" for the Eagles' Week 5 game versus the Jaguars in London, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: After he was unable to practice in any fashion during Week 4 while tending to the hamstring injury, Smith looks like he could be in store for a multi-game absence. The Eagles will likely wait and see how Smith fares in practice during the upcoming week before deciding whether he'll make the trip to London. While they are without Smith's services for at least the matchup with the Rams, the Eagles will look to get by with Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper and Elijah Moore as their main options at receiver.

headline: Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Rams.
story: Smith gutted through a hamstring injury during the Eagles' Week 3 loss at Chicago, playing all 50 offensive snaps en route to six catches (on eight targets) for 65 yards. After Smith failed to practice Wednesday and Thursday, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reported that he was in danger of sitting out Week 4, which now has been confirmed. In Smith's absence, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon will be the primary wide receivers at the disposal of QB Jalen Hurts.

headline: Smith (hamstring) remained sidelined for Friday's practice, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.
story: Smith is trending toward missing Sunday's game against the Rams, as he's been idle for practice all week. His absence will open up more opportunities for Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon in the passing game, making both worthwhile WR3 plays in fantasy.

headline: Smith (hamstring) isn't expected to be available Sunday versus the Rams, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
story: For a second straight week, Smith is dealing with a hamstring injury, but he was able to play through it during Monday's loss at Chicago, logging all 50 offensive snaps en route to six catches (on eight targets) for 65 yards. He hasn't practiced so far this week, and McManus' report indicates Smith likely will remain out Friday before the team eventually makes a ruling on his status for Week 4. If Smith doesn't suit up this weekend, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon would be the primary beneficiaries in the receiving corps.

headline: Smith (hamstring) is not practicing Thursday, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: This marks the second straight day of missed practice for Smith, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Smith's status looks to be in question heading into Sunday's crucial showdown with the Rams. He missed some practice time last week and was still able to play, but this is the second straight DNP for Smith.

headline: Smith missed Wednesday's walkthrough due to a hamstring injury.
story: Smith also kicked off last week with a DNP on the Eagles' first practice report due to a hamstring issue, only to progress to full and no designation ahead of Monday's road matchup with the Bears. In the end, though, his status bears watching in the coming days to ensure he's also good to go for Sunday's contest against the Rams.

headline: Smith secured six of eight targets for 65 yards in the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears on Monday night.
story: Smith led the Eagles across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets on a night when Jalen Hurts passed for just 153 yards. All three of the speedy wideout's totals also qualified as his second highest of the first three games of the season. Smith appears to be adjusting well to new coordinator Sean Mannion's offense despite the Eagles' collective performance on that side of the ball leaving plenty to be desired, and he'll take a robust 19-235-1 line on 27 targets into a Week 4 home showdown against the Rams on Sunday.

headline: Smith (hamstring) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bears.
story: Smith was working through a hamstring injury through Week 3 prep but ended with a full practice Saturday, which was enough for him to be cleared to play Monday. He has a 13-170-1 receiving line on 19 targets through the first two games of the regular season as the Eagles' top pass catcher, and he could see even more targets from Jalen Hurts due to the absence of top tight end Dallas Goedert (knee).

headline: Smith (hamstring) is participating in Saturday's practice, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: Smith has been working through a hamstring injury, which prevented him from practicing Thursday before he returned for Friday's session in a limited capacity. His status for Monday night's game against the Bears will be more clear once the Eagles announce their injury designations following Saturday's practice. Smith is coming off a 10-117-1 receiving line (on 13 targets) against the Titans in Week 2, and if he were to be ruled out or limited against Chicago, then Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper would all be in line for more targets from Jalen Hurts.

headline: Smith (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity Friday.
story: After sitting out Thursday's practice due to a hamstring issue, Smith returned to the field one day later and logged some individual drills before running on a side field, per Brooks Kubena of The Athletic. Smith thus still has some work to do to prove his health ahead of Monday's game at Chicago, and Saturday's injury report will reveal whether or not he has a designation for Week 3 action.

headline: Smith (hamstring) wasn't in uniform at the start of Friday's practice but eventually took part in individual drills before running on a side field, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: After sitting out Thursday's practice due to a hamstring injury, Smith's ability to get in some work Friday generally is a good sign as the Eagles prepare for a Week 3 visit to Chicago. At the very least, he appears as if he'll be listed as a limited participant on Philadelphia's second practice report of the week, and he'll have another chance to mix in at Saturday's session before the team potentially tags him with a designation ahead of Monday's contest.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) officially didn't practice Wednesday.
story: Barkley's DNP to begin Week 9 prep was forecast by his lack of presence during the open portion of Wednesday's session. He continues to deal with the hamstring and back injuries that bothered him last week, but he still was able to play this past Sunday at Washington, log a 32 percent snap share and turn 14 touches into 54 yards from scrimmage and one TD. If he follows a similar practice regimen as last week, Barkley also will sit out Thursday before returning as a limited participant Friday.

headline: Barkley wasn't present for the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: Barkley may still be tending to the hamstring and back issues that he impacted his practice reps last week, but Wednesday's injury report will reveal if he indeed was a non-participant and also the reason for his absence. Jaydon Blue is the only healthy RB on the Eagles' active roster, though practice-squad member Elijah Mitchell tallied 11 carries for 34 yards and four catches (on six targets) for three yards while splitting the backfield with Barkley this past Sunday at Washington.

headline: Barkley said after Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders that he has received assurances from the Eagles front office that he will remain with the team beyond the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports. "The whole time my mindset was, we have a little issue going on right now and I feel like I'm the type of player and the type of leader that can help us get out of it," Barkley said. "And I want to be one of the reasons why we fix it."
story: After dropping their sixth straight game Sunday, the Eagles now sit at 2-6 on the season and could be motivated to explore moving veteran players for draft capital ahead of the deadline. Barkley -- who is under contract through 2028 -- apparently won't be among the pieces the Eagles consider moving, as the team is counting on re-emerging as a playoff contender next season rather than embracing a long-term rebuilding effort. Though he'll be suiting up for a Week 9 matchup with the division-leading Giants, Barkley could continue to have his playing time managed while he gets ramped back up from hamstring and back injuries. He played just 22 of the Eagles' 68 offensive snaps in the loss to Washington, finishing with 13 carries for 30 yards and a touchdown and a 24-yard reception on his lone target.

headline: Barkley rushed 13 times for 30 yards and a touchdown while catching his only target for 24 yards in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
story: Barkley got to the edge to score a three-yard rushing touchdown out of the wildcat formation and give the Eagles a 10-0 first-quarter lead, but it was all Washington after that. He came into the game averaging 5.7 yards per carry but mustered only 2.3 YPC in this one while playing at less than full health. Barkley didn't sit down when on the sideline in an effort to stay loose and mitigate the effects of the back injury he sustained in Week 7 against Dallas while compensating for a hamstring injury that kept him out of the previous two games.
