The banged-up Barkley, who didn't notch a touch in the fourth quarter, likely will try to gut it out again in Week 9 against the NFC East-leading Giants.

headline: The Eagles aren't expected to move Barkley ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Philadelphia's roster has been ravaged by injuries this season, and Barkley himself hasn't avoided health concerns, with two contests where he's played above 70 percent of snaps, three appearances in which he made early exits and two missed games to date. He thus has been capped to just 49 touches for 261 yards from scrimmage and one rushing touchdown, but general manager Howie Roseman won't consider trading Barkley ahead of the NFL's trade deadline. As for Barkley's Week 8 prospects, he doesn't have a designation for Sunday night's game at Washington and has only Jaydon Blue and Elijah Mitchell available behind him, so a workhorse role could be in the cards.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Washington.
story: After missing the first two practices of Week 8 prep, Barkley was able to practice in a limited capacity Friday as he deals with a lingering hamstring injury and a new back issue that he sustained Monday against the Cowboys. Earlier Friday, he told Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com, "I would hope so," when asked if he's playing Sunday. With no designation to speak of on the final practice report, Barkley is in the clear ahead of the weekend, and he likely will retain a workhorse role due to the otherwise banged-up nature of the Eagles backfield.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) said Friday that he hopes to play in Sunday night's game against the Commanders, Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reports.
story: After returning to practice Friday following absences to begin the week, Barkley at least appears to have a chance to suit up Sunday night. Expect Barkley to get a questionable designation, so fantasy players will need to have a backup plan in place. Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue are waiver-wire options for managers looking for a one-for-one replacement.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) is practicing Friday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: After sitting out Wednesday and Thursday's practices, Barkley's return to the field Friday at least gives him a chance to suit up Sunday night against the Commanders. His official participation level and any game designation will provide more clarity on his status heading into the weekend. Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue are next in line for snaps and carries for the Eagles if Barkley is unable to play.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Barkley has yet to practice this week due to dueling hamstring and back issues, the latter of which knocked him out of Monday's loss to the Cowboys. He relayed to Tim McManus of ESPN.com afterward that he isn't concerned about the most recent injury, but he now has just one more chance to get back on the practice field ahead of Sunday's game at Washington. With all of Tank Bigsby (abdomen), Will Shipley (foot) and Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) on IR, Jaydon Blue currently is the only healthy RB on the Eagles' active roster, though the team also used practice squad member Elijah Mitchell in Monday's loss to the Cowboys.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) wasn't spotted warming up at Thursday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: After being deemed a non-participant in Wednesday's walkthrough, Barkley now appears absent again at the start of Thursday's session. His official participation level will be confirmed by Philadelphia's injury report later Thursday, but Barkley seems to be trending in the wrong direction after sustaining what he described as a compensatory back injury during Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys, which marked his return from a two-game absence. Jaydon Blue is the top healthy alternative on the Eagles' active roster behind Barkley heading into Sunday night's game against the Commanders, with Elijah Mitchell a candidate to be elevated from the team's practice squad ahead of Week 8 action.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's walkthrough.
story: The Eagles are listing Barkley's previous hamstring injury and the back issue that he picked up during Monday's loss to the Cowboys as the reasons for Wednesday's absence. He'll have two more chances to mix into drills this week, but even if he isn't able to, he mentioned of the aforementioned contest that his "hamstring came out great" and that he isn't worried about the new health concern, per Tim McManus of ESPN.com. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will reveal Barkley's odds to suit up Sunday at Washington.

headline: Barkley said after Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys that his "hamstring came out great," and noted that the back issue that kept him out for the entire fourth quarter isn't anything that he expects to prevent him from playing Sunday against the Commanders, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
story: While suiting up for the first time since Week 4 after missing the Eagles' previous two games due to a hamstring strain, Barkley took the field for just 10 snaps on the night but was impactful in his limited playing time. He touched the ball on nine of those snaps, carrying seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown to go with two receptions for nine yards on two targets. Heading into the game, the Eagles had deliberately planned to manage Barkley's workload to some extent, but he ended up seeing fewer snaps than anticipated after his back locked up on him following a 29-yard run in the first quarter. He didn't end up taking any snaps after the third quarter, with the Eagles leaning exclusively on Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) and Elijah Mitchell out of the backfield over the final 15 minutes. Fortunately for Barkley, the back issue doesn't seem to be a major concern, but his activity in practice this week will warrant monitoring as the Eagles assess his availability for Sunday's contest.

headline: Barkley said after Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys that he sustained a compensatory back injury, which he tried to play through after tweaking his injured hamstring on his first run of the game, EJ Smith of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: Coming into Monday, Barkley had been listed as questionable after missing the Eagles' previous two games due to a hamstring strain, but he tried to tough it out and give the offense a much-needed boost out of the backfield. He did just that on the team's first drive, gaining 12 yards on a reception on the first play and immediately following with a 29-yard run. Barkley appeared to pull up a bit lame on the latter play, but he still delivered an eight-yard rushing touchdown less than two minutes later. However, the star running back was used only intermittently for the remainder of the contest, and he sat out the entire fourth quarter while backup Dameon Pierce finished with 14 carries (for 47 yards and a touchdown) to Barkley's seven. Smith relayed that Barkley was on a "pitch count" ahead of Monday's game, so the Eagles may have been motivated to hold him out for the rest of the contest once the back issue cropped up. The Eagles will face a quick turnaround with a Week 8 matchup Sunday versus the Commanders, so it wouldn't be surprising if Barkley's practice activity was affected leading up to that contest.

headline: Barkley is questionable to return to Monday's game against the Cowboys due to a back injury.
story: Barkley entered Monday's contest managing a hamstring injury but was ultimately able to suit up. The star running back looked hobbled throughout much of the game but was able to tally 62 yards and a touchdown on just seven carries along with two catches on two targets for nine yards before being deemed questionable to return early in the fourth period. The Eagles indicated that Barkley is dealing with a back issue when announcing his 'questionable' tag, so it's unclear if the hamstring is also still bothering him.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) is listed as active Monday against the Cowboys.
story: Barkley is available to power the Eagles' backfield for the first time since Week 4, ending a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Considering he practiced fully Saturday, he may be ready to operate as a workhorse as he did in his two healthy games (Weeks 1 and 3) this season. In those games, Barkley combined for 32 touches for 160 yards from scrimmage and no TDs.

headline: Barkley (hamstring), who is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Cowboys, is "trending toward playing," Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Though No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for the Week 7 contest, the Eagles are expected to get one of their other top playmakers in Barkley back in action following a two-game absence. Barkley participated in practice throughout the week, turning in limited sessions Thursday and Friday before upgrading to full activity Saturday. Assuming his hamstring checks out fine while warming up Monday, Barkley's availability should be confirmed when the Eagles release their inactive list 90 minutes prior to the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Cowboys.
story: Barkley followed up limited sessions Thursday and Friday with a full practice Saturday, but his status remains up in the air for Week 7 action. He's seeking his first game action since Week 4 as he tends to a lingering hamstring injury, something that'll be confirmed, one way or another, about 90 minutes before Monday's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) was on the field for the start of Saturday's practice, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: Barkley was a limited participant in each of the first two practices of Week 7 prep as the star running back works his way back from a hamstring injury that sidelined him for each of the Eagles' last two games. Saturday's practice report will shed light on Barkley's status ahead of Monday's game against the Cowboys, and a full session would likely be enough for him to avoid an injury designation. His return would result in Dameon Pierce reverting to a rotational role in the backfield.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) was a limited practice participant Friday.
story: Barkley now has logged back-to-back capped practices this week, giving him one more chance to get back to full Saturday, at which point the Eagles may make a ruling on his status for Monday's game against the Cowboys. He's missed the last two games due to a hamstring injury.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) is practicing Friday, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: After practicing in a limited capacity Thursday, Barkley was on the field again Friday as he continues to work back from the hamstring injury that cost him the past two games. His presence at another session keeps him on track for a possible return Monday night against Dallas. Dameon Pierce would then become mostly irrelevant from a fantasy football standpoint.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
story: This marks Barkley's first official on-field work since he initially suffered a hamstring injury in Week 4 against the Rams. He consequently sat out Weeks 5 and 6, but his return to drills this week at least gives him a chance to suit up Monday versus the Cowboys. Barkley told Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer on Thursday that he wants to play in Week 7 but still needs to test out his hamstring over the next few days. Ultimately, Saturday's practice report will reveal Barkley's odds to return to action.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) was in uniform for Thursday's practice, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: The Eagles signaled that Barkley was approaching a return to action by moving on from Carson Steele (shoulder, IR) and Jaydon Blue earlier this week. Mike Garafolo of NFL Network then reported Thursday morning that Barkley was expected to practice Thursday with the aim to play Monday against the Cowboys. While Barkley's activity level as he mixes back into drills isn't known yet, he appears to be trending in the right direction for Week 7 action.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) is expected to practice Thursday and "is in line to play Monday against the Cowboys," Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Barkley has not practiced at all since injuring his hamstring in Week 4, but it appears he will be back out there Thursday. His return would be a welcome boost for an Eagles team that currently only has two other running backs available -- Dameon Pierce and Elijah Mitchell, who joined the practice squad earlier this week.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: After missing a second straight week of practice due to a right hamstring injury, Barkley subsequently will be inactive for a second occasion this season. The Eagles placed Will Shipley (foot) on injured reserve Friday, so the backfield currently is occupied by Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele, the former of whom is the favorite to garner more of the workload for as long as Barkley is sidelined.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reports.
story: Barkley hasn't practiced the past two weeks and now appears likely to miss a second game. The Eagles will be short-handed, to say the least, with QB Jalen Hurts (blood clot) now joining the long list of starters to miss time this season. If Barkley is indeed inactive, Dameon Pierce will be the favorite to start at running back for Philadelphia.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's injury report.
story: Barkley's lack of activity so far this week isn't a surprise considering he hasn't been present for either of the Eagles' two practices. He thus has one more opportunity to attempt to mix into drills Friday, at which point the team may make a ruling on his status ahead of Sunday's game against the Panthers. If Barkley and fellow RB Will Shipley (foot) are sidelined this weekend, Dameon Pierce is the top candidate to pace Philadelphia's backfield, with Carson Steele also on hand for reps that linger.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) wasn't present for the open portion of Thursday's practice, Martin Frank of The News Journal reports.
story: As of Wednesday, Barkley has been listed as a non-participant on four consecutive injury reports due to a right hamstring issue, and he seems poised to make it five such listings once the Eagles post their second Week 6 report. With Will Shipley (foot) likely out for multiple weeks, Dameon Pierce seems set for a large workload out of the backfield Sunday against the Panthers, assuming Barkley doesn't put himself in a position to play.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) officially didn't practice Wednesday.
story: Barkley has yet to mix into drills since suffering a right hamstring injury in the early stages of the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams. Head coach Nick Sirianni expressed hope Monday that Barkley will return to action Sunday against the Panthers, suggesting it's possible he gets back on the practice field by Friday. Until that happens, though, Barkley likely is trending toward another absence in Week 6, which would leave Philadelphia's backfield in the hands of Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele with Will Shipley (foot) set for a multi-week stay on the sideline.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) wasn't spotted at the portion of Wednesday's practice open to the media, Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reports.
story: Barkley was inactive for this past Sunday's loss to the Jaguars in London due to a hamstring injury suffered one week prior, but head coach Nick Sirianni told Zach Berman of The Athletic on Monday that he's "hopeful" the running back will gain clearance to play in Week 6 against the Panthers. Assuming Barkley goes down as a DNP on Wednesday, he's not beginning the week on the right foot, but he'll still have two more chances to mix into drills Thursday and Friday.

headline: Head coach Nick Sirianni said Monday that he's "hopeful" that both Barkley (hamstring) and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will both be cleared to play against the Panthers this coming Sunday, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.
story: Barkley was sidelined for Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars in London due to a right hamstring injury that he sustained during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams. Wednesday will be the first Eagles practice of Week 6 prep, and even a limited session would have Barkley trending toward a return against Carolina. Will Shipley was diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia following Sunday's game, and with Barkley and Tank Bigsby (abdomen, IR) both sidelined, that currently leaves Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele as the two healthy running backs on the Eagles' 53-man roster.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Jaguars in London.
story: Barkley didn't practice this week in the wake of suffering a right hamstring injury this past Sunday against the Rams, so his lack of availability for Week 5 doesn't come as a surprise. With Tank Bigsby (abdomen) on injured reserve, it'll be the Will Shipley show out of the Eagles backfield Sunday, while Dameon Pierce also is on hand for RB reps that linger, and Jaydon Blue and Carson Steele are options to be elevated from the practice squad. Barkley's next chance for game action is Sunday, Oct. 18 versus the Panthers.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, EJ Smith of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: Barkley hasn't practiced this week and isn't likely to play against the Jaguars on Sunday, leaving Will Shipley, Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele as Philadelphia's backfield options for Week 5. Shipley is the favorite to start and get most of the snaps.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) officially didn't practice Thursday.
story: Barkley has yet to log any on-field work since tweaking his right hamstring on his fourth offensive snap this past Sunday against the Rams. Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Barkley is considered week-to-week, and the Eagles can make a ruling on the running back's status for a Week 5 road matchup with the Jaguars on Friday's injury report. Will Shipley is poised for a workhorse role out of Philadelphia's backfield this weekend assuming Barkley indeed is ruled out.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) wasn't present during the open portion of Thursday's practice, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
story: Barkley appears as if he'll go down as a non-participant for a second session in a row to kick off Week 5 prep, something that'll be confirmed once the Eagles post Thursday's injury report. According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Barkley currently is viewed as week-to-week due to the hamstring issue that knocked him out of this past Sunday's game against the Rams after just four offensive snaps, so the running back's continued likely lack of activity isn't unexpected.

headline: Greenard (ankle) is available for Monday's game against the Cowboys.
story: Greenard has been battling an ankle injury. He was considered a game-time decision, though he will be active for the second consecutive contest.

headline: Greenard (ankle) is listed as questionable for Monday night's game against the Cowboys, Martin Frank of The Delaware News Journal reports.
story: Greenard is considered a game-time decision, meaning the strongside linebacker will have to prove he is set to suit up before Monday's contest. If Greenard is inactive for the primetime divisional matchup with the Cowboys, Jalyx Hunt (ankle/knee), Arnold Ebiketie or A.J. Epenesa (back) will need to start opposite Nolan Smith (concussion) for the Eagles' defense.

headline: Greenard (ankle) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against Carolina.
story: Greenard logged a full practice Friday, which was enough for the veteran edge rusher to be cleared to return from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury, and it's a timely return given that Jalyx Hunt (ankle/knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game. Greenard has one solo tackle and one forced fumble across two regular-season games.

headline: Greenard (ankle) was a limited participant at the Eagles' practice Wednesday.
story: Greenard was forced to miss the team's Week 5 loss to the Jaguars in London while dealing with an ankle injury. The linebacker was unable to practice at all last week, so his participation Wednesday is a step in the right direction. Greenard will have two more chances to log a full practice and officially move past the ankle issue prior to a matchup with the Panthers on Sunday.

headline: Greenard (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London.
story: Greenard will be sidelined for the London game after an ankle injury prevented him from practicing all week. After being acquired from the Vikings in April and immediately signing a four-year, $98 million extension with the Eagles, Greenard has played in two of the Eagles' first five games and has contributed just one tackle to go with one forced fumble.

headline: Greenard (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against Jacksonville.
story: Greenard was held out of practice all week due to an ankle injury he sustained against the Rams in Week 4. Despite the lack of practice, the Eagles are still keeping the door open for Greenard to play Sunday, but if he's not cleared to suit up, then Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa would all be in line for more defensive snaps.

headline: Greenard (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
story: Greenard exited Sunday's loss to the Rams. He is considered day-to-day, so his absence from practice Wednesday isn't a surprise. The 29-year-old has logged only 37 defensive snaps during the 2026 campaign, though his absence could allow more involvement from A.J. Epenesa and Arnold Ebiketie.

headline: Greenard (ankle) is considered day-to-day after exiting Sunday's game against the Rams, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Greenard played just 19 defensive snaps against Los Angeles before suffering his injury. If he needs to miss time, Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa would be next in line for snaps off the edge opposite Nolan Smith. Greenard is still looking for his first sack of the season after recording just 3.0 sacks with Minnesota in 2025.

headline: Greenard (ankle) won't return to Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: Greenard suffered an ankle injury and was initially listed as questionable to return. However, he has since been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's contest. Without Greenard on the field, Nolan Smith and Jalyx Hunt are in line for more defensive snaps the rest of the way.

headline: Greenard (pectoral) is active for Monday night's matchup with Chicago.
story: Greenard will make his Eagles debut after missing the team's first two contests of the regular season while recovering from a pectoral injury. The 29-year-old registered 3.0 sacks over 12 regular-season contests with Minnesota in 2025 before being traded to Philadelphia in April, and he'll look to get off to a strong start against the Bears to open his 2026 campaign.

headline: Greenard (pectoral) is listed as questionable ahead of Monday's game against the Bears.
story: Greenard was a full participant in Saturday's practice, marking the first time the linebacker has achieved that level of participation since sustaining his pectoral injury. Despite practicing in full, Greenard remains questionable to suit up for Monday's contest as the team makes certain the 29-year-old is ready for the challenge.

headline: Greenard (pectoral) was a limited participant in Friday's practice.
story: Greenard has logged a pair of limited practice sessions during the Eagles' Week 3 prep for Monday night's game against the Bears. The strong-side linebacker logged three limited sessions in Week 2 before remaining sidelined in the team's 24-20 win over the Titans. Unless Greenard upgrades to a full participant in Saturday's session, the 29-year-old's team/season debut will be delayed at least another week.

headline: Greenard (pectoral) was able to practice on a limited basis Thursday.
story: The pass rusher has yet to make his regular-season debut since getting traded to Philadelphia in the offseason, but he has now opened the practice week on a positive note. That said, Greenard was also a limited participant leading up to the Eagles' Week 2 matchup with the Titans before ultimately sitting out of the game. If Greenard can upgrade to full participation before Monday's matchup with the Bears, it should be a sign that he's on track to play.

headline: Greenard (pectoral) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Greenard was limited in all three Week 2 practice sessions due to a pectoral strain that he sustained during offseason workouts before the start of training camp. He didn't open the regular season on the active/PUP list, so the Eagles appear confident that Greenard is close to making his 2026 debut, which could come as soon as Week 3 against the Bears on Monday, Sept. 28. Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa will all operate in elevated roles at edge alongside Nolan Smith for as long as Greenard is shelved.

headline: Greenard (pectoral) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: Per Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia, Greenard said Thursday that he was close to being available for game action again, but he's still not sure whether that will be the case in Week 2. His status on the Eagles' official injury report Friday may provide some clarity on that front.

headline: Greenard (pectoral) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Greenard logged a limited practice session last Wednesday before downgrading to no participation last Thursday and ultimately being ruled out ahead of last Sunday's 24-22 win over the Commanders. The linebacker will once again be inspected by the Eagles training staff Friday, and they will then rule on whether he is set to suit up for next Sunday's game against the Titans.

headline: Greenard (pectoral) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Commanders.
story: Greenard was upgraded to a limited participant in Friday's practice after being absent from the Wednesday and Thursday sessions. The linebacker's participation level is promising for a potential Week 2 season debut against the Titans.

headline: Greenard (pectoral) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Greenard was activated off the active/PUP list at the end of August, but his status for Week 1 is still up in the air. He'll probably have to log a full practice Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Greenard (pectoral) was limited during Wednesday's practice, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
story: Greenard was activated off the active/PUP list Aug. 30, though that doesn't necessarily mean he will be available for Week 1 versus the Commanders. The 29-year-old, who was acquired by Philadelphia from Minnesota in April, appeared in 12 regular-season games for the Vikings in 2025, accumulating 38 total tackles, 3.0 sacks and one forced fumble.

headline: The Eagles activated Greenard (pectoral) off the active/PUP list on Aug. 30, Chris McPherson of the team's official site reports.
story: Greenard is listed on the Eagles' active roster but remains questionable with a pectoral injury he suffered while lifting weights preparing for training camp in July. The shift to the active roster instead of the reserve/PUP list implies the team thinks the linebacker will be ready for game action sooner rather than later, though it remains unclear if Greenard will be able to suit up for the Week 1 contest with the Commanders on Sunday.

headline: Hunt (ankle/knee) is available for Monday's game versus Dallas.
story: Hunt has been battling a few injuries. He didn't play in the Week 6 loss to Carolina, though he will return against the Cowboys. With Jonathan Greenard (ankle) also available, Hunt could see fewer snaps.

headline: Hunt (ankle/knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against Carolina.
story: Hunt was held out of practice all week due to ankle and knee injuries, which he picked up during the Eagles' Week 5 loss to the Jaguars in London. Hist next chance to play is Week 7 against the Cowboys on Monday, Oct. 26, and in Hunt's absence, Arnold Ebiketie is in line for more rotational snaps behind Nolan Smith and Jonathan Greenard.

headline: Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said Tuesday it would take something "miraculous" for Hunt (ankle) to play Week 6 against the Panthers, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: Hunt was seen wearing a walking boot Sunday, after leaving early in the Eagles' 19-17 Week 5 loss to the Jaguars. If the 25-year-old is unable to play, Arnold Ebiketie could see more playing time alongside Jonathan Greenard at edge.

headline: Hunt (ankle/knee) was seen wearing a walking boot on his left leg after the Eagles' 19-17 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: Hunt exited the contest after sustaining multiple injuries on the last play of the first half. The strongside linebacker's immediate placement in a boot is not a good sign for his chances of playing in the Eagles' Week 6 matchup with the Panthers.

headline: Hunt (ankle/knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London.
story: Hunt is dealing with ankle and knee injuries he suffered on the last play of the first half. The 25-year-old sustained the injuries while making a crucial fourth-down stop.

headline: Hunt (ankle/knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London.
story: Hunt exited the game at the end of the second quarter after assisting in stopping Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten on the goal line. The linebacker is dealing with multiple injuries, making it unlikely he will be able to return to the game.

headline: Hunt required assistance off the field at the end of the second quarter of Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London due to an apparent lower-body injury, Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reports.
story: After the Eagles defense stuffed Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten at the goal line on a fourth-and-goal to close out the first half, Hunt emerged from the play in considerable pain. The Eagles initially brought a cart out for the linebacker, but he was able to instead walk off the field while being supported by team trainers. The team should provide an update on his status following halftime, but he would appear to be questionable to return.

headline: McKee will shift to a backup role for Sunday's game against the Giants with the Eagles set to move forward with Joe Milton as their starting quarterback in Week 9, Adam Schefter of ESPN and Mike Garafolo of NFL Network report.
story: Just two days after announcing that McKee would draw a fourth straight start this weekend, head coach Nick Sirianni appears to have changed his tune. The Eagles' decision to move forward with Milton comes after McKee went 0-3 as a starter while completing 63.2 percent of his passes for 5.6 yards per attempt and a 2:2 TD:INT since replacing Jalen Hurts (calf) atop the depth chart. Since McKee is set to become a free agent next spring and may not be part of the Eagles' long-term plans, he could end up serving as the No. 3 quarterback if the team wants to give rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton the opportunity to suit up on game days.

headline: Head coach Nick Sirianni said Monday that McKee will remain the Eagles' starting quarterback, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports. "Tanner's our guy. We're not making any changes there," Sirianni said.
story: Since stepping into the starting role Week 6 in place of Jalen Hurts (calf), McKee has led the Eagles to an 0-3 record while completing 72 of 114 pass attempts (63.2 percent) for 638 yards (5.6 YPA), two touchdowns and two interceptions while adding 26 yards on six carries. Despite McKee's mediocre returns, the Eagles will stick with him as their starter for Sunday's matchup with the Giants, but another poor showing could prompt Sirianni to re-evaluate the quarterback situation following a Week 10 bye.

headline: McKee completed 23 of 34 passes for 212 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders. He also rushed four times for 25 yards and lost a fumble.
story: McKee operated without top two wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for a second consecutive game and failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time in his three-game stint as Philadelphia's starting QB. He has thrown for between 211 and 215 yards in each of his three outings since Jalen Hurts (calf) was shut down for the season. Expectations should remain tempered for McKee and Philadelphia's injury-riddled offense in Week 9 against the Giants.

headline: McKee completed 23 of 35 passes for 211 yards with one touchdown and one interception and added one rush for one yard in the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night.
story: McKee's final numbers weren't poor by any stretch, but the fourth-year signal-caller couldn't come close to keeping pace with Dak Prescott's exploits. McKee was working without both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), so in that context, the quarterback's production was solid, albeit unspectacular. McKee recorded completions to eight different targets overall, and he'll look to boost his overall numbers with a hopefully healthier receiving corps in a Week 8 road matchup against the Commanders on Sunday night.

headline: McKee completed 26 of 45 passes for 215 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions while adding one carry for no gain in the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
story: McKee's completion total was impressive, but he averaged a modest 4.8 yards per attempt on the afternoon despite having DeVonta Smith back from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury. McKee's longest completion of the day went for 19 yards to Smith on a fourth-quarter scoring strike, which brought Philadelphia to within five at the time. McKee ultimately wasn't able to complete the comeback in the first installment of what figures to be an extended starting assignment in place of Jalen Hurts (IR, calf), and he'll look to be more aggressive during a Week 7 home divisional clash with the Cowboys next Monday night.

headline: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni confirmed Friday that McKee will start Sunday's game against the Panthers, NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: McKee is likely headed for a multi-game run as the Eagles' starter, after Jalen Hurts (calf) was ruled out for Week 6 due to a superficial blood clot before landing on injured reserve Saturday. Rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton is active as the No. 2 quarterback for Sunday's game behind McKee, who will be making the third start of his four-year career. Unlike Hurts, the 6-foot-6, 231-pound McKee is more of a traditional pocket passer who doesn't offer much of a threat as a runner, but he's been serviceable in directing the Philadelphia offense in his limited opportunities. He's completed 54 of 88 career pass attempts (61.4 percent) for 597 yards (6.8 YPA), five touchdowns and one interception.

headline: McKee appears lined up to start Sunday's game against the Panthers after the Eagles announced Wednesday that Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for Week 6 due to a superficial blood clot on his calf, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: While the Eagles could look to re-sign the recently released Andy Dalton to give the quarterback room another experienced option in Hurts' absence, McKee looks poised to draw the start after moving ahead of Dalton on the depth chart prior to Week 4. Hurts' availability beyond Week 6 is in flux while the Eagles determine the appropriate course for his treatment, so McKee could be headed for a multi-game run as the team's starter. A 2023 sixth-round pick, McKee has appeared in just six games (two starts) during his four-year career, completing 54 of 88 pass attempts (61.4 percent) for 597 yards (6.8 YPA) and a 5:1 TD:INT. Assuming he starts, McKee may have few weapons at his disposal, as running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) were absent from practice Wednesday and could be tracking toward sitting out this weekend.

headline: McKee is expected to be active for Sunday's game against the Rams as the top backup to starter Jalen Hurts, while Andy Dalton serves as the Eagles' No. 3 quarterback, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Despite operating as Hurts' primary backup in 2025, McKee slid to third on the depth chart entering the 2026 season after the Eagles acquired Dalton in a trade with the Panthers back in March. Dalton didn't see any snaps on the season until midway through the second quarter of Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears, when Hurts made a brief exit from the contest to get checked for a concussion. After three consecutive Saquon Barkley carries got the Eagles near the goal line, Dalton proceeded to throw a costly interception in the end zone on his lone pass attempt before Hurts returned for the next possession. The gaffe appears to have resulted in Dalton turning the backup gig over to McKee, at least for one week.

headline: McKee (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the team's emergency third quarterback Monday night against the Bears.
story: McKee will operate as the team's No. 3 QB for the third straight week to open the regular season. The 26-year-old will only be eligible to enter the contest if both starter Jalen Hurts and top backup Andy Dalton sustain injuries.

headline: McKee (coach's decision) is inactive as the emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: McKee will be the emergency option for the Eagles in consecutive weeks. The 26-year-old will only enter the game if both active quarterbacks cannot continue to play. The quarterback should stay in this role throughout the 2026 season unless Jalen Hurts or Andy Dalton suffers an injury.

headline: McKee (coach's decision) is inactive as the emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
story: McKee will be the emergency option behind Jalen Hurts and Andy Dalton. The quarterback will only enter the game if both active players are unable to play.

headline: Milton is set to be the Eagles' starting quarterback Sunday against the Giants, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Philadelphia signed Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad Oct. 16, and less than a month later, he's getting the call after the Tanner McKee experience so far has resulted in three consecutive losses. In five appearances (no starts) between New England and Dallas in his career, Milton has competed 37 of 53 passes for 424 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while rushing 15 times for 66 yards and one TD and losing both of his fumbles.

headline: Milton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Eagles' emergency third quarterback against the Panthers on Sunday.
story: The Eagles signed Milton off the practice squad to the active roster Friday following the news that Jalen Hurts would be out indefinitely due to a superficial blood clot in his calf, with the latter being placed on injured reserve Saturday. The Eagles will start Tanner McKee on Sunday while rookie fifth-rounder Cole Payton serves as the backup. As the emergency QB3, Milton is prohibited from playing against Carolina unless both McKee and Payton leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: The Eagles are signing Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports.
story: With Jalen Hurts recovering from a blood clot on his calf, the Eagles are set to start Tanner McKee this Sunday against the Panthers. Should Hurts miss additional time, Milton could eventually become an option to make starts, though he'll likely be focused on learning the offense and otherwise acclimating for the next few weeks.

headline: Moore did not garner a target during Sunday night's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
story: Moore was held without a catch for the first time since Week 5, failing to take advantage of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) being unavailable. Moore figures to remain an afterthought on offense in Week 9 against the Giants.

headline: Moore caught both of his targets for 16 yards during Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys.
story: Moore had the opportunity to work in an expanded role Monday due to the absences of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Moore's 22 snaps on offense were fourth-most among Eagles wide receivers and he logged season highs in both catches and receiving yards. However, the Eagles' offense as a whole struggled without its top wide receivers, and Moore would revert to a deep rotational role against the Commanders on Sunday if one or both of Smith and Wicks were cleared to return.

headline: Moore (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: The veteran wideout will serve as a healthy scratch for the second time in as many games to open the season. Moore appears destined to retain the same status moving forward unless multiple injuries strike at wide receiver for the Eagles.

headline: Moore (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
story: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown are set to be the starting four wide receivers for the Eagles in Week 1. Moore is the odd man out, set to likely be inactive until another player wastes his chance or gets injured.

headline: Brown finished Sunday's loss to the Commanders with two catches for 17 yards on two targets.
story: With both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) missing the contest, Brown ranked third among Eagles wideouts with 32 offensive snaps. He didn't do much with the opportunity, as the veteran wideout notched just two receptions for the second straight week. If Smith and/or Wicks return in Week 9 against the Giants, Brown may see his role diminish.

headline: Brown secured two of five targets for 30 yards in the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night.
story: Brown saw an expanded role due to the absences of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), and the veteran wideout finished third in receiving yards and targets as a result. Brown's stats were his first of the season, and although there have been some rumblings about him being a potential trade candidate, the Eagles' lack of healthy bodies at the position could give Brown some job security through the deadline.

headline: NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports that teams seeking help at wide receiver will likely call the Eagles about the status of Brown before the Nov. 10 deadline.
story: Brown's lone regular-season game this season was in Week 2 against the Titans, when he rushed for 12 yards on two carries and did not record a target. He missed the next three games due to an ankle injury and was a healthy scratch for Week 6 against the Panthers, and the veteran wide receiver doesn't appear to be in the Eagles' offensive gameplan moving forward. The Eagles have a 2-4 record, and with franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts (calf) likely out for the rest of the season, the team could be looking to trade Brown and other players by the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

headline: Brown (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Brown missed the Eagles' last three games due to an ankle injury, but he avoided an injury designation for Week 6 after logging a full practice Friday. However, the veteran wide receiver will be a healthy scratch for Sunday's game as the Eagles go with six active wide receivers, with the position group led by a returning DeVonta Smith. Brown's next opportunity to play is Week 7 against the Cowboys on Monday, Oct. 26.

headline: Brown (ankle) was a limited participant at the Eagles' practice Wednesday.
story: Brown has been sidelined for each of the team's last three contests while nursing an ankle injury, but his limited session Wednesday is a step in the right direction. The wide receiver will have two more chances to log a full practice and officially move past the ankle issue prior to Sunday's matchup with the Panthers.

headline: Brown (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
story: An ankle injury will cause Brown to miss a third consecutive game, and his next chance to play is Week 6 against the Panthers on Sunday, Oct. 18. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has already been ruled out, so Philadelphia's top wideouts against Jacksonville will be Dontayvion Wicks, rookie Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper, with Elijah Moore and Britain Covey also providing depth at the position.

headline: Brown (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
story: Brown didn't practice to begin the week after missing the Eagles' last two games. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also missing Wednesday's practice, Jalen Hurts may need to rely on Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon and Dontayvion Wicks once again in Week 5 versus Jacksonville. There's a chance Dallas Goedert (knee) will be back as well.

headline: Brown (ankle) is listed as out ahead of Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: Brown didn't practice all week and will now miss his second game of the 2026 campaign. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) ruled out, Brown could have had an enhanced role if he was cleared to play in Week 4. However, with Brown, Smith and Dallas Goedert (knee) all on the shelf, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon will likely serve as Jalen Hurts' primary receiving options.

headline: Brown (ankle) did not participate in practice Thursday, Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: Brown suffered an ankle injury in preparation for Week 3, which led to him missing the Eagles' loss to the Bears on Monday night. The severity of his injury is uncertain, but the 29-year-old also opened the week as a non-participant in practice Wednesday. With back-to-back absences, Brown's availability for the Week 4 matchup against the Rams could be in jeopardy should he remain sidelined Friday.

headline: Brown (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Brown has yet to practice since sustaining his ankle injury during Week 3 prep. The wide receiver will likely need to upgrade to at least limited practice participation by Friday to have a shot at playing in the Eagles' contest against the Rams on Sunday.

headline: Brown (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Monday's game against the Bears.
story: Brown suffered an ankle injury during Week 3 prep and has been unable to practice since sustaining the injury. The wide receiver will officially not be suiting up for Monday's game, leaving Darius Cooper to be the No. 4 wide receiver behind DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon.

headline: Brown (ankle) did not participate in Friday's practice.
story: Brown appeared on Friday's practice report as a DNP. The wide receiver appears to be dealing with an ankle injury, though the severity of the issue remains unclear. If Brown is unable to practice in any capacity Saturday, the chances of the 29-year-old suiting up for Monday night's game against the Bears will be very slim.

headline: Brown was active but did not play in the Eagles' 24-22 win over the Commanders on Sunday.
story: Brown signed a one-year contract with Philadelphia in March after notching 49 catches for 587 yards and five scores over 16 regular-season contests with Kansas City in 2025. It's unclear why the wide receiver didn't play Week 1, and he'll look to make his regular-season debut with the Eagles in Week 2 versus Tennessee.

headline: Cooper caught two of six targets for 19 yards Sunday in a Week 8 loss to Washington.
story: Both of Cooper's catches came in the first half -- he didn't haul in any of his three targets in the second half. The second-year wideout led Eagles wideouts with 66 offensive snaps and finished second with the six targets, but it didn't amount to much production, as he couldn't form much of a connection with QB Tanner McKee. Despite an elevated role due to injuries to DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) the past two weeks, Cooper has just three catches for 36 yards in that span, making him an unappealing fantasy option.

headline: Cooper caught one of three passes for 17 yards during the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday.
story: With both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) sidelined, the Eagles' wide receiver group was led by Cooper, rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown during Monday's contest. Cooper led the position group with 61 offensive snaps, but he only had a 17-yard catch to show for it, which he logged on the Eagles' final play of the first quarter. He has only two catches on five targets for 26 yards over his last two games, and his profile as a boom-or-bust touchdown option in fantasy is severely hampered with Tanner McKee under center instead of Jalen Hurts (calf, IR). The Eagles will hit the road for Week 8 against the Commanders on Sunday.

headline: Cooper caught one of two targets for nine yards and added 38 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 25-14 loss to the Panthers.
story: Cooper saw his offensive workload decrease with the return of DeVonta Smith in Week 6, and, as a result, this was the first time he's failed to reel in multiple passes since Week 3. With Smith, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon all active, Cooper's ceiling will be limited from a fantasy perspective moving forward.

headline: Cooper caught two of three targets for 71 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
story: Cooper was able to reach paydirt again Sunday, securing a 62-yard touchdown on a deep pass from quarterback Jalen Hurts in the second quarter. The wide receiver has taken advantage of a larger workload in the last two weeks with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) sidelined, reeling in five of 10 targets for 104 yards and three touchdowns in Smith's absence. On the year, Cooper has caught seven of 13 targets for 137 yards and four scores over five contests.

headline: Cooper caught three of seven targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
story: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dallas Goedert (knee) out versus Los Angeles, Cooper actually led the Eagles in targets and receiving yards while securing both of Jalen Hurts' touchdowns. Each score was of the red-zone variety. Despite carrying a 20-10 lead into halftime, Philly was unable to do anything on the scoreboard after the break. Cooper is unlikely to have much fantasy appeal moving forward if Smith is able to return next Sunday against Jacksonville.

headline: Cooper caught two of three targets for 26 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles' 24-20 win over the Titans on Sunday.
story: With Dallas Goedert (knee) going down early in the game, Cooper played 31 offensive snaps as the No. 4 receiver after logging just eight in Week 1 against the Commanders. Cooper responded to the increased playing time by breaking free in the back of the end zone with nine seconds left in the fourth quarter to catch the game-winning three-yard touchdown from Jalen Hurts. Cooper doesn't carry much value in redraft fantasy leagues and would need an injury or two ahead of him at the position for that to change.

headline: Jones (shoulder) is not listed on the injury report Wednesday.
story: Jones' omission from the injury report is a positive sign regarding his availability for the Week 1 meeting with the Commanders. The 32-year-old agreed to a one-year deal with the Eagles in March after garnering 41 total tackles and 1.0 sacks in 12 regular-season games with Washington in 2025.

headline: Covey (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
story: Covey was unable to practice all week due to a knee injury that he sustained during the opening kickoff of Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys. With Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) on injured reserve, Elijah Mitchell figures to handle most of the return duties in the absence of Covey, whose next chance to play is Week 9 against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Covey (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday's contest versus the Cowboys.
story: Covey appeared to injure his knee during the opening kickoff Monday, and Philadelphia will now have to finish the game without him. All of his snaps so far this season have come on special teams, and Elijah Moore and Dameon Pierce are the next men up in the return game for the Eagles.

headline: Covey (knee) is questionable to return to Monday's game against the Cowboys.
story: Covey appeared to sustain the injury on the game's opening kickoff, which he returned for 18 yards, and he's being monitored by medical staff to determine whether he can re-enter Monday's contest. Elijah Moore and Dameon Pierce will serve as the Eagles' returners on punts and kickoffs for as long as Covey is out of the game.

headline: The Eagles signed Covey to the active roster Tuesday, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
story: Covey returned four punts for 37 yards in Sunday's 24-22 win over the Commanders. The wide receiver's production on special teams has now earned him a spot on the 53-man roster. It remains to be seen if Covey has earned additional responsibilities for next Sunday's game against the Titans.

headline: Covey reverted to the Eagles' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Covey saw six special-teams snaps the Eagles' win over the Commanders on Sunday, returning four punts for 37 yards. While Covey's average of 9.3 yards per punt return was impressive, it remains to be seen if he'll be elevated for a Week 2 road matchup against the Titans.

headline: The Eagles elevated Covey from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
story: With the entirety of the Eagles' wide receiver corps healthy, Covey was likely elevated for his value on special teams. There is a good chance Covey takes punt and kick return reps away from Makai Lemon and Will Shipley, keeping the wide receiver and running back fresh for offensive possessions.

headline: Stowers caught all three targets for 53 yards in Sunday night's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
story: It was just the rookie's second game of the season after he debuted in Week 7 against Dallas. Stowers played on just 18.8 percent of the snaps against Washington, but he could earn more playing time by producing big plays when given the chance. In what's looking like a lost season for Philly, Stowers could be someone to stash in deeper fantasy leagues, especially if the Eagles trade Dallas Goedert ahead of next week's deadline.

headline: Stowers failed to haul in his lone target during Monday's 38-21 loss to Dallas.
story: The rookie second-rounder was activated from injured reserve ahead of Monday's contest after missing the first six games of the regular season due to quad and hamstring injuries that he picked up during training camp. He played a total of 21 snaps (12 on offense, nine on special teams) in his NFL debut, but his lone target from Tanner McKee came within the last two minutes of the fourth quarter, when the game was well out of reach for Philadelphia. Stowers will likely be limited to TE3 duties behind Dallas Goedert and Johnny Mundt for the time being.

headline: The Eagles reinstated Stowers (quadriceps/hamstring) from injured reserve ahead of Monday's game against the Cowboys.
story: Philadelphia had listed Stowers as questionable for the contest, but after bringing him back from IR, the rookie second-round pick out of Vanderbilt will be available to make his NFL debut after sitting out the team's first six games of the season. With Grant Calcaterra (back) also being reinstated from IR, the Eagles now have four tight ends on the 53-man roster. Dallas Goedert should be locked into a sizable snap share as the Eagles' starting tight end, while Calcaterra and Johnny Mundt function mainly as blockers at the position and Stowers provides more of a pass-catching presence. Stowers' receiving skills could come in handy while the Eagles are down their top two wideouts in DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) on Monday.

headline: Stowers (quadriceps), who is on injured reserve, is officially questionable to play Monday against Dallas.
story: After being drafted in the second round of April's NFL Draft, Stowers hurt his hamstring during preseason play and began the campaign on IR. The Eagles opened his 21-day practice window Oct. 14, and the rookie practiced in full all three days this week. Both Stowers and fellow tight end Grant Calcaterra (back) could be ready to return from IR ahead of Monday's matchup, but for that to happen, they'd need to be activated to the 53-man roster at some point this weekend.

headline: Stowers (quadriceps) was a full participant at the Eagles' practice Thursday.
story: Stowers has been on injured reserve since Sept. 12 while recovering from hamstring and quadriceps injuries. The tight end had his 21-day practice window opened Oct. 14, and his ability to open the week with a full practice is a good sign for his chances to return to action Monday night against Dallas.

headline: The Eagles have downgraded Stowers (quadriceps) to out for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Stowers will have to wait at least another week before making his regular-season NFL debut after he had his 21-day practice window opened earlier this week. Stowers should see snaps as a catch-first tight end behind Dallas Goedert once he's ready to return to game action.

headline: Stowers (quadriceps) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: The rookie second-rounder was placed on injured reserve prior to Week 1 due to a quadriceps injury. He opened Week 6 prep with back-to-back limited practices before logging a full session Friday, but he won't be eligible to make his NFL debut unless he's activated from IR on Saturday.

headline: Stowers (quadriceps) was a limited participant at the Eagles' practice Wednesday.
story: Stowers officially made his return to practice Wednesday as continues to recover from a quadriceps injury that has sidelined him for the first five weeks of the 2026 campaign. The tight end was previously also dealing with a hamstring issue, but he appears to have moved past that injury. Stowers will have two more chances to log a full practice before potentially making his NFL regular-season debut against the Panthers on Sunday.

headline: The Eagles opened the 21-day practice window for Stowers (quadriceps/hamstring) on Wednesday.
story: Stowers has yet to play this season while tending to multiple injuries. While he still has some hurdles to clear, it appears he has a shot to suit up in Week 6 versus Carolina or Week 7 against Dallas.

headline: The Eagles placed Stowers (quadriceps/hamstring) on injured reserve Saturday.
story: Stowers has been dealing with a hamstring injury since at least Aug. 24, which limited him in all three Week 1 practices before the Eagles tabbed him as questionable for Sunday's season opener against the Commanders. At the same time the team placed him on IR, he was ruled out with not only the hamstring issue but a quad concern. The rookie second-round pick thus will miss at least the first four games of the campaign, allowing Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins to handle the TE reps that don't go to No. 1 option Dallas Goedert.

headline: Stowers (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus the Commanders.
story: Stowers is about two-and-a-half weeks removed from picking up a hamstring injury, but his ability to log three straight limited sessions this week has put him in position to make his pro debut Sunday. Ultimately, his status will become known, one way or another, about 90 minutes before a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Stowers (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
story: Stowers emerged from preseason Week 2 with a hamstring injury, which sidelined him until this Wednesday. So far during Week 1 prep, the rookie second-round pick has logged back-to-back capped sessions, but even if he's cleared of his health concern ahead of the Eagles' season opener against the Commanders this Sunday, there's a chance he's a healthy scratch, as Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reported on Aug. 26. In such a scenario, Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins would be the available tight ends behind starter Dallas Goedert.

headline: Stowers (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: The rookie second-rounder has been working through a hamstring injury since the tail end of training camp, which prevented him from playing in the Eagles' preseason finale against the Bengals on Aug. 28. Stowers will have two more opportunities to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation for Sunday's regular-season opener against the Commanders. The Vanderbilt product figures to operate in a depth role at tight end this season behind Dallas Goedert, with Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins also in the mix for snaps on offense.

headline: Blue caught his lone target for nine yards in Sunday night's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
story: It was the running back's first action of the regular season after he was signed to the active roster last week. Blue logged eight offensive snaps and sits behind Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell on the depth chart. With Tank Bigsby (IR, abdomen) likely due back in the near future, Blue's stay on the 53-man roster could be short.

headline: The Eagles signed Blue from the practice squad to the active roster Wednesday.
story: Yet another Eagles RB landed on IR on Wednesday, with Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) joining Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and Will Shipley (foot). Blue thus was called up as a reinforcement and could be in line for a decent amount of work right away with Saquon Barkley (back) dealing with another health concern. Blue hasn't played in 2026 but turned 38 carries into 129 yards and one touchdown to go with one catch (on one target) for five yards in five appearances as a rookie fifth-rounder for the Cowboys last season.

headline: Blue was signed to the Eagles' practice squad Thursday.
story: Blue was waived by Philadelphia on Tuesday, but he has now returned as a member of the team's practice unit. The running back was active for the team's Week 6 loss to the Panthers, but he did not appear in the contest. Blue will now look to earn an elevation to the active roster again this season.

headline: The Eagles have waived Blue.
story: In addition to Blue being let go Tuesday, the Eagles waived Carson Steele (undisclosed) with an injury designation, while Elijah Mitchell was signed to the team's practice squad. For now, Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Dameon Pierce are the only two running backs on Philadelphia's active roster.

headline: Blue did not play in Sunday's 25-14 loss to the Panthers.
story: Blue was signed to the Eagles' active roster ahead of Week 6, but the running back did not appear in the team's loss. Dameon Pierce handled all 12 of the team's carries and caught four of five targets for 15 yards while operating as the team's primary option in the backfield. If Saquon Barkley (hamstring) remains sidelined in Week 7, Blue will likely get another shot to make his Eagles debut versus Dallas.

headline: The Eagles signed Blue off the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
story: With Saquon Barkley (hamstring), Will Shipley (foot) and Tank Bigsby (abdomen) all injured and sidelined, Blue joins Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele as the Eagles' healthy running backs. Blue appeared in five games with Dallas as a rookie last regular season, rushing 38 times for 129 yards and a touchdown.

headline: Mitchell reverted to the Eagles' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Mitchell was heavily involved in Philadelphia's loss at Washington in Week 8, carrying the ball 11 times for 34 yards and adding four catches on six targets for three yards. Starter Saquon Barkley was in and out of Sunday's contest with a back injury, and he was less effective than Mitchell as a rusher. Mitchell can be elevated from the practice squad once more this season before the Eagles would have to sign him to the active roster for him to be allowed to suit up for regular-season games.

headline: Mitchell rushed 11 times for 34 yards and caught four of six targets for three yards in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
story: Mitchell led the team in rushing yards while notching two fewer carries than Saquon Barkley, who was in and out of the game while playing through a back injury. Jaydon Blue, whom the Eagles signed from their practice squad Wednesday, contributed primarily as a special-teams kickoff returner while notching one catch and no carries. Mitchell has been elevated from the practice squad for each of Philadelphia's last two games, so he'll be eligible for one more elevation in Week 9 against the Giants before the Eagles have to sign him to the active roster to keep using him on game days.

headline: The Eagles elevated Mitchell from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
story: It's the second consecutive week in which Mitchell has been elevated to the Eagles' 53-man roster. He was the RB3 against the Cowboys in Week 7, and he'll reprise that depth role with Jaydon Blue behind Saquon Barkley for Sunday's game against the Commanders. Mitchell turned three carries into 11 yards and added three catches on four targets for 23 yards during Philadelphia's 38-21 loss to Dallas.

headline: Mitchell reverted to the Eagles' practice squad Tuesday.
story: Mitchell is a prime candidate for promotion or elevation to the active roster ahead of Sunday's game against the Commanders. The running back played 14 offensive snaps in Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys, logging three carries for 11 yards in the contest. With Saquon Barkley (back) banged up and Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) landing on injured reserve, Mitchell could be in line for a meaningful role Week 8.

headline: The Eagles elevated Mitchell from the practice squad ahead of Monday night's game against Dallas.
story: Mitchell figures to operate as the RB3 behind Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Dameon Pierce. Mitchell has appeared in just one regular-season game since the 2023 season.

headline: Mitchell was signed to the Eagles' practice squad Tuesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Mitchell will return to Philadelphia after reaching an injury settlement with the team in August. The running back appears to have fully recovered from his undisclosed injury, and he'll now have a chance to prove himself and potentially earn an elevation to the active roster down the road. The Eagles waived both Jaydon Blue and Carson Steele (shoulder) on Tuesday, and Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is still less than 100 percent, so Dameon Pierce is currently their only healthy option in the backfield. If Mitchell can get up to speed in time, there is a good chance he will be elevated to play in Monday night's matchup with the Cowboys.

headline: Lemon caught six of nine targets for 57 yards in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
story: Lemon has stepped up as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 receiver in the ongoing absences of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). After setting career highs across the board with seven catches for 67 yards and his first NFL touchdown on eight targets in Week 7 against the Cowboys, Lemon led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets Sunday night. The rookie 20th overall pick is building momentum ahead of a Week 9 home game against the Giants, but his target share would likely drop if Smith gains clearance to return.

headline: Lemon will be the Eagles' top wide receiver for a second consecutive game Sunday at Washington due to the absences of both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle).
story: Smith and Wicks have both been held out of practice for the last two weeks while tending to their respective injuries, and they'll both observe Sunday night's NFC East tilt from the sidelines. The Eagles offense has struggled with Tanner McKee under center in place of Jalen Hurts (calf, IR), although Lemon still put together his best game of the season against the Cowboys on Monday, when he caught seven of eight targets for 67 yards and a touchdown. Lemon, Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown will be the Eagles' top wide receivers against a Commanders defense that ranks 29th in the NFL in passing touchdowns allowed (15) and 28th in passing yards allowed per game (254.0)

headline: Lemon brought in seven of eight targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night.
story: Lemon operated as the Eagles' de facto No. 1 receiver on a night where both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were sidelined, and the rookie met the moment by posting career- and team-high figures across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Lemon rounded out his solid performance by recording his first NFL touchdown catch on a four-yard scoring grab with just under six minutes remaining in the third quarter. Lemon could have another opportunity to spearhead the air attack in a Week 8 road matchup against the Commanders on Sunday night, as both Smith and Wicks may be hard-pressed to get healthy enough to suit up for that contest.

headline: Lemon caught three of six targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 25-14 loss to the Panthers.
story: The rookie wideout briefly exited Week 6 with an undisclosed injury but quickly returned and ended up running a team-high 45 routes on Tanner McKee's 49 dropbcks. It still didn't result in much production, as Lemon's six targets were a distant third on the team. The first-round wide receiver has just 18 catches for 127 yards and no touchdowns on 28 targets through six games. He can't be trusted as a fantasy starter headed into next Monday night's game against the Cowboys.

headline: Lemon (undisclosed) returned to Sunday's contest against the Panthers.
story: Lemon visited the sideline tent in the third quarter but was able to reenter the game in the fourth. With Dontayvion Wicks (undisclosed) leaving the game in the final period, Lemon and DeVonta Smith figure to serve as the top WRs available to fill-in QB Tanner McKee the rest of the way.

headline: Lemon entered the medical tent during the third quarter of Sunday's game against the Panthers due to an unspecified injury.
story: The rookie wide receiver had recorded two catches for six yards on five targets prior to checking into the tent. His status for the remainder of the contest is uncertain.

headline: Lemon caught five of seven targets for 43 yards during Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
story: Lemon was able to set new career highs in receptions and receiving yards Sunday, finishing second on the team in targets behind fellow wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (eight). The rookie is slowly coming into his own with Philadelphia, and he's had an opportunity to operate in a more prominent role with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) sidelined for the last two games. Lemon has now caught 15 of 22 targets for 108 yards over the first five contests of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Lemon caught three of six targets for 27 yards during Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
story: Lemon had a chance to step into a more prominent role on offense in the absence of DeVonta Smith (hamstring), but he didn't really see an increase in production. The wide receiver's six targets are a new career high, but he now has registered three or fewer catches in all four games this season while never exceeding 30 receiving yards. Quarterback Jalen Hurts recorded only 93 total passing yards Sunday, so he'll have to be better for Lemon to see an increase in production in Week 5 versus Jacksonville.

headline: Lemon and Dontayvion Wicks will both operate in larger roles against the Rams on Sunday due to the absence of DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Chris McPherson of the Eagles' official site reports.
story: Lemon, a rookie first-rounder, has seen his receiving yards steadily increase over the first three games of the regular season, and with Smith sidelined for at least one week, the former will have the opportunity to establish himself as a go-to target in the passing game for Jalen Hurts. The Rams will be without starting outside cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder), so whomever Los Angeles rolls out as a replacement could be a target that Lemon and the Eagles offense exploits.

headline: Lemon recorded three receptions for 29 yards on four targets in Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears.
story: After taking the field for north of 60 percent of the snaps in both of the Eagles' first two contests, Lemon wasn't a major beneficiary of the absence of tight end Dallas Goedert (knee). Even though the Eagles leaned more heavily on three-wide formations, Lemon saw only a slight uptick in playing time Monday, logging 35 of 50 snaps (70 percent). The rookie first-round pick appears to be little more than a tertiary option in the passing game at this stage of his career, as he's thus far been held to seven catches for 38 yards on nine targets through his first three NFL games.

headline: Lemon caught his lone target for 14 yards while turning one carry into minus-5 yards during the Eagles' 24-20 win over the Titans on Sunday.
story: Lemon recorded minus-5 receiving yards on three catches during his NFL debut against the Commanders in Week 1. He was at least able to stay in the positive against Tennessee with a 14-yard catch on the last play of the third quarter, which moved the chains on third-and-8 and led to a two-yard touchdown run by Tank Bigsby four plays later. Lemon saw his workload in training camp severely limited due to a hamstring injury, so it may take a few weeks for the rookie first-rounder to ramp up his production. That said, with Dallas Goedert set to miss multiple weeks due to a sprained MCL, Lemon could operate in an elevated role in the passing game, starting with the Eagles' Week 3 road tilt against the Bears on Monday, Sept. 28.

headline: Lemon caught three of four targets for minus-five yards in Sunday's 24-22 win over the Commanders.
story: Lemon reeled in a three-yard catch on the team's first possession of the game before later adding a pair of receptions that combined to lose eight yards. The Eagles are operating under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion this season, and they'll look to find more productive ways to get the wide receiver involved Week 2 against the Titans.

headline: Lemon is listed as a starting wide receiver for the Eagles and their top punt returner on the unofficial depth chart released Tuesday, Andrew DiCecco of InsideTheBirds.com reports.
story: The rookie joins DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks as the top three receivers on the depth chart, though Wicks may be prioritized ahead of Lemon in two-wide sets to begin the season. Wicks turned in a strong training camp, while Lemon spent considerable time on the sideline while tending to a hamstring injury. The first-round pick will likely need to impress early in the season before pushing past Wicks as the No. 2 receiver.

headline: Mike Clay: It's hard to trust Dallas Goedert in fantasy
story: Mike Clay: It's hard to trust Dallas Goedert in fantasy

headline: Goedert caught all four of his targets for 30 yards and added a two-yard run in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
story: Goedert has 15 catches for 139 receiving yards in three games since Tanner McKee took over as Philadelphia's starting QB, but the veteran TE has now gone five consecutive appearances without a TD after scoring 13 times in the span of 15 regular-season appearances through Week 1 of this season. Goedert had a ball bounce off his hands for an interception in the second half, but the play was negated by a defensive penalty, removing what would have been the lone blemish on Goedert's otherwise clean, though unimpressive, stat sheet. He'll try to snap his touchdown drought in Week 9 against the Giants.

headline: Goedert secured five of seven targets for 48 yards in the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night.
story: On a night when both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were sidelined, Goedert served as an even more important target than usual. The veteran tight end finished second in all of receptions, receiving yards and targets for the Eagles on the night, and he's now recorded at least five catches in three consecutive games. Goedert has 24 targets over that span as well, and he should remain similarly busy in a Week 8 road matchup against the Commanders on Sunday night.

headline: Goedert (knee) was a full participant in Saturday's practice and does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Cowboys.
story: After opening the week with two missed practices, the veteran tight end returned to full work Saturday, which was enough for him to fade an injury tag for Monday night's contest. Both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have been ruled out, so Goedert and rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon should command the majority of targets from quarterback Tanner McKee. Goedert has a 12-99-0 receiving line on 17 targets over his last two games.

headline: Goedert (knee) said he felt good at Saturday's practice after dealing with inflammation earlier in the week, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: Goedert was back on the practice field Saturday after missing the first two sessions of Week 7 prep while dealing with inflammation in his knee. The Eagles still need to submit their injury designations for Monday's game against the Cowboys, but Goedert noted after Saturday's session that he expects to play, per Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer. The veteran tight end's availability is crucial for Philadelphia, given that both of the team's top wide receivers in DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice all week.

headline: Goedert (knee) is on the field for the start of Saturday's practice, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: Goedert missed the first two practices of Week 7 prep while tending to a knee injury, but he's back on the field and in pads for Saturday's session. The Eagles are also dealing with injuries to DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), so Goedert -- if active for Monday night's game against the Cowboys -- would operate in an expanded role in the passing game if either or both of the Eagles' top two wide receivers is sidelined.

headline: Goedert (knee) was a non-participant at Friday's practice.
story: Goedert has yet to mix into drills this week due to a knee injury, which could be related to the right MCL sprain that sidelined him in Weeks 3 and 4. In any case, how he's listed on Saturday's practice report will provide a sense of his chances to play Monday against the Cowboys.

headline: Goedert (knee) was not seen at Friday's portion of practice open to the media, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
