story: Despite the absence of Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and the premature exit of Mike Evans (Achilles), Cowing went without a catch for the fifth time this season. With neither Samuel nor Evans a lock to suit up in Week 7 versus the Falcons, Cowing might see more snaps alongside Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins. However, that may not be the case if Demarcus Robinson (ankle) can manage to get on the field after spending time on injured reserve since the Week 2 win over Miami.

headline: Cowing failed to corral either of his two targets while playing 17 of the 49ers' 54 snaps on offense in Sunday's 36-30 win over the Cardinals.
story: Even though Demarcus Robinson (ankle) was moved to injured reserve following Week 2 and Mike Evans (rib) was unable to finish Sunday's contest, Cowing didn't benefit from much of a spike in playing time. In fact, after logging 24 of the 49ers' 52 offensive snaps (46.2 percent) in Week 2, Cowing saw his snap share drop to 31.5 percent. The biggest beneficiary of Robinson's absence and Evans' early exit was KhaDarel Hodge, who finished second to only Deebo Samuel (39) among 49ers receivers with 30 snaps.

headline: Cowing returned two punts for 17 yards in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams in Week 1.
story: Cowing also saw five snaps on offense but wasn't' targeted by Brock Purdy. With De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) injured against the Rams and Ricky Pearsall (knee) out for the season, Cowing is looking like the Niners' current WR4 behind Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson.

headline: Cowing (groin) did not appear on the 49ers' injury report Tuesday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Cowing was dealing with a groin injury to end the preseason but he now appears to have fully recovered. The wide receiver is set to operate as a special-teams asset with San Francisco in 2026, handling the primary punt returner role.

headline: James logged a six-yard carry, turned his lone target into an 11-yard catch and registered 119 yards on four kickoff returns during the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday.
story: Most of James' on-field work Sunday came on special teams. Both of his touches on offense happened on back-to-back plays in the second quarter, coinciding with the absence of Christian McCaffrey, the latter of whom was playing through a thigh injury during most of Sunday's contest. The only way James would see consistent playing time on offense is if one of McCaffrey or rookie Kaelon Black were to miss time. The 49ers will get some additional rest thanks to the Week 8 bye, and their next game takes place Week 9 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: James (coach's decision) is inactive against Denver on Sunday.
story: The second-year pro will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines while the 49ers roll with two active running backs in Christian McCaffrey and rookie Kaelon Black. James' next chance to play is Week 5 against the Seahawks on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: James saw four carries for 15 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
story: James saw eight offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in the contest. All of the running back's carries came in the final seven minutes of the fourth quarter when the game was all but over.

headline: James (coach's decision) is officially inactive for Thursday's game against the Rams, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: The 2025 fifth-rounder will not suit up in Week 1, leaving Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black as the only healthy running backs active for the 49ers on Thursday. James' role moving forward may depend on how effective Black is to start the season.

headline: Stout (shoulder) was only active as an emergency depth option during Sunday's loss to the Falcons, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reported Monday.
story: Coach Kyle Shanahan said that Stout was only going to enter the game in an emergency scenario for the 49ers' secondary. The team hopes the Week 8 bye will allow Stout's shoulder sprain to fully heal ahead of the Week 9 showdown with the Raiders.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site reports.
story: Stout is nursing an AC sprain in his shoulder, but the second-year defensive back has been given the green light to play in Sunday's contest. He has 18 tackles (11 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one pass defense through the first six games of the regular season.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
story: Stout logged consecutive DNPs to begin Week 7 prep before upgrading to a limited participant in Friday's session. The last-minute practice participation has given the cornerback a chance to recover from his AC joint issue in time for Sunday's contest, but it remains uncertain if the 24-year-old will suit up. If Stout cannot play, Ashtyn Davis will likely start at slot cornerback in his place.

headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said that Stout's removal from Monday's 23-17 win over the Commanders was due to an AC sprain in his shoulder, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
story: Stout's practice reps during Week 6 prep were limited due to his shoulder injury. He was cleared to play Monday but was hampered by his injury, which led to Stout being replaced by Ashtyn Davis in the second half and finishing with two tackles over a season-low 25 snaps. Stout's practice participation over the coming days will provide some clarity on his status for Sunday's road game against the Falcons.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is active for Monday night's game against the Commanders, Brooke Evans reports.
story: Stout was limited throughout Week 6 prep with a shoulder injury he sustained in the 49ers' Week 4 win over the Broncos. The cornerback has recovered enough to suit up for Monday Night Football opposite fellow cornerback Renardo Green.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is questionable for Monday night's game against the Commanders.
story: Stout was limited in practice all week after he initially injured the shoulder in Week 4 against the Broncos. He's yet to miss a game this season. Across five appearances, the cornerback has 16 tackles (nine solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one pass breakup.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site reports.
story: Stout missed Friday's practice session due to an AC joint sprain the cornerback suffered during the 49ers' Week 4 win over the Broncos. Despite missing the final practice of Week 5 prep, Stout was able to recover enough from the injury to suit up for Sunday's divisional matchup with the Seahawks.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: Stout is day-to-day with an AC joint sprain. The cornerback practiced in a limited capacity Thursday while missing the 49ers' Wednesday and Friday sessions. Stout has an outside chance to play in Sunday's contest, but with one limited practice session during the middle of the week, it is unlikely. If Stout does not play, Ephesians Prysock, Siran Neal or Jack Jones will likely start at slot cornerback against the Seahawks.

headline: San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that Stout is day-to-day with an AC joint sprain in his shoulder, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
story: Stout missed time during the fourth quarter of Sunday's 24-14 win over the Broncos due to the shoulder issue, but he was able to check back into the game after receiving treatment. Though his practice participation could be affected by the injury in Week 5, the expectation is that he'll be ready to play this coming Sunday in Seattle.

headline: Stout (shoulder) returned to Sunday's game against the Broncos, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: Stout briefly missed time in the fourth quarter with the shoulder issue. He has six tackles (four solo) in Sunday's game against Denver.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Broncos, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: With Stout injured, Jack Jones is the only other healthy cornerback on the roster behind Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir. Prior to exiting Sunday, Stout recorded six tackles (four solo). He handles slot cornerback duties for the Niners.

headline: Stout (hip) was a full participant at the 49ers' practice Tuesday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Stout was dealing with a hip injury late in the preseason but he now appears to be back to full health ahead of Week 1. The 24-year-old is slated to operate as the team's primary slot cornerback this season, and he'll get a tough test against the Rams on Thursday night.

headline: Rourke (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: Rourke is inactive but will not be the emergency third quarterback for the 49ers. The team seems content with Brock Purdy and Mac Jones and does not appear to need the "break-glass" button that the 49ers themselves voted to add during the 2023 offseason.

headline: Rourke (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Dolphins but will serve as the emergency third quarterback.
story: As the emergency third quarterback, Rourke is not allowed to play Sunday unless both starter Brock Purdy and backup Mac Jones were to leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Rourke (ribs) did not appear on the 49ers' injury report Tuesday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Rourke has fully recovered from the ribs injury that he suffered during the preseason. He will now be good to go for Thursday night's regular-season opener against the Rams in Australia.

headline: Purdy completed 27 of 40 passes for 288 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions and added two carries for five yards in the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday.
story: Purdy put together an impressive passing yardage total, especially considering he was down both Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), along with De'Zhaun Stribling (IR, ankle) and Demarcus Robinson (IR, ankle). He also lost Christian McCaffrey for the entirety of the second quarter due to a leg injury that the star back eventually returned from, but the scarcity of his top pass catchers eventually led to a more mistake-filled performance than usual. The multi-interception tally was Purdy's first of the season, and the two picks led to 10 points for the Falcons. Purdy should have a chance to work with a deeper pass-catching corps in a Week 9 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8, as the Week 8 bye should offer multiple receivers a chance to recover from their respective injuries.

headline: Purdy completed 21 of 29 passes for 264 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions while adding five rushes for 28 yards in the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday night.
story: Purdy took multiple sacks for the second straight game after not being taken down over the first four contests, but the veteran signal-caller otherwise had a mostly clean night that included a robust average of 9.1 yards per attempt. Purdy's passing yardage total also was his third highest of the campaign, and he kept his season-long touchdown-pass streak alive when he connected with George Kittle on an 11-yard scoring strike to cap off the opening drive of the night. Purdy completed passes to seven different targets overall, and he now boasts a 14:2 TD:INT heading into a Week 7 road matchup against the Falcons on Sunday.

headline: Purdy completed 19 of 29 passes for 189 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 32-29 win over the Seahawks. He also rushed five times for six yards and threw a successful two-point conversion.
story: Seattle's talented defense made life tougher for Purdy than it had been up to this point, as he committed his first turnover since Week 1 and took his first three sacks of the season. Purdy nonetheless did enough to keep the 49ers undefeated. He threw a two-yard touchdown pass to Mike Evans in the first quarter and a seven-yard touchdown pass to Brandin Cooks in the fourth, the latter of which Purdy followed up with a two-point conversion to Evans. The Seahawks responded with a field goal to tie the game at 29-29, but Purdy led the 49ers into position for Eddy Pineiro's go-ahead 44-yard field goal with 1:56 remaining. San Francisco's defense delivered the game-winning stop as Purdy and the 49ers improved to 5-0 heading into a Week 6 MNF home game against the Commanders.

headline: Purdy completed 19 of 30 passes for 218 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while adding 10 carries for 29 yards in the 49ers' 24-14 win over the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Purdy performed admirably against a tough Broncos defense, and his legs helped him to yet another sack-free afternoon despite the challenge posted by Denver's aggressive unit. Purdy didn't fire his first touchdown pass of the day until the 4:15 mark of the third quarter, hitting Deebo Samuel from one yard out to snap a 3-3 tie. The veteran signal-caller then sealed San Francisco's victory with a 56-yard scoring strike to George Kittle just before the two-minute warning, and Purdy remained free of interceptions for the third straight game. Purdy has a league-leading 11 touchdown passes and has yet to be brought down through four games, but he'll have a stiff challenge on his hands in a Week 5 road matchup against the Seahawks next Sunday.

headline: Purdy completed 15 of 27 passes for 297 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed twice for 34 yards in the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Purdy's completion percentage was below his usual standards, but the fifth-year signal-caller more than made up for it with some effective downfield passing and his quartet of scoring tosses. His yardage total also got a boost from an 80-yard hook-and-lateral play in the first quarter between Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel that the latter took all the way to the house from San Francisco's 20-yard line, which served as the quarterback's first touchdown pass of the day. Purdy would go on to connect with Evans (23 yards) and George Kittle (10 and 20 yards) for his other three scoring tosses, with the final one of those coming two plays after a holding penalty on the talented tight end nullified a winding 45-yard touchdown run by the athletic quarterback. Purdy now boasts a 9:1 TD:INT and 789 passing yards over his first three games heading into a tough Week 4 home showdown against the Broncos next Sunday.

headline: Purdy completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins. He also rushed three times for 30 yards and a touchdown.
story: Purdy was in complete command of the offense throughout Sunday's lopsided win, throwing only two incompletions while finishing as the team's leading rusher for the cherry on top. The 49ers have been one of the league's best teams in the early going, outscoring the Rams and Dolphins by a combined margin of 62-20 heading into a Week 3 home game against the Cardinals. Purdy has contributed six total touchdowns during this hot start, including third-quarter touchdown passes of 12 yards to George Kittle and six yards to Kyle Juszczyk against the Dolphins following Purdy's two-yard touchdown run in the second quarter.

headline: Purdy completed 25 of 34 passes for 205 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding five rushes for 29 yards during the 49ers' 27-7 Week 1 win over the Rams in Melbourne, Australia.
story: After an offseason in which the Rams' fearsome pass rush garnered plenty of headlines, Purdy navigated the season-opening matchup against his talented NFC West rival in nearly flawless fashion. The fifth-year signal-caller got off to a fast start with new No. 1 receiver Mike Evans, connecting with him on three occasions for 22 yards during a 15-play opening drive that culminated in a field goal. Purdy went on to hit Evans for a contested two-yard scoring strike early in the third quarter, and he sandwiched impressive touchdown tosses to Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel of 39 and 15 yards, respectively, around that play. Purdy's early second-quarter interception on a pass intended for George Kittle did lead to the Rams' only touchdown, but as the final numbers indicate, the veteran quarterback did more than enough to atone. Purdy should have a strong chance of carrying over the season-opening momentum into Week 2, as a home date with what's expected to be a vulnerable Dolphins defense awaits on Sunday, Sept. 20.

headline: Juszczyk caught all three of his targets for 11 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 29-20 loss to Atlanta.
story: Juszczyk garnered multiple targets for the fifth straight game that he's played in, and he was able to reach paydirt for the second time this season, reeling in a one-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy in the fourth quarter. The fullback has yet to log a carry this season, and he's caught eight of 11 targets for 76 yards and two touchdowns over six contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Juszczyk (knee) was a full participant in Friday's practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
story: Juszczyk was cleared to practice without restriction Friday after being limited in Thursday's session. The full practice designation indicates that the veteran fullback has fully recovered from a knee injury and will play against the Commanders on Monday.

headline: Juszczyk (knee) will be limited at Thursday's practice, head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters Thursday, Cam Inman of Bay Area News Group reports.
story: Juszczyk sat out San Francisco's Week 5 win over the Seahawks after injuring his knee in the Week 4 win over the Broncos. The standout fullback is ramping up in his recovery, but it's too early to say at this point if he will be available for Monday's game against the Commanders.

headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that Juszczyk (knee) could return for the Week 6 matchup against the Commanders next Monday night, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
story: Juszczyk's practice participation during Week 6 prep will ultimately determine whether the veteran fullback will return from a one-game absence due to a knee injury he sustained during the 49ers' Week 4 win over the Broncos. The 49ers will continue to rely on tight ends like Brayden Willis for more snaps as blockers in Juszczyk's absence.

headline: San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that Juszczyk will miss multiple weeks after hyperextending and sustaining a bone bruise to his right knee in Sunday's 24-14 win over the Broncos, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
story: The veteran fullback can be safely ruled out for Sunday's game in Seattle, and while he appears likely to avoid a stint on injured reserve, he could be at risk of missing additional games beyond Week 5. Through the 49ers' first four games, Juszczyk has recorded four receptions for 55 yards and a touchdown on six targets while also filling a key blocking role.

headline: Juszczyk is believed to have sustained a sprained right knee in Sunday's 24-14 win over the Broncos and is likely to miss "several weeks," Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Juszczyk recorded two catches for 28 yards on two targets before exiting early in the fourth quarter with the knee injury. Early evaluations of the fullback's knee have left the 49ers confident that his ACL is intact, but he'll undergo an MRI on Monday to provide more clarity on the extent of his injury. In any case, the 49ers seem to be bracing for Juszczyk to miss multiple weeks, with a stint on injured reserve potentially being on the table. While not typically a major part of the San Francisco passing attack, Juszczyk handles a critical role as a blocker, and his absence for any length of time may have negative consequences on the overall health of the offense.

headline: Juszczyk (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Broncos, Eric Branch of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
story: Juszczyk was injured at the end of a catch in the second half when he was chopped down at his knees on a tackle. Prior to departing, Juszczyk caught both of his targets for 28 yards.

headline: Juszczyk exited Sunday's contest against the Broncos in the fourth quarter with a leg injury, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: Juszczyk suffered the injury after reeling in a pass and gaining 16 yards before taking a blow to his right knee area with 14:03 left in the fourth quarter. The fullback's status for the remainder of the game is now uncertain.

headline: Juszczyk recorded two catches on two targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's win over the Dolphins.
story: Juszczyk madę the start and played just over 50 percent of the offensive snaps. The 35-year-old veteran is in his 14th NFL season but doesn't carry much, if any, fantasy value in redraft formats as a lead blocker.

headline: Juszczyk (finger) does not have an injury designation for Thursday's game against the Rams, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Juszczyk was a limited participant in Tuesday's session as he dealt with the finger issue he sustained in early August. The fullback is healthy and all set to block for Christian McCaffrey in the Week 1 divisional showdown with the Rams taking place in Melbourne, Australia.

headline: Juszczyk (finger) was a limited participant at the 49ers' practice Tuesday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Juszczyk has been dealing with a finger injury since early August and he still appears to be recovering from the injury. His ability to participate in a limited capacity Tuesday is a good sign, but he can erase any doubt about his availability for Thursday night's matchup against the Rams by logging a full practice Wednesday.

headline: Pineiro did not attempt a field goal while going 2-for-3 on PATs in Sunday's 26-20 loss to the Falcons.
story: Pineiro went without a field-goal try for the second time this season, and he hasn't made multiple field goals in a contest since Week 1. To make matters worse, the kicker missed an extra-point try for the second straight week, and he's now 21-for-25 on PATs over the first seven games this season. With the 49ers off next week, Pineiro's next chance to be more involved will come in Week 9 against the Raiders.

headline: Pineiro made his lone field-goal attempt and went 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday.
story: Pineiro's extra-point try late in the first quarter missed wide to the right, but he connected on a 33-yard field goal late in the third quarter to give the 49ers a 23-3 lead. Through six regular-season games, the veteran kicker has gone 6-for-9 on field-goal attempts and 19-for-22 on extra-point tries. He hasn't been the most accurate kicker, but Pineiro's scoring floor will remain elevated with a 49ers team that ranks third in the NFL in points per game (29.5) and ninth in yards per game (366.7).

headline: Pineiro went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his extra-point tries during the 49ers' 32-29 win over the Seahawks on Sunday.
story: Pineiro's 52-yard field-goal try early in the third quarter went wide left, but he made up for that miss with a 44-yard field goal late in the fourth in what ended up being the game-winning kick for the 49ers. The veteran kicker has gone 5-for-8 on field-goal attempts through the first five games of the regular season, although each of those misses have come from 50-plus yards. Pineiro is also 17-for-19 on extra-point tries, and those 17 made PATs are second-most in the NFL behind Jake Bates (20). The 49ers will head back to San Francisco for Week 6 to host the Commanders on Monday, Oct. 19.

headline: Pineiro went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his PATs during Sunday's 24-14 win over Denver.
story: Pineiro made his first field-goal try of the day in the second quarter, converting a 24-yard chip shot. The kicker later had a 54-yard attempt blocked by the Broncos, tagging him with his second missed field-goal attempt of the year. Pineiro has now gone 4-for-6 on field-goal tries, including 2-for-4 from 50-plus yards, while also converting 14 of 16 extra-point attempts over four contests so far in 2026.

headline: Pineiro connected on a 57-yard field-goal try and went three-of-five on extra-point attempts in Sunday's 36-30 win over the Cardinals.
story: Pineiro had not missed an extra point in 2026 coming into Sunday. He has nonetheless made 11 through three contests, so he's getting regular scoring opportunities in the 49ers' high-powered offense.

headline: Pineiro did not have any field-goal tries but converted on all five of his extra-point attempts during Sunday's 35-13 win versus the Dolphins.
story: In a game where Miami's defense was picked apart by quarterback Brock Purdy, Pineiro's services were barely needed. San Francisco is off to a scorching start in 2026, and there's not much reason to think the Cardinals defense will be the one to slow the momentum Week 3.

headline: Pineiro (illness) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Pineiro drew the questionable tag due to an illness, but he's been cleared to play in Sunday's home opener. He went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and connected on all three of his extra-point tries during the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams.

headline: Pineiro (illness) is expected to be active Sunday against the Dolphins, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: The 49ers ended up trying out two kickers Saturday -- Greg Joseph and Younghoe Koo -- but won't sign either of them to the practice squad, meaning Pineiro will handle his normal placekicking duties in Week 2. In 15 regular-season games with San Francisco going back to the 2025 campaign, Pineiro has netted 30 of 32 field-goal attempts and 37 of 41 point-after tries.

headline: Pineiro (illness) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
story: Pineiro has been battling an illness during Week 2 prep and thus is in danger of sitting out Sunday. Coach Kyle Shanahan told Matt Barrows of The Athletic on Friday that the 49ers will sign a kicker to the practice squad and then elevate him in the event Pineiro isn't able to play this weekend, but who that kicker may be isn't known.

headline: Pineiro (illness) was a non-participant at the 49ers' practice Thursday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Pineiro has missed consecutive practices to open the week as he battles an illness, and his status for Sunday's matchup against Miami remains in question. The 31-year-old will have one more chance to practice Friday. If he can't go this week, San Francisco will have to sign a free agent to handle the team's starting kicker role for Week 2.

headline: Pineiro (illness) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: It's not clear exactly what kind of sickness Pineiro is dealing with, but he does have until Sunday to get better. His status will still be worth keeping an eye on when San Francisco publishes its Thursday and Friday injury reports, as the team does not carry another kicker on its active roster or its practice squad.

headline: Pineiro converted two of his three field-goal attempts and all three of his extra-point tries in the 49ers' season-opening 27-7 win against the Rams.
story: Pineiro opened the scoring with a chip-shot 20-yard FG in the first quarter. His second field goal was much more difficult, as he nailed a 56-yarder early in the fourth. Pineiro had one more FG try, but he hit the right upright on a 52-yard attempt late in the fourth quarter with the game essentially in the bag for San Francisco. All in all, it was a successful season opener for the veteran kicker, whose six field goals from 50-plus yards out last season marked a career high. San Francisco's offense looked to be in good form against a tough Rams defense Thursday, so Pineiro could be in for plenty of opportunities in 2026.

headline: Watkins brought in three of six targets for 56 yards in the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday.
story: With the 49ers' receiving corps down all of Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), De'Zhaun Stribling (IR, ankle) and Demarcus Robinson (IR, ankle), Watkins saw an expanded role and made good use of the opportunity. All three of Watkins' catches went for first downs, and he finished third on the team in receiving yards and targets while also tying for that slotting in receptions. The 2025 fourth-round pick's performance was encouraging, but he's likely to slide back down the depth chart since the wide-receiver room could be much healthier by the time San Francisco returns to action against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8, following the Week 8 bye.

headline: Watkins could take on a significant role Sunday against Atlanta with Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) both sidelined, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site reports.
story: Watkins already saw a big jump in participation this past Monday versus Washington, tallying a season-high 76 percent offensive snap share in Samuel's absence. However, he drew just one target, which he caught for a 22-yard gain. Now that Evans will also be out of action, Watkins seems likely to be deployed often again Sunday, though Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing should also get opportunities to step into larger roles. Finally, Christian Kirk (calf), who is currently on IR, may be activated ahead of the matchup versus Atlanta, and he could also factor into the equation in what would be his 49ers debut.

headline: Watkins caught his lone target for 22 yards during the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday.
story: Watkins connected with Brock Purdy for a big gain early in the second quarter, and all three of wideout's catches this season have gone for 20-plus yards. Watkins' 47 offensive snaps ended up leading all 49ers wide receivers, and the second-year pro's role in the passing game could expand in Week 7 against the Falcons, depending on the availability of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring).

headline: Watkins recorded two receptions for 60 yards on two targets in Sunday's 36-30 win over the Cardinals.
story: Making his 2026 debut after he was a healthy inactive for the 49ers' first two contests, Watkins took the field for 15 of the team's 54 offensive snaps and was able to make a mark with 34- and 26-yard grabs. He still finished fifth among 49ers receivers in playing time, but he could see an uptick in opportunities if the rib strain Mike Evans suffered Sunday prevents him from playing Week 4 against the Broncos.

headline: Watkins (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Watkins will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive game, and his next chance to play is Week 3 against the Cardinals on Sept. 27. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson will lead the 49ers' wide receiver group in Week 2.

headline: Watkins (coach's decision) is officially inactive for Thursday's game against the Rams, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: After flashing during the preseason, Watkins will be a healthy scratch to begin the regular season. Presumably, veterans Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel and rookie second-rounder De'Zhaun Stribling will see the lion's share of the 49ers' snaps at wide receiver in Week 1.

headline: Black rushed 12 times for 63 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of three targets for minus-4 yards in the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday. He also lost a fumble and returned one kickoff for 34 yards.
story: Christian McCaffrey suffered a thigh injury in the opening period that eventually led to him missing the entire second quarter, affording Black expanded opportunity. The rookie made good use of the extra touches, averaging a career-high 5.3 yards per carry and recording his highest rushing yardage total since his Week 1 NFL debut. Black also rang up his first TD as a professional, a 30-yard breakaway run on the first play of the second quarter. However, the rookie made a key mistake when he lost a fumble with San Francisco nearing the red zone in the second quarter. McCaffrey did return to the game for the second half and now has the Week 8 bye to recover, so Black could be back to a more reduced role in a Week 9 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Black rushed eight times for 34 yards and brought in his only target for three yards in the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday night.
story: Black logged half as many carries as Christian McCaffrey and a whopping nine fewer targets, cementing the pecking order in the 49ers' ground attack. However, Black is getting some nice complementary run as a rookie, as he's logged 45 carries over his first six games. Black has just three targets in that same span, however, so his fantasy upside will remain capped to a large degree in a Week 7 road matchup against the Falcons on Sunday.

headline: Black was excused from Saturday's practice to address a personal matter but does not have an injury designation for Monday's Week 6 matchup against Washington, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: Since Black wasn't given an injury designation, his absence from practice Saturday isn't expected to impact his availability Monday. The rookie should thus continue to work as the 49ers' No.2 running back behind Christian McCaffrey. That role hasn't yielded much fruit for Black of late, however, as he's totaled fewer than 20 yards in each of his past three contests.

headline: Black (illness) upgraded to a full practice Thursday, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
story: Black was limited Wednesday but appears to be fine ahead of Sunday's Week 5 date with the Seahawks. The rookie running back has plodded to 2.5 yards per carry over the last three weeks and is merely a bench stash in fantasy as Christian McCaffrey's top backup.

headline: Black (illness) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
story: Black should be fine to handle his normal role Sunday against the Seahawks as Christian McCaffrey's direct backup. The rookie running back has turned 20 carries into just 55 yards (2.75 YPC) over the last three games following a strong Week 1 debut in Australia against the Rams.

headline: Black turned six carries into 13 yards during the 49ers' 24-14 win over the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Black's longest carry of the day went for five yards, with four of his other touches going for two yards or fewer. With Christian McCaffrey clearly leading the backfield, Black's workload will be volatile on a week-to-week basis and dependent on game script. The 49ers will hit the road for Week 5 in an NFC West showdown against the 3-1 Seahawks.

headline: Black turned four carries into 17 yards and failed to haul in his lone target during the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Black accumulated 95 scrimmage yards on 22 touches through the first two games of the season while working behind Christian McCaffrey, but the rookie observed most of Sunday's game from the sidelines, seeing the field for only eight of the 49ers' 54 offensive snaps (14.8 percent). Keeping McCaffrey healthy is a top priority, but Black's workload is likely to remain erratic and dependent on game script. The 49ers will remain home in Week 4 to host the Broncos this Sunday.

headline: Black (groin) rushed seven times for 25 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
story: Black suited up for his second NFL contest after being listed as questionable coming into the game. He actually had two more rushing yards than Christian McCaffrey, but McCaffrey scored two touchdowns on 10 carries and added four catches for 43 yards. Black is poised to continue splitting the rushing workload with CMC in Week 3 against the Cardinals, though McCaffrey remains the preferred option in valuable goal-line and passing situations.

headline: Black (groin) is active for Sunday's Week 2 matchup against the Dolphins, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: The rookie running back was reported to be trending up for Sunday's contest earlier Sunday, and his availability now has been made official. Black will therefore once again serve as the primary backup to Christian McCaffrey, a role that afforded the former 15 touches (14 carries, one reception) across 28 snaps in a Week 1 win over the Rams in Melbourne, Australia.

headline: Black (groin) is on track to play Sunday against the Dolphins, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Black popped up on Thursday's injury report as a limited participant due to a groin injury, and he was given a questionable designation after getting in another limited session Friday. While there is reason to believe he will take the field Sunday, his availability will not be confirmed until the 49ers release their inactives 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Black (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
story: Black made a surprise appearance on Thursday's practice report as limited due to a groin issue, and he wasn't able to do enough Friday to enter the weekend without a designation for Week 2 action. His status may not be confirmed until about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, but if Black is inhibited or sidelined, Jordan James would be the primary reserve RB behind starter Christian McCaffrey.

headline: Black was limited at Thursday's practice due to a groin injury, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Black did not show up on Wednesday's injury report, but he was unable to get a full session in a day later. The extent of his injury is uncertain, but his status will be updated again Friday when the 49ers release their final report before Sunday's matchup with the Dolphins.

headline: Black rushed 14 times for 65 yards and brought in his only target for five yards during the 49ers' 27-7 Week 1 win over the Rams in Melbourne, Australia.
story: The rookie third-round pick opened the season as Christian McCaffrey's primary backup, but he actually ended up outpacing his star backfield mate by four carries as the 49ers progressively took control in the second half. Black earned the touches with multiple productive runs that showed off his explosiveness, and his ability to help keep McCaffrey fresh throughout the game should only help lead to more opportunities for the first-year back going forward. Black garnered the No. 2 job thanks to an impressive two-game preseason where he performed similarly to Week 1, lending credence to the notion the Indiana product could maintain his fantasy relevance, particularly in deeper formats, as his first NFL season unfolds.

headline: Shaheed (knee) did not practice Wednesday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Shaheed missed Monday night's loss to the Bears, which allowed Tory Horton to log a season-high 43 offensive snaps, which he turned into a 3-26-0 receiving line on six targets. Horton would again be in line for WR3 duties if Shaheed needs to sit Sunday against Arizona.

headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Tuesday that Shaheed (knee) has a chance to play Sunday against the Cardinals, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
story: Shaheed was sidelined for the first time all season in Monday's 34-17 loss to the Bears, after his knee injury kept him from practicing throughout the week. In Shaheed's absence, Tory Horton handled elevated snaps as the Seahawks' No. 3 wideout behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp, while George Holani served as the team's top kickoff returner. Shaheed may need to turn in a full practice at some point during Week 9 prep to put himself on track to return to action Sunday.

headline: Shaheed (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bears, Curtis Crabtree of FOX 13 Seattle reports.
story: Shaheed will miss his first game of the 2026 season due to a knee injury that he sustained during the Seahawks' Week 7 win over the Chiefs. Tory Horton and Velus Jones are the top candidates to operate as Seattle's returners on kickoffs and punts, and Horton and Cooper Kupp should see a bump in offensive snaps in Shaheed's absence. Shaheed's next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Shaheed (knee) didn't practice Friday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Shaheed suffered a knee injury in the first half of this past Sunday's win against the Chiefs and wasn't able to return. Since then, head coach Mike Macdonald told Brady Henderson of ESPN.com that the "early returns are positive" on Shaheed, but with no on-field work yet this week he likely will need to mix into drills Saturday to have a chance to play Monday versus the Bears.

headline: Shaheed (knee) did not practice Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Shaheed was injured in last Sunday night's win over the Chiefs, but indications are he avoided a serious injury. If he's unable to play Monday night against the Bears, Tory Horton will slot into WR3 duties behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp.

headline: Shaheed (knee) is unlikely to practice Thursday, Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle reports.
story: Coach Mike Macdonald provided the update Thursday, stating that the wideout is "doing well" but was not quite ready to return to practice. Shaheed exited Sunday's win over the Chiefs with a knee injury, which is not expected to keep him out long-term. He gets an extra day to rehab as the Seahawks get ready for their Monday Night Football matchup with the Bears.

headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that the early returns on Shaheed's knee injury are positive, Brady Henderson reports.
story: Shaheed logged 22 snaps and caught two of his three targets for one yard before exiting Sunday's 20-3 win over the Chiefs. While Macdonald's initial assessment of the wideout's knee issue is encouraging, Shaheed's status will nonetheless be worth monitoring as next Monday's game against the Bears approaches.

headline: Shaheed (knee) won't return to Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Shaheed didn't return after halftime due to a knee injury. The wide receiver and standout special teams return man will have an extra day to recover before the Seahawks face the Bears on MNF in Week 8.

headline: Shaheed (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Curtis Crabtree of FOX 13 Seattle reports.
story: Shaheed didn't come out for the second half, as Tory Horton returned the second-half kickoff in Shaheed's stead. Prior to getting hurt, Shaheed caught two of three targets for one yard while adding a 32-yard punt return.

headline: Shaheed (hip) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Shaheed was limited Wednesday but appears to be on track for his normal role Sunday against the Chiefs. Playing behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp in an offense that likes to use multiple tight ends, Shaheed has yet to get going in the receiving department this season, as he has just 14 catches for 162 yards through six contests.

headline: Shaheed (hip) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Corbin K. Smith of EmeraldCitySpectrum.com reports.
story: It's the first time Shaheed has been listed on the injury report this season. A popular summer breakout candidate, it hasn't yet happened for Shaheed this season, as he has just 14 catches for 162 yards on 27 targets through six games. He's added 39 rushing yards and a touchdown on four carries. Shaheed can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows some sort of reliable floor or even a ceiling performance.

headline: Shaheed brought in five of eight targets for 66 yards, rushed once for two yards, returned three kickoffs for 77 yards and ran back three punts for 39 yards in the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday. He also caught a two-point conversion pass and committed two fumbles, recovering one.
story: Shaheed's extremely busy stat line included season-high totals across all three components of his receiving line. The veteran speedster tied for second in receptions and was the runner-up in receiving yards as well for the Seahawks on the night, but his lost fumble likely cost Seattle points since it was recovered at the Broncos' 34-yard line late in the first half. Shaheed did provide a critical two-point conversion grab after a George Holani fourth-quarter touchdown to bring the Seahawks within three points, and Shaheed also was the intended target on Sam Darnold's interception in overtime that led to Denver's game-winning field goal. Shaheed will carry a modest 14-162-0 line on 27 targets into a Week 7 home showdown with the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: Shaheed caught two of four targets for 23 yards while also adding 86 kickoff-return yards during Sunday's 32-29 loss to the 49ers.
story: Shaheed was held to two or fewer catches for the fourth time in five games, and he has yet to score a touchdown through the air this year. The wide receiver played a season-low 28 offensive snaps in Week 5, and his upside is rather low as a fantasy asset at the moment. On the year, Shaheed has caught nine of 19 targets for 96 yards while adding three carries for 37 yards and a touchdown and 359 yards as a kick returner.

headline: Shaheed caught one of three targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 30-23 win over the Chargers. He added two carries for 33 yards and a touchdown.
story: Shaheed had been mostly nonexistent through the first three games of the season, totaling 57 yards on seven touches, but he was able to break out for a long touchdown in this one, scoring from 28 yards out as a rusher in the second quarter. With Jaxon Smith-Njigba completely dominating the targets in Seattle's passing game, Shaheed has remained a low-floor fantasy option early on in 2026.

headline: Shaheed caught two passes on three targets for 14 yards during the Seahawks' 33-31 loss to the Commanders on Sunday, He also returned three punts for 29 yards and added 63 yards on two kickoff returns.
story: Shaheed continued to operate as the Seahawks' primary return man, and his 31 offensive snaps were third-most among Seattle wide receivers behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (58) and Cooper Kupp (45). Shaheed has yet to find the end zone this season, with his last touchdown taking place in the 2025 NFC divisional round against the 49ers, when he took the game's opening kickoff 95 yards to the house. The Seahawks will play five of their next six games at home, starting this Sunday against the winless Chargers.

headline: Shaheed caught three of six targets for 35 yards while also adding a four-yard rush, 29 yards on three punt returns and two kickoff returns for 47 yards during Sunday's 31-7 win over Arizona.
story: Shaheed found himself more involved as a pass catcher during Week 2, finishing second on the team in both targets and catches behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The wide receiver logged 39 snaps on offense, which was nine more than Cooper Kupp (30) in the contest. Shaheed will look to continue to establish himself as the No. 2 option at wide receiver Week 3 versus the Commanders.

headline: Shaheed caught one of three targets for four yards while adding three kickoff returns for 80 yards and a nine-yard punt return in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the Patriots.
story: After some offseason whispers about a larger role on offense for Shaheed, that didn't materialize in the season opener, as he wasn't among the five players who recorded multiple catches for the Seahawks. The standout return man maintained his prominent role on special teams, and he was on the field for 33 of Seattle's 50 snaps on offense. Shaheed is likely to have Drew Lock as his quarterback Week 2 against the Cardinals, as starting signal-caller Sam Darnold (hip) is likely to miss that game after exiting in the first quarter Wednesday.

headline: The Seahawks acquired Nelson from the Colts on Tuesday in exchange for a 2027 third-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round draft pick, Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport of ESPN report.
story: After a 2-5 start to the season, the Colts already found themselves on the periphery of the AFC playoff picture and opted to cash out on the eight-time Pro Bowl left guard before he became an unrestricted free agent this offseason. In Seattle, Nelson will join 2025 first-round pick Grey Zabel to form one of the NFL's better guard tandems. The Seahawks are hoping that the addition of Nelson can help open up more running room for a ground attack that has averaged just 3.9 yards per carry through the first seven weeks of the season.

headline: The Seahawks activated Bradford (knee) from injured reserve Saturday, and he does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chiefs, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Bradford has been given the green light to return from a five-game absence due to a knee injury. He should reclaim his starting spot at right guard for Sunday night's game.

headline: Bradford (knee) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Bradford remains on IR with a knee injury but has been cleared of any injury tag tied to the issue. The Seahawks will need to decide whether to maintain the 53-man roster spot or bring Bradford back for Sunday's game.

headline: Bradford (knee) was designated to return from injured reserve by the Seahawks on Monday, John Boyle of the team's official website reports.
story: Bradford has been on IR since Sept. 23 while recovering from a knee injury, and he will now have his 21-day practice window opened ahead of Week 7. The offensive lineman is eligible to return to action against the Chiefs on Sunday, and his status at the team's first practice of the week Tuesday will shed more light on his chances to do so.

headline: The Seahawks placed Bradford (knee) on injured reserve Wednesday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Bradford missed the team's Week 2 win over the Cardinals and will now be forced to sit out at least another four games before he's eligible to return. In his absence, Christian Haynes will likely serve as Seattle's starting right guard.

headline: Bradford (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Bradford was unable to practice Friday, downgrading his participation level after two limited sessions earlier in the week. The starting right guard will be unable to suit up to defend Drew Lock, leaving Christian Haynes as the most likely option to start Sunday's game.

headline: Bradford (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Bradford was limited in the Seahawks' first two practices of the week before sitting out Friday's session altogether. If Bradford is indeed inactive on game day, Christian Haynes is set to start at right guard.

headline: Bradford (knee) was a limited participant in practice Thursday,  Corbin K. Smith of Emerald City Spectrum reports.
story: The guard was limited Wednesday as well and is also now dealing with a hip injury, per Smith. Christian Haynes is Bradford's backup.

headline: O'Toole (hamstring) was a full participant in Friday's practice, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
story: O'Toole was held out of Week 7 against the Chiefs due to a hamstring injury, but his ability to practice in full Friday indicates that he'll be available against the Bears on Monday. He has three tackles (one solo) and one fumble recovery across four regular-season games while contributing mostly on special teams.

headline: O'Toole (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday night's game against the Chiefs.
story: The second-year linebacker has played almost exclusively on special teams across 12 career regular-season appearances. He has three tackles (one solo) across four games this season.

headline: Milroe will get added reps at practice ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Cardinals, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
story: Milroe is expected to serve as the top backup behind Drew Lock at quarterback in Week 9 with Sam Darnold (quadriceps) sidelined. Milroe has yet to appear in a regular-season contest this season and likely won't do so Sunday unless Lock is forced out of the contest with an injury.

headline: Milroe is active and operating as the Seahawks' primary backup quarterback for Sunday night's matchup with Kansas City.
story: Milroe will be active for the first time since Week 2 as Drew Lock (elbow) will serve as the team's emergency third quarterback in Week 7. The 23-year-old has yet to appear in a regular-season contest this year, and he will only do so if Sam Darnold is forced out of Sunday night's contest.

headline: Milroe (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against Denver, though he will once again serve as the Seahawks' emergency quarterback.
story: With Sam Darnold and Drew Lock active, Milroe will be available only if both players exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Milroe (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the 49ers on Sunday.
story: Milroe remains the third QB behind Sam Darnold and Drew Lock. The 2025 second-rounder will only be able to enter Sunday's contest if both Darnold and Lock cannot return to the game.

headline: Milroe (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Chargers on Sunday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Because Milroe is the emergency QB3, the second-year pro is now allowed to play Sunday unless both Sam Darnold and Drew Lock leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Milroe (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Washington.
story: Sam Darnold (glute) is available for Sunday's meeting with the Commanders, meaning Drew Lock will move back to the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. Despite being inactive for Week 3, Milroe could still see the field if both Darnold and Lock exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Milroe will be more involved in practice ahead of Sunday's game versus Arizona, Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle reports.
story: Sam Darnold (glute) won't suit up in Week 2, meaning Drew Lock will be the team's starting signal-caller. Milroe will occupy the No. 2 spot on the depth chart, so head coach Mike Macdonald wants to be sure he is ready to go in case Lock gets injured.

headline: Milroe (coach's decision) will be the emergency third quarterback for the Wednesday night matchup with the Patriots.
story: Milroe is the No. 3 quarterback behind Sam Darnold and Drew Lock. The second-year player is already settling into what will likely be his weekly role throughout the 2026 season, set to only check in to the game if both quarterbacks are unable to continue playing.

headline: Lock (right elbow) was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: The Seahawks ruled out Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, which places Lock in line for his second start of the campaign. However, Lock suffered a right elbow injury during Week 7 prep that left him as Seattle's emergency third quarterback the last two games. Assuming he gains clearance to suit up in Week 9, he'll be under center for Sunday's NFC West matchup.

headline: Lock (elbow) is slated to start Sunday's game against the Cardinals, per NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano.
story: Siciliano adds that Lock has an elbow injury that the team will manage during the week, but he's nonetheless set to get the starting assignment Sunday with fellow signal caller Sam Darnold unavailable due to quad and rib issues. Beyond this weekend, it's possible that Lock's QB1 stint could continue given that Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports that Darnold is viewed as week-to-week, according to coach Mike Macdonald.

headline: Lock (coach's decision/elbow) is inactive for Monday's matchup with the Bears but serving as the team's emergency quarterback, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: The quarterback is nursing an elbow injury and entered the day with a questionable tag. Now, he can only play against Chicago if Sam Darnold and Jalen Milroe have to exit the contest.

headline: Lock (elbow) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Bears, Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle reports.
story: Lock's practice reps during Week 8 prep were limited by a lingering elbow injury on his throwing arm. He opened the season as the Seahawks' backup QB and started in Week 2 against the Cardinals, but it's possible that he operates as Seattle's emergency third quarterback for a second consecutive game. In that case, he would not be allowed to play Monday unless both Sam Darnold and Jalen Milroe were to leave the game.

headline: Lock (elbow) was a limited participant in Friday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Lock continues to work through a right elbow injury, which led to him operating as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Chiefs in Week 7. He'll have one more chance to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Monday's game against the Bears.

headline: Lock (elbow) was a limited participant at the Seahawks' practice Thursday.
story: Lock remained limited at practice Thursday after logging three straight limited sessions before being ruled out for the team's Week 7 win over the Chiefs. The quarterback has been dealing with an elbow injury, and he will have two more chances to notch a full practice prior to Monday night's matchup with the Bears.

headline: Lock (elbow) is inactive but serving as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback for Sunday night's contest against the Chiefs, Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle reports.
story: Lock was limited at practice throughout the entire week with a right elbow injury and he will likely have the night off Sunday. Lock will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Sam Darnold and primary backup Jalen Milroe are unable to continue.

headline: Lock (elbow) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Lock logged three consecutive limited practices during Week 7 prep. The backup quarterback's throwing arm remains a problem, leaving it unclear whether he will suit up for Sunday's game or if Jalen Milroe will be active for the contest.

headline: Lock (elbow) was a limited practice participant Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Lock has now been limited in each of Seattle's past five practice sessions, though he was able to suit up last Thursday against Denver. It seems likely that he'll be active again for this Sunday's matchup against Kansas City, though Seattle's practice report Friday should provide more clarity in that regard. If Lock does indeed suit up Sunday, he'll again work as Sam Darnold's backup.

headline: Lock (elbow) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Corbin K. Smith of EmeraldCitySpectrum.com reports.
story: Lock remains limited in practice as the string of arm issues continues. The backup quarterback will need to practice both Thursday and Friday to have a shot at avoiding an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs.

headline: Lock (forearm) won't carry an injury designation into Thursday night's matchup with Denver, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Lock remained limited at practice for the third straight day Friday as he continues to deal with a right forearm injury, but the quarterback will be good to go for Week 6. The 29-year-old will operate in his typical role as the team's primary backup behind starting quarterback Sam Darnold on Thursday night versus the Broncos.

headline: The Seahawks listed Lock (forearm) as a limited practice participant on Tuesday's estimated report, Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle reports.
story: Lock is working through a right forearm injury. Jalen Milroe would step in as Seattle's backup QB behind Sam Darnold if Lock is not cleared to play against Denver on Thursday.

headline: Lock (forearm) was listed as a limited participant on Monday's estimated practice report, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: It's unclear when Lock picked up the injury, given that he did not play a single snap during Sunday's 32-29 loss to San Francisco. He's got two more chances to increase his practice participation, but if he cannot play against the Broncos on Thursday, then Jalen Milroe would serve as the Seahawks' backup quarterback behind Sam Darnold.

headline: Lock will return to a backup role for Sunday's game at Washington after coach Mike Macdonald said Friday that Sam Darnold (glute) is "going to play," John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: After Darnold suffered a right glute injury on Seattle's first possession of the season Week 1 against the Patriots, Lock directed the offense for the next seven-plus quarters, leading the team to two victories while completing 35 of 48 passes (73 percent) for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions and rushing twice for 13 yards. With Darnold back in action this weekend, though, Lock's time as the starter is over for now.

headline: Lock completed 19 of 26 passes for 235 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 31-7 victory over Arizona.
story: Lock didn't make it too hard on himself, looking for superstar wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba early and often. The duo connected for an 82-yard score in the first quarter before later adding touchdowns of seven and 12 yards in the second half. Lock has tossed four touchdowns over the first two weeks, all of which have been to Smith-Njigba. The quarterback has completed 35 of 48 passes for 422 yards with four scores so far this season, and he could be asked to start another contest Week 3 versus the Commanders while Sam Darnold (hip) continues to recover.

headline: Lock will start Week 2 against the Cardinals with Sam Darnold (glute) unavailable, Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 in Seattle reports.
story: Darnold will miss Week 2 as expected, prompting the Seahawks to tab Lock as the starter. Lock was competent in relief of Darnold in the season opener, completing 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards and a touchdown. Importantly, Lock was clean on the turnover front. He will lead the Seahawks for at least the upcoming road game against the Cardinals, which puts him on the radar in superflex and two-quarterback formats.

headline: Lock is likely to start Week 2 against the Cardinals, as Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reports that Sam Darnold (hip) is expected to miss at least one game.
story: Lock stepped up in relief after Darnold was hurt in the first quarter of Wednesday's season opener, as the backup guided the Seahawks to a 13-10 win over the Patriots while finishing the game with 187 passing yards and one touchdown. Darnold hasn't officially been ruled out for Week 2, but the Seahawks are likely to take a cautious approach with their starting QB since the strength of Seattle's team is the defense, so Lock is in good position to hold the fort effectively while Darnold recovers. Lock has a 10-18 career regular-season record as a starter.

headline: Lock took over for Sam Darnold (hip) with 7:29 remaining in the first quarter of Wednesday's 13-10 win over the Patriots and completed 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 13 yards.
story: Lock unsurprisingly took some time to get going, with his first six possessions netting just 95 total yards and zero points. However, the veteran signal-caller finally got into a rhythm late in the third quarter and led Seattle to its 13 points, the final 10 coming after Drake Maye's first two interceptions. Lock also picked up his connection with Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the second half, hitting the star wideout for a 45-yard touchdown that knotted the game at 10 early in the fourth quarter. While Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports that head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed a fracture has been ruled out for Darnold, it's still possible Lock is under center for a Week 2 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday, Sept. 20.

headline: Head coach Mike Macdonald announced that Darnold won't play Sunday against the Cardinals due to a quadriceps injury, NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano reports.
story: In addition to a quad issue that Darnold sustained late in Monday's loss to the Bears, Macdonald revealed that the quarterback suffered a rib injury early in that contest. The pair of health concerns may have played a part in Darnold's subpar performance, which included 188 yards, two touchdowns and one interception on 17-for-34 passing and two carries for 20 yards. With Darnold out for the first time since Week 2, backup QB Drew Lock will draw the Week 9 start under center for the Seahawks.

headline: Is Tyler Shough or Sam Darnold a better fantasy option in Week 9?
story: Is Tyler Shough or Sam Darnold a better fantasy option in Week 9?

headline: Darnold completed 17 of 34 passes for 188 yards with two touchdowns and one interception while adding two rushes for 20 yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night.
story: Darnold averaged just 5.5 yards per attempt and took three sacks from a Bears defense that made an impact addition in Jeffery Simmons on Thursday via trade with the Titans. Darnold's 50.0 percent completion rate was a season low for him in non-injury-shortened games, and the veteran signal-caller also threw an interception for the sixth consecutive contest. Darnold did toss multiple touchdowns for the first time since Week 4, connecting with Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43 yards) and Cooper Kupp (seven yards) for his pair of scoring strikes. Darnold will take an unsightly 10:9 TD:INT heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

headline: Darnold completed 20 of 28 passes for 257 yards, one touchdown and one interception in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Chiefs. He added two rushing attempts for 17 yards.
story: Darnold threw a 28-yard touchdown pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the second quarter to give the Seahawks a 10-0 lead, but Darnold's end-zone interception from the 3-yard line in the final minute of the first half allowed the Chiefs to stay within striking distance. Seattle's dominant defense made sure Darnold's eighth interception in five starts since returning from a glute injury wouldn't prove too costly. He has matched that interception total with eight touchdown passes over that span. Darnold and the 4-3 Seahawks will play at home in prime time again Week 8, hosting the Bears on MNF.

headline: Darnold completed 27 of 51 passes for 278 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed twice for 19 yards in the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday. He also threw a two-point conversion pass.
story: Darnold's final passing yardage total appears perfectly acceptable from a fantasy standpoint, but the veteran quarterback couldn't produce anywhere near enough scoring and also committed a pair of critical turnovers. While Darnold's first interception didn't lead to any points, it came at the Broncos' 31-yard line with 1:31 remaining and could have cost Seattle the game had the Seahawks not gotten another opportunity with the ball by subsequently forcing a three-and-out. Darnold's second pick did ultimately help lead to the loss, as it came on the first drive of overtime at the Seahawks' 43-yard line to set the Broncos up on the edge of field-goal range. Darnold's yardage total was his second highest of the season, but he's been much more mistake-prone early in the 2026 campaign while throwing seven interceptions, half of his 2025 total. Darnold may have a tough time atoning in Week 7 as well, as the Chiefs will pay a visit for a Sunday night showdown on Oct. 25.

headline: Darnold completed 18 of 29 passes for 195 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Sunday's 32-29 loss to the 49ers. He added one rushing attempt for five yards.
story: Darnold threw another two interceptions, bringing him up to five in three full games this season after he had a league-worst 20 turnovers in the 2025 regular season. His lone touchdown pass was a 16-yarder to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the third quarter, on which the star wide receiver did most of the work after the catch. Darnold is in no danger of losing the starting job ahead of Thursday's Week 6 home game against the Broncos considering he has earned a long leash coming off a Super Bowl title, but it's worth noting that backup Drew Lock completed 72.9 percent of his passes while playing turnover-free football to lead Seattle to a pair of wins while Darnold was sidelined by a glute injury earlier in the year.

headline: Darnold completed 13 of 22 passes for 168 yards, two touchdowns and one interception and rushed three times for six yards during Sunday's 30-23 victory against the Chargers.
story: On a day in which the Seahawks rode the ground game to the tune of 33 carries, led by RB Emanuel Wilson's 21, Darnold didn't have to do much to keep the Chargers at bay. Darnold's two touchdown throws went for 23 (Wilson) and six yards (WR Tory Horton), bringing his total on the campaign to six in a little more than eight quarters of play. Darnold will be seeking to bounce back in terms of yardage, at least, next Sunday versus the 49ers.

headline: Darnold completed 31 of 45 passes for 379 yards and four touchdowns with two interceptions in Sunday's 33-31 loss to the Commanders. He added five yards on his only carry.
story: Making his return from a Week 1 soft-tissue injury, Darnold put up big numbers against a shaky Washington defense as he connected for two scores with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and one each to Cooper Kupp and Eric Saubert. However, Darnold's two INTs both came in the second half and led directly to 14 points for the Commanders, including a 50-yard pick-six by third-string linebacker Kain Medrano that proved to be the game-winning score. Darnold will look to clean things up in a Week 4 home tilt against the Chargers.

headline: Coach Mike Macdonald said Friday that Darnold (glute) is "going to play" Sunday at Washington, Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle reports.
story: Darnold thus will miss only seven-plus quarters after initial reports indicated that he could be out up to one month due to the right glute injury he picked up in the Seahawks' Week 1 victory against the Patriots. Considering he logged a full practice Thursday, he'll supplant Drew Lock in the starting lineup this weekend, looking to build upon his one completion on two pass attempts for 13 yards so far this season.

headline: Darnold (glute) was a full practice participant Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: After returning to practice Wednesday as limited for the first time since suffering a right glute injury in the early stages of the Seahawks' Week 1 win against the Patriots, Darnold has experienced a quick upward trajectory in his recovery by handling every on-field rep one day later. Coach Mike Macdonald is expected to name a starting quarterback for Week 3 between Darnold and Drew Lock on Friday, so the overall situation may be resolved in short order. If Darnold gains clearance to return, he'll take over direction of the Seahawks offense Sunday at Washington.

headline: Darnold (glute) said Thursday that he's "feeling good" and aiming to play Sunday at Washington, but the Seahawks are taking the situation "day by day," John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Darnold got back on the practice field Wednesday as a limited participant, splitting reps with No. 2 QB Drew Lock. Coach Mike Macdonald told Brady Henderson of ESPN.com that Darnold was "on a good track" to return to action for the first time since Seattle's first drive of the season Week 1. Darnold's activity level is expected to increase as the week goes on, but Thursday's injury report will reveal if he was limited again or upgraded to full participation.

headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said after Wednesday's practice that Darnold (glute) is "on a good track" to play Sunday against the Commanders, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
story: After suffering a right glute strain early in the Seahawks' season-opening win over the Patriots, Darnold sat out the team's Week 2 win in Arizona, but that could end up being the extent of his absence. Darnold returned to practice Wednesday as a limited participant, splitting first-team reps with Drew Lock. Macdonald noted that Darnold's workload will be ramped up as the week progresses, and if the 29-year-old responds well to the added reps, he could get the green light to start Sunday in Washington. The Seahawks are likely to wait until after Friday's practice concludes before formally deciding on a Week 3 starter.

headline: Darnold (glute) officially was a limited practice participant Wednesday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Prior to Darnold returning to practice Wednesday, head coach Mike Macdonald told Brady Henderson of ESPN.com that the quarterback wouldn't take every rep, his activity level is expected to increase as the week continues, and the team will make a decision between Darnold and Drew Lock as the Week 3 starter by Friday. Darnold then was seen throwing while stretching during the media-access portion of Wednesday's session, per Gregg Bell of The Tacoma News Tribune. Darnold is seeking his first game action since straining his glute on Seattle's fifth offensive snap of the season on Sept. 9 against the Patriots.

headline: Jones recorded 13 tackles and a defensed pass in Monday's Week 8 loss to Chicago.
story: Jones not only led Seattle in stops in the loss, he also tied the season-high mark he first established in Week 1 versus New England. The veteran linebacker continues to be an impactful IDP asset in his sixth NFL campaign, as he ranks third in the NFL with 81 tackles through eight weeks. Jones has recorded at least eight stops in every one of his appearances this season.

headline: Jones notched nine tackles (five solo) Sunday in a 20-3 win against Kansas City.
story: Jones had a three-game streak of recording at least one sack snapped, but he remained highly productive. The veteran linebacker has now tallied exactly nine tackles in three straight games and has posted at least eight stops in each of his seven contests this season. Overall, Jones is tied for third in the NFL with 68 tackles through seven games.

headline: Jones recorded nine tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Thursday night's 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos.
story: Jones has now recorded a sack in three straight games and has at least eight tackles in all six contests to kick off the 2026 campaign. He's up to 59 tackles (31 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and three pass breakups, with one interception, on 99.5 percent of the Seahawks' defensive snaps.

headline: Jones recorded 12 total tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, and added an interception during Sunday's 30-23 win over the Chargers.
story: Jones was masterful in Week 4, leading the team in tackles in the victory. The linebacker was able to get to quarterback Justin Herbert for his first sack of the season in the second quarter before intercepting a pass from the QB later in the quarter. Jones has now compiled 41 total tackles (21 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and intercepted a pass over four contests to open the 2026 campaign.

headline: Jones (neck) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.
story: Jones opened the week as a limited practice participant due to a neck issue. That limited practice was a precautionary measure given his full participation in Thursday's session, and the 2021 third-rounder is well on track to play in Sunday's road game against the Commanders. Jones has 21 tackles (12 solo) through the first two games of the regular season.

headline: Jones (neck) was a limited participant at the Seahawks' practice Wednesday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
story: Jones secured eight total tackles (four solo) during the team's 31-7 win over Arizona in Week 2, and he appears to have suffered a neck injury during the contest. The linebacker's ability to practice in any capacity to open the week is a positive sign, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the Commanders.

headline: Jones recorded eight tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 31-7 win at Arizona.
story: One thing limiting Jones' production in Week 2 was the fact that the Cardinals' offense simply couldn't stay on the field - he played 48 defensive snaps Sunday after playing 71 defensive snaps in Week 1. He's still firmly on the IDP radar going into a Week 3 tilt against the Commanders.

headline: Jones accumulated 13 tackles (eight solo) during Wednesday night's 13-10 win over the Patriots.
story: The defensive signal-caller led a defensive front that dominated the Patriots' run game all night. Jones and his linebacker corps penetrated the Patriots' offensive line frequently, and the captain was able to lead the next closest player (Drake Thomas) by four tackles in the box score.

headline: Horton recorded three receptions for 26 yards on six targets in Monday's 34-17 loss to the Bears.
story: Horton was on the field for 43 of the Seahawks' 63 offensive snaps, with his 68 percent share representing a season high. The six targets were also a season-best total for Horton, who was the main beneficiary of extra playing time due to the absence of Rashid Shaheed (knee). If Shaheed is cleared to play in the Seahawks' Week 9 game against the Cardinals, Horton will likely see his role get reduced.

headline: Horton failed to haul in his lone target and returned two kickoffs for 60 yards during the Seahawks' 20-3 win over the Chiefs on Sunday.
story: Horton's 31 offensive snaps were third most among Seahawks wide receivers behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (53) and Cooper Kupp (45). 17 of Sam Darnold's 28 pass attempts went to Smith-Njigba (12) and tight end AJ Barner (five), with Horton and the rest of Seattle's pass catchers serving in complementary roles. The Seahawks offense revolves around Smith-Njigba, so most of Horton's work will come on special teams, although the latter could see an uptick in opportunities if Rashid Shaheed (knee) cannot play against the Bears in Week 8.

headline: Horton caught one of five targets for 13 yards and returned a punt for 13 yards during the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday. He also logged one tackle.
story: Horton finished Thursday's game fourth on the Seahawks in targets but managed to catch only one pass from Sam Darnold, the latter of whom attempted a season-high 51 throws.
